reviews.summary: All 18 existing HUD modes and 115 console panels now have explicit stable URLs, browser history, titles, unknown-route handling and real lazy chunks with loading/error fallback. Existing rail, palette, hotkeys, desktop and World navigation share URL state. Selected panels receive focus; demo/floating context is preserved. Overlay return destinations are bound to individual history entries and independently verified across historical/nested visits and malformed state. Desktop and Pixel 7 browser smoke passed against a local stubbed backend. Existing route/history/focus smoke remains green after grid sizing and cockpit composer wrapping. Three actual desktop-width regressions and three independent stacked-layout checks verify contained controls; cloud approval/gallery also passes at1280px.
reviews.remaining: Nerva has no global multi-profile switch or plugin route registry; profile-keyed remount and plugin-aware route extension from the full Hermes contract remain unsupported. Current route/demo-context remount does not claim multi-profile equivalence. Browser tests validate navigation with a stubbed backend, not production-host services.

reviews.summary: Același bundle SPA funcționează la rădăcină sau sub un JARVIS_ROOT_PATH validat, cu reverse proxy care elimină prefixul. Bootstrap-ul serverului, navigarea și istoricul, API/SSE/streaming, chunk-urile lazy, fonturile, manifestul și service worker-ul folosesc prefixul; cache-urile PWA sunt separate per prefix. Paginile /map și /mission-control legate din SPA sunt adaptate. Teste prin aplicația reală și proxy HTTP verifică reload, shortcut-uri, cache offline, auth pe POST și lipsa cererilor la rădăcina greșită; coliziunile /v2 și /api au regresii. Sub prefix, /metrics păstrează eticheta de rută (middleware-ul de prefix întoarce scope["route"] către golden-signals, la fiecare mesaj trimis și la eroare), iar căile nerutate rămân <unmatched>. Contractul este pentru browser cu proxy prefix-stripping: wrapper-ul nativ cere prefix gol, /v1 și proxy-urile care păstrează prefixul nu sunt incluse. Fixture-ul dezactivează lifespan/provider startup; nu se pretinde deployment sau probă cu provider live.

Browser HUD, ambient and responsive phone layouts synchronize fixed appearance preferences through a narrow user-guarded Settings DB document. Boot reads never write defaults; stale known values coerce to supported choices. Prefix-scoped immutable edit journals preserve offline changes across tabs, server revision CAS prevents stale writes without Web Locks, and acknowledgements remove exact edits even after unmount. Motion defaults to the OS System preference. Two independent real browser contexts recover saved choices after cache loss. Five fixed local UI font choices now share that normalization, revision and offline journal contract. The HUD applies the body/display override at its root; code and explicitly monospace elements retain their independent font stack. Real root/prefix browser tests verify computed families, persistence in a fresh browser, look independence, offline replay and code font invariance. The separate native application now reads the same owner Settings DB document at boot and foreground entry. Its connection-scoped finite cache, explicit-save hydration epochs and serialized current-record writes prevent stale credentials or appearance from returning. All 19 native consumers react without resetting local component state; code fonts remain independent. The accepted cross-client preference contract is implemented; native authoring and a full curated font catalog are not required by this row. Scope remains one configured owner instance. Unsupported native fonts have explicit platform fallbacks; unavailable storage cannot preserve offline choices across process restarts. Native rendering is covered with real React source and host mocks, not device GUI proof.

Shared browser composer now accepts image selection, paste and drop, with transient previews, removal and eight pending-read reservations. Authenticated composer-specific vision routes validate static PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP bytes and bounded raster decoding before provider dispatch. A random persisted destination revision and one configuration snapshot bind explicit remote consent; stale configuration refuses dispatch. Vision replies identify the actual configured model and remain separate from ordinary agent chat. Cancellation and late-response suppression preserve one active turn; ordinary text payloads remain unchanged. Independent source review, 27 new backend cases, 10 frontend cases and desktop/mobile-browser checks pass.
reviews.remaining: No persisted chat image artifact, native agent multimodal context, native mobile composer or ?learn seed. Vision uses a separate configured VLM turn; no live provider proof. Static images only, at most eight 4 MiB images, 8192 pixels per edge and 16 MP each before downscaling. Destination status stores inert revision metadata in the existing owner Settings DB; this does not provide per-account preferences.

reviews.summary: The hub's own log is readable from the UI. GET /api/admin/logs (agents/core/routers/admin.py:475) is admin-only and read-only; it reads off the event loop and answers a refused filter with 400, its reason and no-store. Behind it, agents/core/log_tail.py reads the file the hub's own setup_logging actually opened, or reports the error it met (FILE_LOG_STATE, agents/core/log.py:19; _writer_state, agents/core/log_tail.py:95), falling back to the configuration for a process that never set logging up ($JARVIS_LOG_FILE, else data_path('logs','jarvis.log') with system.log_to_file: configured_log, agents/core/log_tail.py:86). It lists only that file and its rotations named with ASCII digits, and only regular files by lstat, so a link, a pipe or a directory is never listed (list_files, agents/core/log_tail.py:114; _listed, agents/core/log_tail.py:105); a file is chosen by one of those names, and it is opened without following a link or blocking and checked to be a regular file (_read_window, agents/core/log_tail.py:193). The read is bounded: at most the last 4 MiB, read in one go and closed before parsing, at most 500 records, each at most 8,000 characters (read_path, agents/core/log_tail.py:275). Lines are grouped into records by the log format's header, so a traceback stays with its error: a record over the limit keeps its header and its newest lines behind a "[… N lines not shown]" marker, so the error line is always there; lines above the first header read (a record whose header rotated away, a file not in the log format) are records of their own, beyond the window too. Filters: File, a minimum Level (WARNING shows WARNING, ERROR and CRITICAL; a line with no level is not shown under a floor), a Component (a logger and its children) and Lines (1-500), decided on the record as written, so only returned records are redacted. Redaction runs on every returned field, each line whole before anything is cut, so a secret is never split into a visible half: the H495 secret scanner, an assignment rule for names ending like a credential (`SMTP_PASS=`, `?token=`, `password:`), and the known values of the process's secret-named environment variables and encrypted settings, so it masks at least what /api/admin/env masks (_Redactor, agents/core/log_tail.py:159; _known_secret_values, agents/core/log_tail.py:137); when the scanner cannot be loaded nothing is shown, with a note (_redactor, agents/core/log_tail.py:177; _record, agents/core/log_tail.py:247). Terminal escape sequences, C0 and C1 controls and bidirectional overrides are removed (_clean, agents/core/log_tail.py:186). The answer carries the components seen (redacted), the bytes scanned and whether only part of the file was read, and an honest note: file logging off and how to turn it on, a file the hub could not open at start, no file yet, or a file that may no longer be written (read_log, agents/core/log_tail.py:323). The HUD's Logs panel (frontend/src/panels/logs.tsx:54, registered in the Console's Observe group) has the File / Level / Component / Lines filters, colours records by level (ERROR/CRITICAL red, WARNING amber, DEBUG dim), shows them newest first as text, never markup, auto-refreshes every 5 s while switched on and the page is visible, skipping a tick while a read is in flight and stopping on a refused credential, shows LIVE only while the hub writes its file, shows no old records after a refused filter (and goes back to the current log when a rotation is gone), and names the admin token on a 401 or 403. `nerva logs -n N` (cmd_logs, agents/cli/nerva.py:1218) reads the same bounded, redacted tail (N counts records), says when only part was read, and refuses cleanly on an unreadable file or a missing redactor. tests/test_log_tail.py (33 cases) covers the resolution and the off state, rotations and refused names, records and tracebacks, the caps, the level floor and component children, the byte budget, a partial last line, bytes that are not UTF-8, control characters, redaction (current file, rotation, traceback line, filtered fields), the route and the CLI; tests/test_h145b_log_review.py (32) covers the first review: a secret across the cut (four offsets, and in a continuation line), a long traceback keeping its error line, links and a link swapped in after listing, a pipe, secret-named environment values and credential assignments (and ordinary numbers left alone), a redactor that cannot load (route and CLI), C1 and bidi controls, filtering before redaction, the writer's error and its path, setup_logging's record, no file yet, plain lines beyond the window, the 4 MiB budget, level-less lines under a floor, component redaction, the CLI's records, window note and -n 0, rotation names, a directory and the 400's no-store; frontend/src/test/logs-panel.test.tsx (14) covers the registration, the query, the admin read, order and colours, each filter, the 5 s auto-refresh, a tick skipped in flight, a hidden page, stale records after a refusal, LIVE only while writing, the off note, no match and a partial read, 401 and 403, a kept component and text-only rendering. The first review (two majors: a secret split by the cut came back in part, and a long traceback lost its error line; ten minors; nine nits) is answered; the feature's 29 mutants were caught but one equivalent, and this round's 26, all but one equivalent (the regular-file check after open, which lseek or read also enforces), two after their cases were added (a pipe, the partial first line). Test manual: PNB-169, PNB-170; the API sweep lists the route. Adapted from Hermes: one log file and its rotations instead of six named files, since the hub writes one log; the level is a floor rather than an exact match. Known limits: a record forged by a multi-line message that contains a header-shaped line is shown as its own record (a property of the log format).

JobStore/HUD/CLI au creare și editare pentru cele patru acțiuni, constructor vizual de program, 16 blueprint-uri cu formulare tipizate, repeat limitat atomic și livrare per job către canale deja configurate sau doar istoric. Există doctor, incidents (pauze după eșecuri), notepad editabil, status/remove și tick idempotent în fusul scheduler-ului, refuzat când scheduler-ul rulează. Gate-urile task/quiet hours/buget/e-stop sunt păstrate; flush-ul mesajelor amânate verifică acum e-stop. Accesul Automations din bara principală deschide un spațiu dedicat; dialogul nativ de creare gestionează focusul, Tab, Escape și revenirea la buton. Tipurile OpenAPI includ cele patru rute noi. Review: update scrie doar câmpurile cerute și nu poate reseta rezervările atomice; istoricul păstrează textul efectiv pentru brief/remind fără livrare. Scripturile Python locale au acum snapshot de sursă legat de aprobarea fiecărei execuții, rezultate pending persistente și livrare directă no_agent sau context izolat ca date neîncrezătoare. API/CLI disting acceptarea de finalizare; conținutul gol nu apelează modelul. Manual run now persists a bounded receipt and returns HTTP 202; scheduler/offline tick executes through the shared job firing path. Atomic coalescing and portable cross-process locks prevent duplicate execution. Configuration snapshots, pending-script reconciliation, crash-unknown state without replay, and concurrent retention are tested. HUD and CLI restore accepted request status and distinguish queued, waiting and completed execution. Ask jobs now persist effective request-local model/provider pins through CLI/HUD options, with preflight routing, closed lifetimes, approved-model enforcement and resolved context budgets. Unavailable pins fail explicitly; ordinary chat configuration is unchanged. Independent review repaired file_read re-spilling under a pinned window. Owner-authored reminder media IDs now produce actual bounded Telegram file/text delivery with frozen content/recipient bindings, a validated total deadline and durable held/partial/unknown outcomes. CLI/HUD authoring and status expose these outcomes; editing an explicit empty options document clears prior settings correctly. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported. Model-bearing ask jobs now accept enabled_toolsets through CLI and HUD using an explicit installed basic/files/terminal catalog. Missing/null retains defaults; [] disables tool offers. Immutable per-run name sets intersect both runtime/profile offers and ToolRPC intake before preflight, handlers or approval enqueue. Nested scopes only narrow and inherit revocation; ordinary callers and concurrent jobs retain isolated defaults. Unknown/unavailable groups refuse. Existing approvals retain frozen concrete arguments and do not reread job options or revive a request scope. Doctor reports the configured tool-name upper bound, not effective contextual offers. Actual runner/Agent/RPC, queued-edit/restart, cancellation, UI and concurrency tests are evidence; tool selection grants no new authority.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc contextul izolat per job pentru model workdir și skills, agregarea între profile și noul grant schedule.create cerut de original (rădăcină protejată în afara scopului). Opțiunile fără runtime sunt refuzate, nu salvate inert. Nu există probă live pentru scheduler/canale sau autorare nativă mobilă; monitoarele depind de sursele configurate, nu instalează integrări. Cloud pins must match existing policy routing; changed local models require loaded context metadata, and LM Studio currently cannot resolve a changed model. Pinned jobs use deterministic compression and omit auxiliary embedding recall. The initial catalog intentionally excludes dedicated code-runner, delegation and dynamic plugin groups; their transitive restriction contracts remain unimplemented.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 in five rounds. The first round shipped with H200 (critic note 7). After an adversarial review reopened it, the second round added the receiver switch, an event list and a prompt template. After a second review, the third added where a delivery goes (Hermes' Deliver to and deliver only), a description and a receiver switch that fails closed. A third review (review-H153c) found that as shipped, Deliver to reached none of the owner's channels, and the fourth round made a real send reach each offered channel, tested through the real path down to the channel adapter. A fourth review (review-H153d) found that the fourth round's plain-text rendering let one delivery freeze the hub, and rewrote the sender's file names and addresses; the fifth round sends the text as written, bounds every renderer, and fixes the review's minors. A fifth review (review-H153e) found no major; its three minors (inline code spans still quadratic in two renderers, first-read waiters holding worker threads, eight unpinned behaviours) and six nits are fixed.

Backend CRUD is admin-guarded, and the store serves every change without a restart:
- GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE /api/webhooks (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:174, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:180, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:193, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:220) list, create, update and delete hooks.
- A create that carries a field it does not know (Hermes' skills, deliver_chat_id) is refused with 422, never silently dropped (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:86).
- WebhookStore.create (agents/core/webhooks.py:486) mints a token and, when signed, an HMAC signing secret. Both are returned once, and every list masks them (agents/core/webhooks.py:635). A save that fails undoes the change in memory.

(1) The receiver card (Hermes' platform-level toggle). The setting webhooks.receiver_enabled is a declared toggle, on by default. It is written through the audited PUT /api/admin/settings/webhooks, and the audit row ends with the value (receiver_enabled=false). A reseed is audited too (agents/core/routers/admin.py:319). When the switch is off, the trigger refuses every delivery with 503. It checks before the body is read and again after authentication, so a switch that lands while a sender streams its body stops that delivery (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:238).
- It fails closed (agents/core/webhooks.py:251):
  - only a literal true is on, and a missing row is the declared default;
  - when the settings store cannot be read, settings_db.read_setting raises instead of answering the default (agents/core/settings_db.py:640), so the last state read or written stays in force;
  - a receiver never read is refused with "the webhook receiver's state cannot be read".
- It is read off the event loop, and by one caller at a time: while a read runs, every other caller gets the last state at once. A caller with no state known yet (the first read after a start) waits for that read, at most two seconds, so a burst that arrives while it runs is answered, and a read slower than that is still refused, closed. The router waits on the event loop (agents/core/webhooks.py:377): who reads is decided on the loop, only the read runs on a worker thread, and a waiter holds none, so a burst on a slow fresh receiver leaves the default executor free (review-H153e MINOR-2). A caller from a thread waits in it, at most four at once (RECEIVER_FIRST_READ_WAITERS, agents/core/webhooks.py:247); any other is refused, closed. A write, a reset or another store wakes the waiters. A state is used for a second before the store is read again. A read that a write, a reset, a reseed or another store overtook while it ran is dropped, a failed one included. A write in this process is seen at once; one from another process (nerva config set) within the second.
- The admin routes keep working, and hooks keep their credentials.
- The panel's receiver row shows on, off, or "not read" with the reason:
  - a failed re-read drops the last state instead of showing it;
  - an answer is shown unless a newer one already is, so an earlier read never overwrites a newer one and a poller slower than its interval still sees each answer (frontend/src/panel-kit.tsx:20);
  - ↻ re-reads it;
  - a stored value that is not true or false is shown as off;
  - a store with no row yet, which the hub answers with its own 404 naming the category, shows the hub's default, "on · not stored", and can be switched off, because the write creates the row (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:197); any other 404 (a proxy's) is a failed read.
- Interop and the /v1 panel show every hook as refused while the switch is off.

(2) The New-subscription modal: name, description, agent or workflow target, target id, HMAC signing (the secret, shown once), an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only. Create is last in the tab order (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:389).
- Events: up to 32 printable names of 1 to 64 characters, no comma, stored stripped and kept once each, ignoring ASCII case (agents/core/webhooks.py:137).
  - The delivery's event comes from the sender's header (X-GitHub-Event, X-Gitlab-Event, X-Event-Key, X-Event-Type, X-Webhook-Event), else from the payload's event or type (agents/core/webhooks.py:121). It is bounded when read but never cut to the 64-character limit, so a longer name matches no subscription.
  - A hook with a list runs only the deliveries whose event is on it. Every other delivery is answered 202 with the reason, never run, and counted as skipped (agents/core/webhooks.py:605). That includes a delivery that names no event, and a list a hand edit broke (null, not a list, an item that is not a name).
- Template: {a.b.0} reads the JSON payload by key and list index, {event} is the event, {payload} the whole body, and {payload.x} a payload key the template reserves (agents/core/webhooks.py:173).
  - Nothing else is read. A missing value is empty, a string is used as is and anything else as JSON.
  - The work is bounded by the caps (agents/core/webhooks.py:157): each path is read once per render, a value is encoded only up to 4,000 characters, and substitution stops at 16,000.
  - A template that renders nothing is skipped, not run. So is an untemplated delivery with no text, which gets its own reason.
- A body over 5 MiB is refused with 413 before it is read whole (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:235).

(3) Deliver to and deliver only (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:354, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:366).
- deliver is log (the default: the reply stays in the sender's response and the session) or one of the owner's own channels that something receives: telegram, voice or ntfy (agents/core/webhooks.py:70). Names are matched exactly.
- web is refused by name: nothing in the hub connects a client to the web channel, so a push there would never arrive. /api/channels/targets and nerva send --list say the same: web is not ready while no client is connected (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:88).
- The reply, or a workflow's last step, goes through send_to_target and ChannelManager.send to the owner's own destination (Telegram's owner chat). send_to_target writes an IntentLog row per send. The text is labelled "Webhook <name> - <event>", and each channel carries the label its own way:
  - ntfy gets it as its title, folded to printable ASCII and cut to 120 characters;
  - telegram and voice get it on the first line.
- The text goes as written: nothing is rendered and nothing is rewritten, so a file name, an address and a Markdown link arrive as the sender wrote them, and a link shows its address. What hides or reorders text is dropped: every format and control character but a newline, a tab, a zero-width joiner and non-joiner (the bidi controls and marks, zero-width spaces, word joiners, invisible operators, the soft hyphen, the BOM, the TAG plane), and the characters that render blank (the Hangul fillers, the grapheme joiner, the Mongolian selectors, the blank braille pattern); a subdivision flag emoji stays (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:312; review-H153e NIT-1). A lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:338). Telegram sends it with no parse mode, no link preview and no voice note, and ntfy unrendered (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:208, agents/core/channels/telegram.py:338, agents/core/channels/ntfy.py:137). Voice speaks it without the markup. A longer text is cut at 4,000 characters with a note that says where the rest is (the session for a reply, nowhere for deliver-only text).
- Nothing on the push path renders, so a delivery costs linear time in its text: one long line cannot hold the event loop. The renderers the rest of the hub uses bound every marker span (a link, bold, italic, a heading line), and put inline code spans back in one pass (agents/core/channels/render.py:52; review-H153e MINOR-1), so one long line costs linear time there too, and a span past the bound is left as written (agents/core/channels/render.py:40).
- The hook is read again after the turn. If it was deleted or switched off, or the receiver was switched off or cannot be read, nothing is pushed and the hook says why; a hook moved to another destination is pushed there, labelled with its name as it is then.
- Quiet hours (ambient.quiet_hours_start/end, 22 to 7 by default, hours taken modulo 24, the jobs' own reading, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:275) keep every push off the phone and the speaker. An hour setting that is not a number (an infinity, NaN, text) keeps its default, for the jobs too (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:82). The push is noted on the hook, not held for the morning as a job's message is.
- A hook makes at most 30 push attempts an hour (agents/core/webhooks.py:422, per process). An attempt the channel refused counts, and the panel says so; a push held by quiet hours spends none. A push over it is noted, not sent.
- deliver_only skips the agent: the rendered text goes straight to the destination, and no turn runs. It needs a channel: deliver-only with the log is refused on create and on PATCH, with the reason (agents/core/webhooks.py:101). A record from before that rule can still be switched off, and its delivery says the text was dropped.
- A workflow delivers its last step's output, or nothing when the run failed or its last step returned an error, never an earlier step's output (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:439). The last step is the last to run, in the pipeline's batch order, not the last listed, and a run that stopped early delivers the last step that ran (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:415). An output the router cannot read is recorded, and nothing is pushed.
- Each delivery's outcome (channel, ok, reason, time) is kept on the hook and shown in its detail pane, and the response carries it too. Every exit after a call is counted is recorded, a missing or invalid workflow and a failed turn included (agents/core/webhooks.py:695).
- A delivery that fails is recorded and answered 200. Every answer is encodable whatever the sender or a step put in it: a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD, a NaN or an infinity null, and anything else JSON cannot carry (a date, bytes, a set, an object) its text (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:464), so a delivery is never a 500 after its push. A workflow hook answers with ok, the steps that ran and the delivery, never the run's context, which holds the sender's text and every step's output. A failed turn itself still answers 500, so the sender's retry runs it again.

(4) The subscriptions list with per-route enable/disable and delete. PATCH /api/webhooks/{hook_id} (agents/core/webhooks.py:553) takes any of enabled (a strict boolean), events, prompt, deliver, deliver_only and description, and changes them in place. It refuses:
- null (and its schema advertises none);
- an empty body;
- an unknown field;
- a destination the create would refuse.

The schema names the four destinations as an enum. A hook switched off keeps its token and secret. The trigger refuses it with 403 after authentication, from the live record, before the event filter.

Each row has an on/off switch, an HMAC or token badge, an event-count badge, the destination (none for the log) and delete with an inline confirmation. The detail pane shows the description, the calls, the skipped deliveries, where the result goes, how a push goes (on a hook that pushes) and how the last delivery went. It edits all of them and opens at the hook's own destination. After a save focus returns to the hook's row, or to the create form when the hook is gone. The legacy /v1 panel lists, creates and deletes through adminFetch, and shows the receiver as the hub reads it and each destination (agents/web/static/tools.js:341).

(5) The restart banners. Nerva needs no restart for either kind of change: the receiver switch is a setting read at most a second old, and hook CRUD is served live.

Audit: create, switch, update and delete each write a SecurityEvent (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:142). It names:
- the hook id;
- the target as a JSON string;
- the event list;
- the template's length (never its text);
- the destination and deliver only;
- the signed and enabled flags.

It never records the token or secret. A switch alone is recorded as enable or disable; any other change is an update. The receiver switch is audited by the settings route, with its value, and a choice setting's value is in its row (a toggle, a select, a number, a slider). A nerva config set from the shell writes no audit row (H378).

Deliveries: an agent-target delivery goes through handle_input(channel="webhook"). origin_for_channel (agents/core/action_origin.py:36) classifies that channel as inbound, so the payload is tainted and the kernel's GRANT->QUEUE escalation applies. A workflow target runs its pipeline (agents/core/routers/workflows.py:37) under the inbound action origin. The sender waits for the push as well as the turn. A retried delivery that carries an Idempotency-Key is not run again; it gets the first outcome back (H659, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:551). One without a key runs again.

Adapted, not copied:
- Deliver to: Hermes offers log, Telegram, Discord, Slack, email and a GitHub comment. Nerva offers the log and the owner's own telegram, voice and ntfy, and refuses the rest by name with a 422 (agents/core/webhooks.py:75):
  - Email is never an outbound side effect of an inbound delivery (the rule ChannelManager.send keeps).
  - A GitHub comment writes to someone else's system, so the hook's agent proposes it through the governed write-back path, one approval each.
  - Discord and Slack are reply-only transports here, with no home channel to address.
  - The web HUD has no push receiver yet.
- Per-subscription skills: a Nerva hook targets an agent or a workflow, and the agent brings its own skills to the turn. Hermes' own modal does not expose skills either.

Tests:
- tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py (54 cases) covers the receiver, the event filter, the template and the update.
- tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py (35) covers the switch, the audit and the in-flight race.
- tests/test_h153b_webhook_delivery.py (63) covers the second round with fakes for the send and the clock.
- tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py (80, the fourth round) runs the real path, the router through send_to_target and ChannelManager to a recording adapter per channel. It covers:
  - each channel (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:104), with and without a turn;
  - the real quiet-hours rule on a fixed clock (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:273);
  - the real Telegram adapter's HTTP body (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:229);
  - fail-soft delivery (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:319);
  - a switch thrown during the turn (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:455);
  - the workflow rule (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:534);
  - the push cap, the single-flight receiver (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:605), and the audit of free text.
- tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py (61 cases, the fifth round) covers:
  - a long line of brackets pushed at once, and the text as written on Telegram and ntfy (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:67);
  - every renderer in linear time on one long line (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:129);
  - the hidden characters, the first-read burst (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:151), the workflow answer and the encodable answers (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:253);
  - the last step as run, the unreadable receiver after the turn, a Telegram refusal, the hour of the allowance, quiet hours and the allowance, the live label, an overtaken failed read, a slider's audited value, the hour settings and web's readiness.
- tests/test_h153e_webhook_review.py (49 cases, the sixth round) covers the renderers' scaling on inline code spans, the restore's escaping, an ordinary long link, the waiter cap and wake, a burst through astate holding one thread, every hidden character and what stays, the cut boundary, the quiet-hours end and the encodable answer; frontend/src/test/panel-state.test.tsx (2) a failed poll shown while loading.
- frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx has 55 cases, frontend/src/test/use-api-sequence.test.tsx 4 (a poller slower than its interval, loading until the newest answer, an earlier answer never over a newer one, another address), frontend/src/test/interop-live-honesty.test.tsx 14 and the /v1 tests/frontend/tools.test.js 18.

Mutation:
- The fourth round: 92 mutants of its guards and of the reviewer's 35 unpinned survivors (70 backend, 20 panel and Interop, 2 /v1). Three no longer applied to the final code; the reviewer replayed the 89 that apply, and each is caught.
- The fifth round: 40 mutants of its guards (32 Python, 8 HUD), each run against its own suites. All 40 are caught, one of them (the answer's dict keys) by a test added for it. Four were first written malformed and were rewritten before they counted.
- The fifth review's own 68 mutants left eight unpinned behaviours (five hidden characters, the cut boundary, the quiet-hours end, the link bound); each has a test now. This round's 13 mutants (12 Python, 1 HUD) were all caught.
- The fourth review's own 104 mutants left 20 survivors: seven equivalent, one a strengthening (catching an infinite hour, now the code) and twelve unpinned. Each of the twelve now has a test.

An agent's persona can now be edited in the UI and is live on its next turn. That is Hermes' persona editor, over the version history Nerva already kept. Until now the history was a side record: a commit or rollback in the Prompts panel changed a JSON file while the agent kept its old persona. agents/core/soul_edit.py holds the one path an edit takes, apply_soul (:152). (1) Refusals. An agent the hub has not loaded is refused (404; agent_folder, :100, returns an enumerated folder name in the id alphabet, so no request value reaches a path). So is text over MAX_SOUL_BYTES (256 KiB of UTF-8, :40; 413), safe mode (:171; 409, because overlays are not read there, H275) and a persona the H387 guard would drop (:174; 422 with the verdict). guard_verdict (:60) runs the same scan and cap as Agent._load_soul, and GET /api/agents/{id}/soul now reports it through the same function. A line the guard only quarantines is applied, and the verdict names it. (2) Nothing live is lost. The first edit keeps the file on disk as v1 ("on disk before the first edit"). A file changed on disk since the last version, such as a hand edit, is kept as its own version ("on disk, changed outside the editor") before it is replaced (:185). An agent with no persona file has nothing to keep. (3) Written where the model reads it. The text goes to the owner's overlay (overlay_path, :115): souls/<id>/SOUL.local.md in the data home, else the repo-local SOUL.local.md, never the shipped SOUL.md. The write is atomic (_write_atomically, :126: temporary file, fsync, replace; a failure leaves no temporary file and records no new version). (4) Versioned, then live. The text is committed (:195; the same text twice is one version). The agent re-reads its persona (_load_soul, :197), and the result says whether the running agent now reads the written file. (5) Audited without the text. A SETTINGS_CHANGE row names the agent, the version and its hash. A plain commit and a history-only rollback are audited the same way (record_version, :224; agents/core/routers/admin.py:635, :690). Surfaces. PUT /api/admin/agents/{id}/soul {content, message} (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:132, admin). POST /api/admin/prompts/{id}/rollback applies the version through the same path for a loaded agent (agents/core/routers/admin.py:676); the shared contract _identity (served from IDENTITY.local.md) and keys that are no loaded agent keep the history-only rollback. Description. A description: field in the SOUL front-matter is the agent's one-line description (description_of, :84, and description_in, :98: one line, at most 400 characters). It is listed on GET /agents and the SOUL read (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:179, :124) and is never part of the prompt. POST /api/admin/agents/{id}/description/draft (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:150; draft_description, :238) asks the strict-local model for one paragraph from the live persona and saves nothing. With no local model it is a 503, never a cloud call (:255). HUD. The Dossier has an Edit persona button that opens the live SOUL in frontend/src/soul-edit.tsx (SoulEditor, :49, mounted at frontend/src/modes.tsx:96). It offers Preview against the live text, Apply, Draft description with Use it (withDescription, :15, writes the front-matter line), and the hub's refusal in words (refusalText, :32). The Dossier also shows the description. The Prompts panel gets apply beside commit (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2757) and says when a rollback is live. Tests: tests/test_soul_edit_route.py (29) covers the apply, the seed and hand-edit versions, deduplication, blocked and quarantined text, the audit row, size, ids, an unloaded folder, admin, the repo overlay, safe mode, a failed write, no store, a reload that misses the file, rollback (live, to the shipped text, refused, missing, history-only keys, audited), a plain commit, the description (listed, bounded, never prompted) and the draft (a proposal, strict-local, empty). frontend/src/test/soul-edit.test.tsx has 6. tests/test_h10_22_prompt_versioning.py now asserts that the rollback is live, in a throwaway data home. 61 mutants: 58 caught, eight of them after survivors got cases. Two survivors of the first-edit-only seed led to keeping hand edits as versions; that code's own five mutants are caught. The fsync is a crash-only property.

Every configuration key is reachable, searchable, portable and resettable from the UI. The backend it builds on: `GET /api/admin/settings` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:73) returns every category, and the per-category PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:166) validates with `validate_category` and answers 422 before any write, auditing the changed key names and the new value of a choice only (`_audited_values`, agents/core/routers/admin.py:120). New in H157: `GET /api/admin/settings/export` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:78, registered before the `/{category}` read so it is never taken for one) returns the declared settings as a `nerva-settings/1` document with an attachment disposition, leaving out every secret (encrypted at rest, or named like a token, secret, password, client id or API key), `mcp.servers` (it holds credentials by design) any URL that carries a password (`http://user:pw@host`, in a list too), and any free-form value the H495 secret scanner would mask (or every free-form value, when the scanner cannot run), and naming each left-out setting with its reason (export_settings, agents/core/settings_db.py:951; is_secret_setting, agents/core/settings_db.py:897; _looks_like_credential, agents/core/settings_db.py:930; _url_password, agents/core/settings_db.py:914). `POST /api/admin/settings/import` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:213) takes such a document (at most 1 MB and 1,000 keys, the body counted as it streams in, so a chunked upload is bounded too: _bounded_body, agents/core/routers/admin.py:200). The import and the reset take only an `application/json` request (415 otherwise, a type a browser must pre-check before sending) and refuse one the browser marks cross-site (403), since the admin guard trusts loopback on a default install (_refuse_cross_site_write, agents/core/routers/admin.py:186); every reply is no-store, and only a JSON `true` makes a dry run. A NaN, an Infinity or nesting too deep to store is refused (422), never stored, an `mcp.servers` entry needs a name (validate_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:791, via _mcp_servers_problem, agents/core/settings_db.py:820; the loader skips a nameless entry too, MCPManager.load_from_config, agents/core/mcp/client.py:814), and 2000 and 2000.0 are the same number, so no change (_same_value, agents/core/settings_db.py:1033). In the document every key must be declared and passes the same `validate_category` a single write does, so a posture flag or an out-of-range value is refused like any other; one refusal and nothing is written (422 with every reason) (plan_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:981). Only the keys whose value differs are written, in one sqlite transaction, all or nothing, secrets encrypted as a single write encrypts them (apply_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:1067), with one audit row naming the settings (and the new value of a choice); `"dry_run": true` answers what would change, a secret's values shown as `(secret)` and a credential-shaped free value as `(hidden)`, so the preview never echoes one (describe_changes, agents/core/settings_db.py:1041). `POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:261) puts one category back to its declared values and names the keys that moved, with an audit row; it keeps the category's secrets and names them (kept, reset_kept, agents/core/settings_db.py:1083) and names the settings the product posture still forces (overridden, posture_overridden, agents/core/settings_db.py:1090), where the global reseed (agents/core/routers/admin.py:296) was the only reset (reset_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:1180). The v2 console SettingsPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2653; widgets typed by settingsField, frontend/src/gap.tsx:2639) now has a search across every category matching a setting's category.key or label, with a match count and an honest no-match line (settingMatches, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:32); a reset per category heading (only one with declared rows) that asks first, by a second click that names how many settings go back and moves the focus to itself, drops the category's unsaved edits once it runs and names what was kept and what the posture still forces (ResetCategory, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:82); edits hidden by the search are counted beside the save; and a MOVE A CONFIGURATION section (SettingsTransfer, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:177) that downloads the export and names what the hub left out, and imports a pasted or chosen file by showing the hub's dry run (each change old → new) and applying it only on a second step, listing every reason on a refusal; a pasted `dry_run` is dropped so the apply step is never a dry run, the text is held while the hub answers, and the file picker is reachable from the keyboard. The standalone /admin app's GlobalConfigPage (agents/web/static/admin.js:447) is unchanged, and `nerva config list|get|set|check` (cmd_config, agents/cli/nerva.py:803) still edits single keys offline. tests/test_settings_transfer.py (28 cases) covers the export (every declared key either exported or named as left out, secrets, client ids, mcp.servers, a token-shaped value, a scanner that cannot run, the stored value), the import (an export imports back as no change, valid changes, every refusal a single write makes, nothing written on one refusal, one transaction, the posture flag, a secret encrypted and never echoed, the bound), the per-category reset, and the routes (admin only, the export not read as a category, preview then apply with one audit row, every reason on a refusal, no row when nothing changes, reset and 404); tests/test_h157b_settings_review.py (30, the first review) covers the JSON-only and cross-site refusals, URL passwords, a credential in a list, the hidden preview, NaN, Infinity and deep nesting, nameless MCP servers, number equality, secrets kept on a reset, the posture's settings named, the change listeners, the 1 MB bound for a sized and a chunked body and the JSON-only dry run; frontend/src/test/settings-tools.test.tsx (12) covers the search, the two-step reset, the export note, the dry-run preview and the second-step apply with the admin credential, a refusal's reasons, text that is not JSON, an import that changes nothing, a reset that drops unsaved edits and names kept secrets, edits hidden by the search, a pasted dry run never applied and the keyboard-reachable file button. 25 backend mutants, all caught (one after its case was added: a scanner that cannot run). The first adversarial review (review-H157: 2 major, 7 minor, 12 nit) found that a page the owner visited could post a plain-text import to a loopback hub, and that a URL password was exported; all are fixed, and its 18 mutants were all caught but one equivalent (two after their cases were pinned). Test manual: PNB-171, PNB-172; the API sweep lists the three routes. Adapted from Hermes: no raw YAML editor (the typed widgets and the JSON import cover it, and a free-form editor would bypass the per-key widgets), and export/import are JSON documents rather than a Form/YAML toggle.

The memory/disk warning Hermes shows is here: ranked conditions, only the worst undismissed one on screen, a suspected OOM restart, dismissal per boot, clearing on confirmed recovery, and a watch that does not depend on autonomy. agents/core/resource_pressure.py holds it apart from the autonomy observer, whose thresholds it reuses (85 % elevated and 95 % critical for memory and disk: DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS, :39, pinned to observer.DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS). (1) Ranking. CONDITIONS (:38) orders disk_critical > memory_critical > oom_restart_suspected > disk_elevated > memory_elevated. PressureMonitor.snapshot (:259) answers every raised condition in that order, with its level, percent, since and whether it is dismissed, plus the worst one not dismissed. Disk covers every watched volume, and the entry names the paths near or over the line. (2) Volumes. take_sample (:81) reads psutil memory and each distinct watched path once (watched_paths, :283: the filesystem root and the data home). A reading that fails is None, never a healthy 0 %, and changes nothing. (3) Hysteresis. Each resource's _Held.update (:109) raises at once. It clears, or steps critical down to elevated, only after RECOVERY_SAMPLES (3, :40) samples in a row under the line by RECOVERY_MARGIN (5 points, :41). A reading just under the line is not counted and restarts the count, so a flapping reading neither clears nor re-raises. (4) Suspected OOM restart. A small state file in the data home (_write_state, :159, atomic through a temporary file, left behind on no failure) holds the boot id (current_boot_id, :69: the kernel's /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, else one from psutil's boot time), the memory level, the dismissals and a clean-shutdown mark. start (:172) finds a run on the same boot that ended without the mark while memory was elevated or critical, and raises oom_restart_suspected naming that level. It logs a warning, and says "suspected" because the kernel's log is not read. stop (:191) writes the mark. The web lifespan calls start before the hub serves and stop as the very first teardown step, so a later step that hangs cannot make a clean stop look like a kill (agents/web.py:642, :649). (5) Dismissal. dismiss (:269) takes a condition and this boot's id. It refuses another boot's id, an unknown condition or one not raised. The dismissal persists across a restart on the same boot; a new boot re-arms it, and so does the condition's recovery, because a new episode is a new warning. Unknown names in the file are dropped. (6) Sampling apart from autonomy. SchedulerService.schedule_pressure_monitor (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:431) samples every 60 s on the hub's scheduler, so autonomy off or ESTOP engaged does not stop it. The route samples on demand when the last sample is over a minute old (fresh, :226). Samples from the route's worker thread and the scheduler are folded in one at a time under a lock. (7) Surfaces. GET /api/system/pressure and POST /api/system/pressure/dismiss {condition, boot_id} are both user-guarded (agents/core/routers/pressure.py:30, :36; 409 on a refused dismissal). The HUD's frontend/src/pressure-banner.tsx is mounted under the power chip (frontend/src/app.tsx:514). It polls the route, shows only the worst undismissed condition in one sentence (an alert for critical and a suspected OOM restart, a status for elevated), and dismisses it for this boot. Tests: tests/test_h161_resource_pressure.py (40) and frontend src/test/pressure-banner.test.tsx (6). They cover the ranking, the volumes, the hysteresis (a margin, a near reading, a step-down, an unreadable sample), the dismissal (this boot, stale boot, unknown, re-armed by a new boot and by recovery, persisted), the OOM suspicion and each of its three conditions, the state file (atomic, damaged, unwritable, failed replace, unknown names), the boot id, concurrent samples, the route, the guards, the scheduler job and the lifespan order. 50 mutants: 47 caught after ten survivors got cases. m11 (raise on > instead of >=) is equivalent: a same-level reading resets the count on both paths. The since line was simplified rather than kept as an equivalent. m23 (writing in place instead of the atomic replace) is a crash-consistency property that only a crash mid-write shows.

Built on this branch. Hermes has a Documentation page inside its dashboard with an "open in a new tab" affordance. Nerva's written material (the user guide, FLAGS.md on what each posture flag costs, and the privacy and camera-privacy notes) was only in the repository. The Dockerfile copied it into the image, but nothing served it.

(1) The route. agents/core/routers/help_docs.py is registered in agents/web.py (agents/web.py:1520) and user-guarded on the router (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:27).
- GET /api/help/docs (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:103) lists the allowlist: slug, title, whether the file shipped, and each document's sections.
- GET /api/help/docs/{slug} (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:113) returns the Markdown text, capped at MAX_DOC_CHARS with a truncated flag (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:121).
- The allowlist is the fixed DOCS table (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:31): user-guide, flags, privacy, camera-privacy. A slug is only ever a key into it, never joined into a path, so an unknown slug, '../' or encoded traversal is 404.

(2) The page. DocsPanel (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:37) is registered in the console's Start group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:6), in PANEL_COMPONENTS (frontend/src/gap.tsx:4809) and in the desktop app's route allowlist (desktop/src-tauri/hud-routes.json:49).

The HUD now has one confirmation for every action that needs one, graded the way the approval queue grades risk, and agent text renders as Markdown wherever it is shown. Both halves of Hermes' confirm-and-render behaviour are covered. (1) One confirmation, graded by RiskTier. frontend/src/confirm.tsx declares RISK_TIER (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:19) with the names and values of agents/core/autonomy/policy.py:26 RiskTier, and tests/test_confirm_tiers.py:22 ties the two lists together. confirmStyle (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:23) gives READ_ONLY one click, REVERSIBLE two steps (the button arms, a second button confirms) and EXTERNAL and IRREVERSIBLE_OR_MONEY a phrase typed exactly (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:143); a tier it does not know takes the most. ConfirmAction (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:74) moves focus to the control that replaced the one pressed. Escape cancels, and a cancelled phrase is not remembered (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:95). Enter confirms only on a match. An action that returns a promise keeps the confirmation open, with both buttons held, until it lands; one that answers false keeps it armed to retry (fire, frontend/src/confirm.tsx:97). A page can open and close it itself (armed/onCancel, frontend/src/confirm.tsx:114, taking focus as it opens, :110) or keep a typed one always open (open: no trigger, no cancel). (2) Every hand-rolled site uses it. The kill switch's HALT ALL stays one click on purpose, because an emergency stop must never wait for a second click; disengage is typed (DISENGAGE, frontend/src/gap.tsx:772, :774). Forget-me types FORGET (frontend/src/gap.tsx:3241) and the acquisition purge its phrase (frontend/src/gap.tsx:4138). Trust-ops rotation types the scope in an always-open confirmation that a refusal leaves filled and a rotation clears (frontend/src/panels/trust-ops.tsx:397). The marketplace uninstall types the folder it deletes, because the rmtree has no undo on this box; a changed folder is typed again, and a refusal keeps it armed (frontend/src/panels/marketplace-admin.tsx:313, confirmRemove :207). The webhook delete is two steps, opened by the row and held while that row's switch is pending (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:420, remove :285). The ESTOP pause is two steps (frontend/src/modes3.tsx:209). tests/test_confirm_tiers.py:26 checks that each of these files imports and uses ConfirmAction and has no window.confirm. (3) Markdown wherever agent text is shown. Chat bubbles, for agent and vision replies (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:77, :93), and decision cards (frontend/src/shell.tsx:144) render through Bubble (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:127). Bubble is memoised on the text, so a streamed token re-parses one bubble. It uses the shared React-only Markdown (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:101): lists, fences, tables and http(s) or same-origin links render, while raw HTML and any other link stay text. Canvas Markdown artifacts go through the same renderer (MarkdownBody, frontend/src/artifacts.tsx:78) and are bounded to MARKDOWN_LIMIT (4,000) code points when shown as well as when saved. A new breaks option (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:171) keeps a single newline as a line break for chat and artifacts, and documents keep paragraph joining. The owner's own turns are shown exactly as typed. Test-manual gap G22 (collapsed newlines, fences as prose) is closed. Tests: frontend/src/test/confirm.test.tsx has 11 tests: the grading, click, two steps, typed and case, busy and disabled, a promise and a refusal, a rejected promise, the controlled and open modes, a cancelled phrase, and inert labels. frontend/src/test/markdown-adoption.test.tsx has 6: the agent, vision, user, decision-card and artifact rendering, line breaks, and the bound cut on a code point. frontend/src/test/markdown.test.tsx gains 1 for breaks. The kill-switch, marketplace, trust-ops and webhooks tests each gain cases, and the purge, marketplace and artifact tests follow the new steps. tests/test_confirm_tiers.py has 2. Of 51 mutants, 48 are caught, eight of them after survivors got new cases. The three survivors were equivalent (the return value of a confirmation the page closes itself, a guard ConfirmAction already enforces, and a pause whose success unmounts the card), and that code was removed.

reviews.summary: The uninstall model exists and is sound. plan_uninstall (agents/core/uninstall.py:50) is a side-effect-free probe reporting which UNINSTALL_TARGETS exist, and as what kind. run_uninstall (agents/core/uninstall.py:65) removes only those targets and reports what it could not remove. Data erasure is a separate opt-in that runs purge_data backup-first before any target is removed. The CLI _main (agents/core/uninstall.py:127) refuses without --confirm (agents/core/uninstall.py:134). uninstall.sh and UNINSTALL.bat wrap the module. tests/test_uninstall.py checks the targets against install.sh/INSTALL.bat, plan reporting (tests/test_uninstall.py:75), idempotence and purge ordering. The data half is already reachable in-app: BackupPanel's typed FORGET reveal (frontend/src/gap.tsx:3217) calls POST /api/admin/forget (agents/core/routers/backup.py:99), which requires {confirm: 'FORGET'}. The row's kernel gate would plug into agents/core/kernel/registry.py, which has no uninstall action today.
reviews.remaining:
There is no uninstall from inside the app.
- plan_uninstall has no caller outside tests: no --gui-summary flag, no admin route serving the pre-flight summary, and no HUD Danger-zone panel rendering it.
- No route or HUD control runs the software-only or software+data removal.
- The run must cross the kernel at the irreversible tier (approval queue floor) with a typed confirmation.
- It must be executed by a detached cleanup that waits for the hub process to exit before deleting the .venv the hub runs from.

reviews.summary: Execuția guvernată pe altă mașină există. Ținta declarată de owner intră în registrul de politici din aceeași sursă ca detaliile de conexiune, iar o comandă trece hardline → politica țintei → aprobare durabilă → contractul terminal.exec pe rădăcinile remote declarate → Action Kernel înainte să atingă firul. Firul rulează un argv reconstruit cu shlex pe shell-ul remote (niciun string de shell nu pleacă de aici), cu cheia de gazdă pinuită, doar pe cheie, fără ~/.ssh/config, fără agent și fără forwarding. Default-off în spatele JARVIS_TERMINAL_SSH_HOST; cu flagul nesetat inventarul rămâne identic.
reviews.remaining: Rândul cere mult peste execuție și restul nu e livrat: manager de conexiuni ControlMaster, erori clasificate, sugestii de gazde din ~/.ssh/config, bootstrap care refolosește-sau-pornește un serviciu remote, revalidare de liveness, tranzacție de update cu jurnal de recuperare și linii de restore per profil, fan-out "update all instances". ControlMaster e o divergență deliberată, nu o scăpare: un socket de control partajat e un canal autentificat reutilizabil lăsat pe disc, iar transportul îl dezactivează explicit. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: nicio sesiune SSH reală nu a fost deschisă din această livrare — suita e ermetică, fără socket și fără binar ssh, deci interoperabilitatea cu un sshd real rămâne nedovedită.

Refolosește ChatMode, autentificarea HUD și sesiunea server; refresh la focus/finalizarea unui turn fără suprascrierea streamului. Compilare și verificare UI macOS. Invalidările primite cât timp turnul local este ocupat sunt păstrate și reconciliate la idle; teste cu BroadcastChannel asincron real verifică două ferestre cu turnuri suprapuse.
