reviews.summary: Nerva keeps the machine awake while a turn runs, reads and streams its power state, and eases off on battery, as Hermes does. agents/core/power.py holds one shared power assertion while at least one turn runs (KeepAwake, refcounted). It is off by default and turned on with JARVIS_KEEP_AWAKE=1 (keep_awake_enabled). The mechanism is the platform's own (backend_name, backend_argv): caffeinate -i -w <hub pid> on macOS, systemd-inhibit --what=idle:sleep --mode=block around tail --pid=<hub pid> on Linux, so both helpers end with the hub even when it is killed, and SetThreadExecutionState on Windows. The helper is started in its own process group (start_new_session) and released by signalling that group while its leader is still unreaped, so the child systemd-inhibit starts ends too; a helper that already exited is reaped by its handle, and one that ignores SIGTERM is killed after one second. A missing binary or mechanism never fails a turn and is reported (status error), as is a helper that exits on its own. Every turn entry holds it: Orchestrator.handle_input, handle_input_stream and the one-shot process take it at the start (hold_for_turn) and drop it in their finally (release_for_turn), so a reply, an error and a cancel all release it; the lifespan releases every hold at shutdown (agents/web.py) and atexit does at exit. It is gated as host.control (authorize_keep_awake), in the llm_control order: the owner's system-control permission, the host-control contract, whose action list now names power.keep_awake (agents/core/autonomy/remediation.py), an Action Kernel GRANT (the kernel must be on; QUEUE, DENY and anything that is not a GRANT refuse), then a durable audit row (no audit log, or a refused row, refuses too). The action carries the fixed trusted origin, since keep-awake is the owner's switch and not the content of the turn that asks first. It is asked once per process; a refusal keeps it off until the next start and is named in the status. The power state comes from psutil.sensors_battery (read_battery: on battery, percent, plugged). A resume from sleep is seen as the wall clock running more than 60 s ahead of the monotonic clock between two reads (PowerMonitor.tick), which stops while Linux and macOS sleep, and is shown for ten minutes. The scheduler reads it every minute (SchedulerService.schedule_power_monitor, skipped under JARVIS_TESTING), so a resume is noticed without anyone asking. GET /api/power answers the power state, the deferral threshold, whether background work is being deferred and the keep-awake status (enabled, active, holders, backend, refused, error); GET /api/power/stream pushes the same payload to a connected client on every change, with a keepalive while it does not change (agents/core/routers/power.py). Both are user-guarded. Battery-aware throttling: below system.battery_defer_percent (a settings row, 50 by default; 0 never, 100 always on battery) on battery, or on battery with an unknown charge, the heavy background jobs skip their run and return deferred_on_battery, which scheduler health records as skipped: memory maintenance, the tech scout, the learning-loop promotions, prompt evolution and the WorldView KG sync (the last three through SchedulerService wrappers the scheduler now registers). An unreadable power state lets the job run. Nothing the owner asks for directly is deferred. The HUD shell shows a PowerChip (frontend/src/power-chip.tsx): on battery with the charge and whether background jobs wait, a wake from sleep, and keep-awake holding, ready or refused with its reason; a plugged-in machine with keep-awake off shows nothing. It polls GET /api/power every minute and follows the stream where the browser can attach to it. The desktop shell turns webview background throttling off for both windows (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs, background_throttling), so a HUD in the background keeps reading a streaming reply instead of being suspended and having its turn cancelled; NERVA_DESKTOP_BACKGROUND_THROTTLING=throttle or suspend asks for it back and an unknown value is named and ignored (desktop/src-tauri/src/throttling.rs). macOS 14+ honours the policy; Linux and Windows webviews ignore it. The binding-writer inventory's pinned lines in scheduler_service.py move with the file. Tests: tests/test_h182_power.py (76), including a real helper process whose own child is ended by the release, and rustc unit tests of throttling.rs; src/test/power-chip.test.tsx (6). 100 mutants: 98 killed after five cases were added; the other two were redundant checks, removed.

Motorul SQLite, CLI și HUD pot crea, edita, porni, pune pe pauză, relua și șterge joburi; există istoric, un constructor vizual de program, galeria de 16 blueprint-uri tipizate (`BLUEPRINTS` din `jobs.py`, bază + `EXTRA_BLUEPRINTS`) și o țintă de livrare per job (`Job.channel`). Reevaluat 2026-09-19: textul anterior spunea „3 blueprint-uri și nicio țintă per job" — ambele expirate.
reviews.remaining: „Deliver to" în Hermes e o listă cu mai multe ținte bifabile; Nerva are o singură țintă per job (`channel: str | None`), nu mai multe. Avertismentul de impact al modelului și toast-ul de confirmare pentru un model scump nu sunt verificate în panou. Crearea unui job trebuie să treacă prin kernel (`schedule.create` nou, sau `goal.approve` refolosit) — kind în `agents/core/kernel/**`, path protejat, sarcina owner-ului. NEVERIFICAT pe scheduler și canale reale.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 together with H153 (critic note 7: one spec, one panel), then fixed after an adversarial review. The v2 console has a Webhooks panel, WebhooksPanel (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:187), registered in the Interop group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:50; frontend/src/gap.tsx:16). Interop mode's WEBHOOKS list links to it by an accessible name (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:341). Every panel call sends the admin credential. The backend stays admin-only CRUD: list, create, switch and delete all carry Depends(admin_guard) (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:174, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:180, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:193, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:220).

Interop mode is built from its four sources alone (hydrateInterop, frontend/src/api/live.ts:126). All four (A2A peers, MCP servers, widgets, webhooks) are admin-only routes and are fetched with the admin credential, and so is the webhooks settings category: while the receiver switch is off every webhook row reads "receiver off", and a switch it could not read is said under WEBHOOKS (frontend/src/api/live.ts:119, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:342). A section whose source failed is empty and says "not connected", and an empty real list says "none" (Section, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:302); the demo seed's rows are never shown under the LIVE chip. When no source answers nothing is overwritten, so the mode stays "Not connected" and DEMO keeps its seed. The review found that fetching only the webhooks list with the credential had marked the whole mode LIVE over seeded peers, MCP servers and widgets.

The five accepted parts:
(1) Create dialog: name, agent or workflow target, target id and an HMAC-signed toggle, and, since H153, a description, an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only, posted to POST /api/webhooks. A refusal shows the hub's own reason, and an empty target is refused before any request. The create button is held while the call is pending and while a new hook's credentials are on screen, so a second hook cannot replace a secret before it was saved.
(2) Created result, shown once (Reveal, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:145): the absolute trigger URL (triggerUrl, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:52: the page origin, the base path and the encoded id), and the token, or the signing secret for a signed hook, each with a copy button that says "copied" in a polite live region, plus the header the sender must send. Only the warning sentence is an alert, so a screen reader does not read the secret aloud. On a loopback origin it says a sender elsewhere needs an address it can reach. The secret lives only in the panel's state and is dropped on "I have saved it" (focus returns to the create form) or unmount. The list never carries it: WebhookStore masks the token to a 4-character hint (agents/core/webhooks.py:635).
(3) Detail pane: clicking a hook expands its trigger URL, auth header (with the token hint), calls, last call and creation time, the deliveries its event list skipped and the last event skipped, and an editor for its event list and prompt template (H153). The row shows target_type:target, an HMAC or token badge, an on/off badge and an event-count badge.
(4) Delete with confirmation: "delete…" arms an inline confirmation that explains the sender's credential dies with the hook and moves focus to "delete for good", which sends DELETE; "keep it" returns focus to "delete…". Each row button's accessible name includes the hook's name. A row's buttons are held while its call is pending, and every switch or delete reloads the list whatever the hub answered: a hook already deleted elsewhere is reported as gone ("ci was already deleted", "ci no longer exists") and its row disappears, with focus moved to the create form; a refused delete keeps the confirmation and says why. A per-hook on/off switch (PATCH, H153) is offered as the reversible alternative.
(5) Governance: creating, switching and deleting a hook each write a SecurityEvent (_audit_webhook, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:142, called at agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:189, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:214 and agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:226). It names the hook id, the target as a JSON string (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:136), so a target cannot pass its own text off as the row's id or flags, and the signed and enabled flags as the store reads them, never the token or signing secret. A delete of an unknown id writes nothing and answers 404 "webhook not found".

The receiver-disabled banner: when the receiver switch (H153, the setting webhooks.receiver_enabled) is off, the panel's receiver row says every delivery is refused until it is switched back on (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:352). The restart-gateway banner is not needed: a delivery sees the switch at most a second old (at once after a write in this process), and hook CRUD is served live; the receiver row says so. Not built, and not part of this row: a `nerva webhooks` CLI verb (critic note 7 places it with H409, as `nerva webhooks inbound|outbound`) and a mobile screen.

Tests: frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx has 55 cases. By describe block, 22 are this row's (the panel, the trigger URL and the review round), and 13 of those failed on the pre-review panel: the pending hold, the reload and the ghost row after a switch or delete, the one-POST create and the create held while a secret shows, the hook-named buttons, focus, the alert without the secret, the "copied" live region, the loopback hint and an unencodable id. The other 33 are H153's: the subscriptions, the receiver row and banner, the event list, the template, Deliver to, focus after a hook is gone, the push note and a proxy's 404. frontend/src/test/interop-live-honesty.test.tsx (14 cases, 5 of them H153's receiver read) drives the real useLiveModes against admin-guarded mock routes and renders InteropMode. The backend audit and DELETE guards are pinned in tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:353, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:362, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:371). Mutation: 60 mutants of the review round's guards (11 backend, 27 panel, 15 Interop, 7 v1) and 16 of the H153 panel additions were each run against their own suite, and all were caught; before the review round, 12 of the reviewer's 42 mutants had survived.

The installed-tree and registry surfaces are wired end to end. GET /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:37) and the admin-guarded marketplace routes (list, history, rollback, publish, install, install-zip, review, uninstall, pending, approve; agents/core/routers/skills.py:479-713) each have a HUD caller. The console panels are all registered in frontend/src/console-routes.ts: SKILLS MARKETPLACE (review + rollback, frontend/src/gap.tsx:1782), Marketplace Admin (frontend/src/panels/marketplace-admin.tsx: publish, install-zip and uninstall keyed by folder name, which avoids the manifest-title trap), Skills Import, Skill History, Pending Skills and the Security Skills Map. Per-skill usage counters (use_count, last_used_at) are tracked in agents/core/skills/usage.py:34. SkillCurator (agents/core/skills/curator.py:36) archives stale agent-created, unpinned skills on its own schedule. Per-agent scoping exists only as author-declared manifest `agents:` filtering in SkillLoader.catalog_gate (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1353-1354), which prompt_catalog applies, and the static agents.yaml `tools:` list (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:52). test_skills_api.py, test_skill_lifecycle_curator.py and test_skill_approval_revoke.py: 37 pass.
reviews.remaining: Both gaps the rationale accepts are absent. (1) Per-agent skill enable/disable as a capability grant: the permission ledger's SURFACES (agents/core/permission_ledger.py:69) has no skill surface. No route or HUD control enables or disables a skill for an agent, there is no All master switch, and neither SkillLoader.prompt_catalog nor SkillLoader.execute (agents/core/skills/loader.py:548) consults an owner-set grant. The manifest `agents:` field is author-controlled and only un-advertises. (2) A 'Disable unused' sweep: usage.py records use_count and last_used_at, but no owner-triggered route or control disables idle skills. The curator acts only on agent-created skills, on its own schedule, and never on imported or bundled ones. The profile-scope selector waits on the profile export/import row.

reviews.summary: Memoria și graful au backend; DW-1 afișează entități și legături reale, cu mostre doar în Demo.
reviews.remaining: Rămân timeline/as-of, paritatea exploratorului și controalele de memorie cerute de rând; o listă de vecini nu închide harta semantică.

reviews.summary: The HUD's keyboard shortcuts live in one registry, as in Hermes. frontend/src/shortcuts.ts defines every action once (ACTIONS: id, category, label, default chord, scope): the ten mode keys, World (w), the Console (`), Ambient (a), Cinema (m) and its three stages (o, n, b, scope cinema), focus the message box (/), the command palette (mod+k) and the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (mod+/). app.tsx, world_app.tsx and the cinema overlay in shell.tsx dispatch through matchAction over bindings(overrides) instead of literal key maps. frontend/src/shortcuts-panel.tsx is the panel mod+/ opens: categories Navigation, View, Composer and Session with search (searchBindings); click a chord to record a new one ("Press a key…", Esc cancels, a lone modifier keeps listening; chordFromEvent, rebind); per-binding reset and Reset all (resetBinding); an "Also bound to X" note when two actions share a chord (conflictsFor). Overrides persist per viewer in localStorage under hud.shortcuts, validated on read (readOverrides, loadOverrides, saveOverrides), and survive storage that is off. Governance: defineActions refuses any action whose id, category or label names an approval, a decision, an accept, reject, deny or consent (FORBIDDEN_TARGET), so no chord can reach a Decision Inbox action. Tests: frontend/src/test/shortcuts.test.tsx (16), app-routing.test.tsx (+3: panel, rebinding, persistence, World, composer focus), cinema.test.tsx (+1: rebound stage keys); 38 mutants, 36 killed, 2 equivalent.

Archived chats exist, as in Hermes. CheckpointManager.set_archived stamps or clears archived_at in a session's metadata without creating a session. get_sessions(archived=...) filters on it in SQL, read only from valid JSON, so the limit counts only the view asked for. agents/core/routers/sessions.py serves several routes. GET /sessions leaves archived chats out; ?archived=true lists only them, each row with archived_at. POST /sessions/{id}/archive and /unarchive (user_guard) are 404 for an unknown session and 400 for an invalid id. Resuming a chat through POST /sessions/resume unarchives it. agents/core/session_archive.py holds the rest. run_auto_archive archives sessions whose ended_at, else started_at, is older than memory.auto_archive_days (0 = off, at most 3650) and never touches the active one; SchedulerService.schedule_auto_archive runs it daily at 03:40. DELETE /sessions/{id}?confirm=DELETE is admin_guard only and refuses the active session (409) and an unknown one (404). delete_session first collects every trace of the session: the sessions row, its checkpoints and session_clock rows, the transcript snapshot and JSONL log, its TodoStore plan and the precompress compaction archive. It writes them to <data home>/backups/sessions/<id>-<stamp>.json (mkstemp 0600, fsync of file and directory, os.replace, read back and verified). Only then does it delete them all and clear the live conversation. A backup that does not land raises backup_failed and deletes nothing. The HUD SessionsPanel (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx) has chats and archived tabs, archive, unarchive and a two-step "delete permanently" that names the backup. llm.project_dir, the default project directory inside the file roots, is where H594 reads convention files from (project_context.start_dir). Tests: tests/test_h218_archived_chats.py (39), frontend/src/test/sessions-archive.test.tsx (7); 41 mutants, 38 killed, 3 equivalent.

Spend is measured and capped. cost_tracker records each agent turn against the routed model, persists per-UTC-day rollups and flags unpriced calls (agents/core/cost_tracker.py). apm_summary (agents/core/cost_tracker.py:381) returns {totals, by_agent, by_model} (agents/core/cost_tracker.py:456), served by the admin-guarded GET /api/admin/apm (agents/core/routers/admin.py:554). agents/core/routers/analytics.py adds GET /api/analytics/cost (analytics.py:92), /api/analytics/model-tiers with local/fast/standard/heavy/unknown tiers (analytics.py:99), /api/analytics/locality (analytics.py:151) and per-agent/per-day /api/cost (analytics.py:309). The Trust-mode %-local meter reads /api/analytics/locality (frontend/src/app.tsx:457, derivation in frontend/src/locality.ts). test_h10_16_apm.py, test_cost_measurement_and_cap.py, test_h10_24_cost_trace.py and test_cost_tracker.py: 59 pass.
reviews.remaining: The owner still cannot see where the money went. The only HUD reader, APMPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1876-1883), reads d.runs, d.tokens and d.cost, but apm_summary nests those under d.totals. Every field therefore renders '—', and no per-agent or per-model breakdown is shown. /api/cost, /api/analytics/cost and /api/analytics/model-tiers have no HUD caller. No surface shows a local-vs-cloud split of spend or tokens: the %-local meter counts runs only. The Command Center has no Usage section. There is no per-session context/usage meter (tokens, context used/max/percent, cost): the /chat ChatResponse in agents/web.py carries only reply, pending_approvals, H677's warming flag and H674's notices, and the CLI usage report hard-codes cost_basis 'unavailable' (agents/cli/nerva.py:1760).

reviews.summary: Nerva shows whether it is listening outside its main window, as Hermes does. agents/core/voice/listening.py keeps one process-wide, thread-safe listening state per source (ListeningState, STATE). The host's own voice path publishes it: the wake-word detector marks hub armed once it holds the mic open and off when it stops (WakeWordDetector.start, stop; agents/core/voice/wake_word.py), and a capture marks hub listening while it records, thinking while it transcribes and answers, speaking while it plays the reply, and falls back to armed (or off when the detector is not running) in a finally, so an early end or a failure never leaves it lit (VoicePipeline._capture_and_process; stop marks it off; agents/core/voice/pipeline.py). Wyoming satellites publish it too: an authenticated satellite's detection or voice-started marks satellite:<id> listening and voice-stopped marks it thinking; a transcript marks it thinking while it is answered and clears it after; a closed connection clears whatever it lit; with authentication required an unauthenticated peer can set nothing, and with authentication off the one anonymous satellite is named satellite (LISTEN_EVENTS, WyomingServer._listening_source, handle_connection; agents/core/voice/wyoming.py). The API is get / set / on-change in process: set_state (a bounded, printable source name and one of off, armed, listening, thinking, speaking; off forgets the source; at most 32 sources), snapshot (each source's state, the loudest by ORDER — listening, then armed, both an open mic, then thinking, speaking, off — mic_open, and a seq that moves on every change), subscribe and unsubscribe (callbacks run outside the lock and a failing one is ignored). A transient state not re-said for 120 s expires, and the expiry moves seq, so a crashed capture never leaves the indicator on; an armed mic stays. GET /api/voice/listening answers the snapshot and GET /api/voice/listening/stream pushes it on every change with keepalives (agents/core/routers/voice.py); both are user-guarded and GET-only, so nothing can set the state over HTTP. Every writer and reader loads the one agents.core.voice.listening module (a test pins it, since core.X and agents.core.X load as different modules here). The push to the desktop shell: frontend/src/listening.ts follows the stream with the HUD's own token (EventSource cannot send one) and falls back to polling every 5 s; it combines the hub's state with the window's own mic (useVoice active counts as listening), and only inside the desktop app forwards the loudest to the shell (setDesktopListening in frontend/src/desktop.tsx sends only changes and re-sends after a refused call; a closing window sends off). The indicator surface is the tray icon (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs): a desktop_listening command, allowed only to the local HUD windows (verify, capability allow-desktop-listening, build.rs manifest), records each window's state on a board and shows the loudest (desktop/src-tauri/src/indicator.rs): a menu-bar title while a mic is open (● listening, ○ wake word) — shown on macOS and next to the icon on Linux, not on Windows — and a tooltip naming the state on macOS and Windows. It is read-only: nothing on the tray or in the command can open or close a mic. Tests: tests/test_h222_listening.py (44), including the capture's state trail, every early end, a failing transcription, authenticated, unauthenticated and anonymous satellites and a satellite dropping mid-capture, the stream framing, the routes and guard, the shell's command, permission and capability, and the rustc unit tests of indicator.rs; src/test/listening.test.tsx (8) and src/test/desktop-listening.test.ts (3). 65 mutants: 64 killed after five cases were added; the other was a redundant check, removed. The desktop crate was not compiled here: its tray calls were checked against the Tauri 2.11.5 source.

Hermes' "what can it do right now" view is here: one read-only answer, for one agent as seen by one principal, built from the code a turn runs and served on three surfaces. agents/core/inspector.py holds it; build_inspector (:108) returns up to five sections (SECTIONS, :63). (1) Views. VIEWS (:56) names the five tool-profile postures: the owner and a guest on the HUD (owner, guest), the owner and a stranger on an external channel (inbound-owner, inbound; Telegram stands for every channel, under the inbound action origin a real channel turn has) and no human (internal). The look binds that principal and origin in a task of its own (:125), so nothing it binds, and nothing the runtime notes while resolving the offer, outlives it. (2) status (_status, :155): version, the backend and model the router serves, the local model's state through project_llm_status, the transcript budget llm.tool_loop_context_tokens (0 reads as 75 % of the model window), the tool loop and safe mode. (3) tools (_tools, :194): the tool runtime's own resolved offer for the agent under that principal (_resolve_offer: registry or the capability registry's view, job toolset, posture, the agent's tools: list, the shared-session rule), not the raw registry. Each row says whether the tool is gated and whether its output is fenced as untrusted, with the description cut to DESCRIPTION_CHARS (160, :65). The withheld names are listed, a resolver failure offers nothing, and loop_enabled says whether the model sees any of them (with the loop off they are what the posture would offer). (4) skills (_skills, :215): the rows prompt_catalog gives the prompt under that principal and that offer, or none when llm.skills_in_prompt is off. (5) mcp (_mcp, :225): each server's transport, trust tier, transport-aware liveness (is_connected, so an HTTP server reads connected; a probe that raises is down) and visible tools, with no URL or command line. (6) system_prompt (_prompt, :253): the agent's system prompt and the user part Agent.build_prompt sends for an empty user message: persona, agent context, the core-memory block, the runtime, language and grounding rails and the skills block. tokens (:266) estimates what that fixed part costs every turn before history. The texts are masked by the log redactor (SecretRedactionFilter; nothing is shown when it cannot load, _redactor :73) and capped together at PROMPT_CAP_BYTES (64 KiB, :64) on a character boundary. The core block is read with freeze=False (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3056, :3098, :3125): the frozen block when a turn froze one, else a fresh render that is not kept, so a look never fixes the day's snapshot. (7) Surfaces. GET /api/admin/inspector?agent=&view=&section= (agents/core/routers/status.py:123, admin-guarded; 404 for an unknown agent, 400 naming the views or sections, 503 before the hub is up). nerva inspect [agent] [--as VIEW] [--section tools|skills|prompt|mcp|status] [--json] (cmd_inspect, agents/cli/nerva.py:927; render_inspector :948) prints the same payload section by section, or as it came. The HUD's Inspector panel (frontend/src/panels/inspector.tsx, Console → Admin) reads the same route with a status line, an As switch and folding sections. Tests: tests/test_inspector.py (43) builds a partial orchestrator over the coordinator's real ToolRPC registry. It covers the guest's tools equal to ToolProfileResolver's set and not the registry, every view's posture and bindings, the agent's list, the marks and the cut, the loop off, a failing resolver, an unwired runtime, the skills, the prompt (skills block, core memory, rails, empty message, tokens), the unfrozen core block, masking, the withheld prompt, the 64 KiB cap on a split character, no leaked binding, MCP liveness, the status line and safe mode, section order, the route (payload, defaults, refusals, admin token, guard snapshot, 503) and the CLI (--json equal to the payload, rendering, --section, the loop-off line, the tree, one list of views and sections). frontend/src/panels/inspector.test.tsx has 4. 82 mutants: 79 caught, ten after survivors got cases. One redundant reset was simplified away. The origin passed to classify_turn is equivalent, because each view's principal alone decides the surface.

Nerva copies Hermes's setup.runtime_check into the owner's terminal. The hub resolves the route with the same llm_router.select_backend call a Jarvis turn makes (agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:269) and names its verdict: a local provider/model pair must be resident, and a cloud route (Gemini, Claude, or the cloud-compatible adapter set by llm.compatible_provider) counts only when the router handed back the very backend that route names (agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:142, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:307-315), and (H380) when its provider accepts the key that route would use. A real HybridRouter pins this for the local, cloud-flash, claude and both cloud-compatible paths (tests/test_first_run_command_center.py:533). `nerva doctor` (and `python scripts/doctor.py`) adds the advisory runtime_resolves row: one GET of /api/onboarding/command-center at the hub `nerva status` reads (scripts/doctor.py:275), run only after /readyz answered at that same address and otherwise reported as skip, never ok (scripts/doctor.py:424-428). It sends one credential, the user token when both are set and the admin token only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address (scripts/doctor.py:392-399, scripts/doctor.py:345), never prints it, and is ok only on a ready verdict that names the route, provider and model (scripts/doctor.py:475-479). A refused token, a reply cut off mid-body, a listener that does not speak HTTP, a bad URL or an odd resident list is a named warn, not a traceback (scripts/doctor.py:455-460; tests/test_doctor.py:433, tests/test_doctor.py:458). `nerva status` now labels the old any-model state 'resident' and adds a runnable: line from the same verdict (agents/cli/nerva.py:572); a timeout or reset on that read shows 'unknown — hub_unreachable' and the rest of the status still prints (agents/cli/nerva.py:582). A reply cut off mid-body or a garbled status line on any hub read is HubUnavailable, so `nerva status` reports an unreachable hub instead of a traceback (agents/cli/client.py:181, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:181). Both tools dial a wildcard bind (0.0.0.0, ::) over loopback (agents/cli/client.py:56). An end-to-end test drives both terminal checks against the real app (tests/test_first_run_command_center.py:590). Diagnostics stay local: the redacted bundle is served over one admin GET (agents/core/routers/support.py:21), and neither module imports a network client (tests/test_support_bundle.py:67), so the share_nous upload stays refused. The projects/workspaces model was skipped by decision. Known limits the row does not require: the verdict is for the route a short Jarvis chat takes; and a cloud route is judged by the router's own selection, not by a live call.

The local half is admin-guarded and working. `GET /api/models/local` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:103) lists LM Studio/Ollama models and marks the active one. `POST /api/models/local/switch` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:363) switches models, and `POST /api/llm/load` / `unload` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:487, agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:515) load and unload them. The HUD reaches all of this through `LMStudioPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2393). The cloud side is read-only. `GET /api/llm/auth-profiles` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:442) returns masked Anthropic/Gemini pool status, rendered by `AuthProfilesPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2606). HybridRouter builds those pools only from environment variables (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:327, via `AuthProfilePool.from_env` at agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:86). The shared command catalog the row depends on exists: `GET /api/commands` (agents/core/routers/commands.py:29) with name/description/tier/usage, and `GET /api/quickbar/help` (agents/core/routers/quickbar.py:59). Both are consumed by `QuickbarPanel` (frontend/src/panels/quickbar.tsx:98), which lists commands but does not complete a partial line. Path completion is conditional in the rationale on a terminal client shipping. `nerva` has only the one-shot `nerva chat` and no interactive composer, so path completion is not owed yet.
reviews.remaining: (1) No provider options: no route returns models grouped by provider (cloud and local) with cost hints, and cost_tracker's price table is not shown per model. (2) No save-key: no admin route writes a provider API key to the secret store and returns the refreshed model list. The pools read env vars only, so a key saved at runtime would never reach the router without a pool rebuild. (3) No disconnect: no route removes a provider's credential and rebuilds its pool, so there is no single place to revoke a provider. No audit event exists for either write. `/api/secrets/broker` (agents/core/routers/secrets.py:29, agents/core/routers/secrets.py:56) stores action-time `{{secret:NAME}}` values, not the router's provider keys. (4) No slash completion: neither the chat composer nor QuickbarPanel completes command names or their `usage` arguments from `/api/commands` as the user types.

reviews.summary: The voice primitives exist; per-surface mic arbitration does not. Host side: `WakeWordDetector` (agents/core/voice/wake_word.py:28) runs inside `VoicePipeline`, which `VoiceChannel.start` (agents/core/channels/voice.py:24) starts. That channel is registered at boot with wake words from `general.wake_words` (agents/web.py:536). Browser side: frontend/src/voice.ts captures through getUserMedia, VAD-segments one utterance, and has 'hands-free' and 'ptt' modes (frontend/src/voice.ts:74). TTS and STT are user-guarded routes: `POST /tts`, `POST /api/voice/stt` and `GET /api/voice/capabilities` (agents/core/routers/voice.py:48, agents/core/routers/voice.py:198, agents/core/routers/voice.py:297). Per-chat spoken replies (the `/voice` toggle) are covered by tests/test_voice_mode.py. `config.set` maps to the admin settings PUT, and `ping` maps to `GET /healthz` (agents/core/routers/ops.py:42).
reviews.remaining: The adaptation's one required concept is missing. No arm/pause/resume/stop/status call carries a surface identity. Nothing records which surface (HUD browser loop, mobile, satellite, host pipeline) holds the microphone, so the host pipeline and a browser hands-free loop on the same machine can both open the device. No status call answers who holds the mic. Arming does not pass the capture-consent policy the governance requires; the policy that exists (mobile/src/screens/capturePolicy.ts) covers passive capture only. Arming also writes no audit event, and the host pipeline starts at boot with neither check. The separate open item that no install path installs a voice engine is outside this row.

reviews.summary: A settings reset now shows what it will change, never touches a secret and can be undone, and the HUD marks every setting that differs from its default. Hermes' config-reset and defaults surface is covered, on top of H157's search, secret-free export, dry-run import and per-category reset. (1) Defaults. Every declared row that is not a secret carries its declared default (agents/core/settings_db.py:583, in _mark_overlay :576, used by GET /api/admin/settings and each category read). A secret carries none. The Settings panel marks a row whose value, or staged edit, differs from its default ("changed", with the default in its tooltip); a ↺ button stages the default and the usual save writes it through the validated PUT (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2717). (2) A preview before any reset. plan_reset (agents/core/settings_db.py:1113) computes what a reset of one category, or of every category, would write: each declared setting that is not a secret and whose stored value is not its default. POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset and POST /api/admin/settings/reseed take {"dry_run": true} and answer the changes as current → default without writing anything (agents/core/routers/admin.py:261, :296; _dry_run_asked, :249; only a JSON true, in a body of at most 4 KB). The changes use describe_changes, so a credential-shaped value shows as (hidden). Arming the reset in the HUD asks for that preview and lists it, and names the secrets kept and the settings the posture still forces (ResetPreview, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:56; ResetCategory, :82). (3) The reseed no longer deletes the store. It used to run DELETE FROM settings, wiping every setting, secrets included, with no preview and no way back. It is now the per-category reset over every category: secrets are kept (and named), rows nothing declares are left, it takes a JSON request from this origin only (415/403 otherwise, as H157's writes), and it is audited with the settings that moved (agents/core/routers/admin.py:296). The v1 admin page sends it as JSON (agents/web/static/admin.js:1478). The HUD gets "reset every category…" with the same preview (ResetAll, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:105). (4) Undo. reset_settings (agents/core/settings_db.py:1152) writes the defaults and records what it replaced in settings_resets (:117) in the same transaction, keeping the last 20 (RESETS_KEPT, :1135). POST /api/admin/settings/undo (agents/core/routers/admin.py:325; undo_last_reset, agents/core/settings_db.py:1206) puts back the latest reset not yet undone. A setting changed since that reset, one its declaration no longer accepts, or one no longer declared is left as it is and named in skipped. The undo is audited, and the listeners hear every value a reset or an undo writes, so the webhook receiver switch follows it. GET /api/admin/settings/resets (agents/core/routers/admin.py:91; list_resets, agents/core/settings_db.py:1193) lists the resets, newest first, naming settings but never their values. The HUD shows "last reset: <scope> · N settings · <time>" with "undo…" (UndoReset, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:125). Every reset and undo in the HUD is a two-step ConfirmAction at the REVERSIBLE tier (H168). Adapted from the row's ask: the reseed does not go through the approval queue's irreversible tier, because it is no longer irreversible. It keeps secrets, previews, and can be undone. Routing it through the queue would need a new kernel action kind (agents/core/kernel is owner-only). Tests: tests/test_settings_defaults_undo.py has 24: defaults on rows and none for secrets; the plan (what moves, never a secret); a recorded reset and its undo; nothing moved means nothing recorded; the listeners; a setting changed since, no longer valid or no longer declared left as it is; latest first; the list keeps 20 and names no values; everything reset with secrets and undeclared rows kept; and the routes (admin-only, dry run, a hidden credential, JSON only with a 4 KB bound, the reseed's preview, audit and undo, nothing to undo 404, and /resets not taken for a category). frontend/src/test/settings-reset-undo.test.tsx has 7. The H157 reset test, the H153b reseed test (a JSON body) and the settings row-shape test (default) follow. Of 54 mutants, all 54 are caught, ten of them after survivors got cases.

The TTL-deletion half is in place. The retention settings are off by default, and a TTL of 0 means keep forever (agents/core/settings_db.py:424-425, plus audit, ingestion and artifact TTLs). run_retention (agents/core/retention.py:148) deletes session transcript files by last activity and prunes the audit chain through AuditLogger.prune_before, which re-anchors the Merkle chain (agents/core/security/audit.py:336). It also prunes Howard ingestion roots and unpinned binary artifacts. schedule_retention registers a daily 03:30 cron (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:195), and run_retention_purge (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:612) does nothing unless retention.enabled is set. tests/test_retention.py covers old-vs-new pruning, the TTL-0 no-op, chain verifiability after a prune and the default-off settings.
reviews.remaining: There is no reversible archive tier: purge_old_conversations unlinks files directly (agents/core/retention.py:76), with no soft-hide stage, no restore and no exemption for pinned sessions. Nothing runs VACUUM after a prune: prune_before issues DELETE FROM security_events (agents/core/security/audit.py:367) and commits, so the audit database file never shrinks. There is no vacuum_after_prune or min_vacuum_interval setting; the only VACUUM is on the forget path (agents/core/data_purge.py:243). There is no persisted last-run marker and no min-interval gate shared across processes; the sweep is a fixed daily cron in each scheduler process. Changes to retention TTLs or the enabled flag are ordinary admin PUT /api/admin/settings/retention writes. The governance field requires them to go through the irreversible approval tier instead.

reviews.summary: H270 stays PARTIAL; the triage's "already equivalent" does not survive contact with the code, and this re-read retires three claims the row had carried since before H502 (#1174 moved the hash while the text stood still) plus one the text was about to inherit. Hermes' contract has two halves and Nerva has only one of them. Outbound (what a child inherits) is genuinely stronger than Hermes and is tested: scrub_child_env (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:172-210) is default-deny with SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES (:17-33) plus the three-name JARVIS_CHILD_ALLOWED_ENV (:47-51), covered by tests/test_environment_primitives.py:62,90; STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST (agents/core/mcp/client.py:161-173) with stdio_env_baseline (:245-280) drops a credential-shaped name even when it is on the static list (:275, _SECRET_LIKE :174-176), covered by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:351 — and since H502 the baseline is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in: stdio_env_baseline_enabled() returns env_flag(STDIO_ENV_BASELINE_FLAG, True) (:179-190; flag :90 "Default ON"), docs/FLAGS.md says "on by default since H502" (its MCP defaults block, the JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE entry and the flag table row), and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins unset-flag → OPENAI_API_KEY withheld and =0 → full inherit (the row previously cited :395-399 as pinning the opposite; that was the pre-#1174 test, which at 45be62bd read "Flag off (default): historical behaviour — inherit everything"). The outbound allowlist's one deliberate exception is the owner's own: a name listed in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — owner-declared and host-wide, not an inbound gate. What #1179 changed here is disclosure, not policy: the module docstring (:17-39) now names the filesystem as a second recovery route for a same-UID child (cwd defaults to the hub's, so open(".env") reaches the file the keys came from), cwd_secret_files (:215-242) reports a readable .env/.env.local in the child's cwd, and _merged_env (:561-572) logs a WARNING "withholding is undercut" (:567) beside the INFO count, filenames only — pinned by tests :830-853 and :854-890. None of it touches a name policy, a writer or the override path, so it moves nothing for this row. The fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) is likewise off-subject: it added tool_patterns_over_bounds (agents/core/mcp/client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ (:407-418) and a bounds refusal for tools_allow/tools_deny in admin_mcp_add (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:202-208); none of it reads or writes an env name, and MCPServerConfig still has no env field, so only line numbers moved (client.py +19 from the new helper on and +31 from that __init__ block on; routers/mcp.py +4 from the filter check on). Inbound (what a surface may persist) does not exist as a policy at all: no ENV_VAR_NAME/ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env symbol anywhere in agents/, scripts/, tests/ or frontend/src/, and no `config.write` kind in agents/core/capability_actions.py. A correction the row must carry, because it shapes the deliverable: Hermes' hijack names are NOT all absent from the code. LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER appear nowhere outside the research docs, but PATH and SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are MEMBERS of the two outbound allowlists — deliberately, because a child needs them as plumbing — and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 pinning that collect_tokens keeps only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. So the two allowlists the rationale points at as the pattern to reuse admit precisely the names Hermes forbids on write; the inbound registry has to be its own list, and "run overrides through the same name policy" is not by itself a fix, since that policy passes PATH/NODE_PATH/PYTHONPATH untouched. Confirmed there is still no env writer to gate: no os.environ assignment in agents/ except the reality harness's JARVIS_STRICT_EGRESS toggle (agents/core/observability/reality_harness.py:685,714; scripts/qa_audit_probes.py and scripts/install_smoke.py set os.environ only as probe/smoke harnesses); no set_key/dotenv write; agents/core/paths.py:133-137 only copies .env.example verbatim; GET /api/admin/env (agents/core/routers/admin.py:379-391) is read-only and mask-redacted, and its one sibling, GET /api/admin/env/sources (H273), is read-only and returns key names and layers only, so neither writes the environment; the HUD states it in its own copy (frontend/src/panels/workflows-advanced.tsx:48 "There is NO route to change either"). Nerva's actual config writer is settings_db.put_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:845-880), which UPSERTs only DEFAULTS-declared keys and skips the rest (agents/core/settings_db.py:861-871), behind validate_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:791-817) and the 422 at agents/core/routers/admin.py:167-173 — the right shape, but over settings keys, not env names. Three things are nevertheless still owed, so this is not equivalence. (1) The row's own deliverable — a declared-names allowlist at the write boundary, depends_on "the key registry" — is unbuilt, and the rationale defers rather than excludes it ("the moment the config writer lands, this must land with it"). (2) The MCP env boundary is unrefused: MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:131-142) has no env field and sets no model_config, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" SILENTLY DROPS an `env` body key rather than refusing it — reproduced at HEAD both on the model (model_config {} and env absent from model_dump) and end to end through TestClient: POST /api/admin/mcp with {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}} → 200 {"ok": true}, the stored MCPServer.env is {} and to_config() carries no env — and POST builds the MCPServer without one (:212-224). The non-round-trip half IS now pinned — test_per_server_env_has_no_owner_reachable_config_surface (tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522, from #1174) asserts "env" not in MCPServerConfig.model_fields, to_config (agents/core/mcp/client.py:798-812) exports no env and load_from_config (:814-849) ignores one — but no test asserts the route REFUSES an env body, and the field it would fill is live: MCPServer.env (:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Reachability today: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449; no add form, nothing sends env) and no CLI or script adds servers, so the raw API is the only path. (3) Per-server overrides still bypass the allowlist in both branches: stdio_env_baseline applies them unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring agents/core/mcp/client.py:253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch — reachable only under JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 since H502 — does merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env) unfiltered (:575-576). Latent, not live: the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names set on the host (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56), and the admin route cannot pass one. Also checked and cleared: scripts/nerva_import.py IS a setup-flow writer that persists foreign env-var names verbatim (docstring scripts/nerva_import.py:31-32, .env lines scripts/nerva_import.py:357-358, JSON walk scripts/nerva_import.py:371, settings.json env block scripts/nerva_import.py:389-393, SecretStore write scripts/nerva_import.py:1022), but _SECRET_NAME_RE (scripts/nerva_import.py:85) is applied on every path and admits only credential-shaped names — tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 is the one existing test that exercises a hijack-shaped name (EDITOR) at an import boundary and pins it dropped — and SecretStore (agents/core/secrets.py) never exports a name to a process env (it reads only JARVIS_SECRET_KEY, :111). HEQ lot 1 moved two cited files without touching this row's subject: settings_db.py gained the H583 openrouter_* llm rows and a slug check inside _validate_value (settings keys, not env names; put_category and validate_category are unchanged), and scripts/nerva_import.py gained H344's skill.install mediation and --update re-import for skills, while its token path (the .env/JSON/settings.json readers and _SECRET_NAME_RE) is unchanged. Tests re-run on the lot-1 head: 55 passed, 0 failed across the four cited files (test_environment_primitives 6, test_mcp_transports 33 — two of them #1179's, test_mcp_admin 8, test_settings_integrity 8), and tests/test_nerva_import.py 44 passed, 1 skipped; none exercises an env-var write boundary.
reviews.remaining:
Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. #1179 changed nothing on this row's subject: its client.py change is an outbound disclosure (cwd_secret_files :215-242 and the "withholding is undercut" WARNING in _merged_env :561-572), not a name policy or a writer. Neither did the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1: tool_patterns_over_bounds, a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ and a tools_allow/tools_deny bounds refusal in admin_mcp_add) — it touches no env name, writer or override path and only moved line numbers. H502 (#1174) did change item 3 and half of item 2, and that is folded in here. Three items owed, two shippable today against real surfaces:

1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No ENV_VAR_NAME allowlist/denylist exists anywhere (grep for ENV_VAR_NAME/ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env across agents/, scripts/, tests/, frontend/src/ is empty at HEAD) and no `config.write` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py. Of Hermes' hijack names, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER are named nowhere in code or tests — but PATH, SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) ARE named, as members of the two OUTBOUND allowlists, and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 (pinned dropped at tests/test_nerva_import.py:825). Design consequence: the outbound lists cannot double as the write-side registry — they deliberately admit the plumbing names Hermes forbids on write — so the registry is a separate, inbound-only list. When any env/config writer lands, that allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:139-143 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :151-152.

2. THE MCP `env` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED (shippable now; the "untested" half closed with #1174). MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:131-142) sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes `POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it — reproduced end to end at HEAD through TestClient (200 {"ok": true}; stored MCPServer.env == {}; to_config() has no env key). The field it would populate is live — MCPServer.env (agents/core/mcp/client.py:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Already pinned by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522: `env` is not a MCPServerConfig field, to_config (:798-812) does not export it and load_from_config (:814-849) does not read it. Reachability: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449) and no CLI adds servers, so the raw admin API is the only path today. Still owed: `extra="forbid"` (or an explicit named refusal) on MCPServerConfig, plus a test asserting the route refuses an `env` body rather than swallowing it — and the same refusal must cover the hijack names above on the day `env` becomes operator-settable.

3. PER-SERVER `env` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring :253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does `merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env)` with no filter (:575-576). The "decide whether the baseline should become the default" half of this item is DONE: since H502 the baseline is on unless JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 (:179-190; docs/FLAGS.md "on by default since H502") and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins both directions, so the legacy branch is now the explicit escape hatch rather than the shipped path. Owed: gate per-server overrides on the item-1 write-side registry (NOT merely on STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST + _SECRET_LIKE — that policy passes PATH, SHELL, NODE_PATH and would pass an operator-supplied PATH/NODE_PATH override untouched), or make the bypass an explicitly reviewed, audited exception. Severity, checked directly rather than inferred: LATENT. `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field, the admin route constructs MCPServer without one (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:212-224), and the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56). No untrusted input reaches the override loop, so this is a boundary to close before `env` becomes operator-settable, not a live hole. The outbound allowlist's one intentional exception — a name the owner lists in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — is owner-declared and host-wide, and is not this row's write boundary.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only.

The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:356) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour:
- Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO.
- The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used.
- PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch.
- The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read.
- A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once.
- It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?".
- files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read.

provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:494) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running.

The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:436) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once:
- serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:239). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard.
- The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:457). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed.
- The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:92), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:57): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:456), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:56; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:94; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183).
- agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect.
- PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:80), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry.
- Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off.

Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:480) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment.
- What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:91).
- JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72).
- Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:84): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies.

The lists are measured, not declared:
- A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there.
- A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:666).

The two false read-again entries are fixed:
- The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:286; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:393). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:108): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:136), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits).
- The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:33), which re-reads the client ids after the load.

Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:193): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:134) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too.

derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:318) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:285). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe.

Surfaces:
- GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:394) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included.
- `nerva doctor`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:641):
  - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:371). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://[::1]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:289), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:329). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost., ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:345). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:387). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why.
  - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, *_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's *_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:509).
  - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:747). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:527); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters.
  - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why.
  - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash.
- The `nerva` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:111) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only. Its loopback rule is the doctor's, pinned equal over one table of spellings. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:151), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:632; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4).
- The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:544). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown or unreadable stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection. `nerva config list` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:803).
- The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:254).

Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment.

Known limits:
- On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled.
- A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound.
- In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once.
- JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split.
- The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why.
- A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1).
- A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together.
- A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked.
- A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py.
- Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value.
- A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token.
- The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines).
- The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it.
- Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it.
- The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today.
- JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before.

The hub can boot in safe mode, with every owner customization left out and no gate relaxed. JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1, or `python serve.py --safe-mode`, which sets it before the hub is imported (apply_safe_mode_switch, serve.py:33), is the one flag, read at call time by one module (enabled, agents/core/safe_mode.py:110). It leaves out seven layers (LAYERS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:54). Skills: discovery does not open the data home's skills folder (agents/core/skills/loader.py:641), and any skill in the bundled tree that is not a shipped one (generated, imported, edited or pending review, by the loader's own external classification) is not loaded (agents/core/skills/loader.py:709); every shipped skill still is. MCP: the saved servers are not registered (agents/web.py:1807) and their saved configuration is not touched: _save_mcp_config never rewrites it from the empty manager (agents/web.py:1778), and adding or removing a server answers 409 `safe_mode` before anything changes (_safe_mode_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:160). Acquired packages and extensions: the acquisition runtime reports itself disabled (agents/core/acquisition/runtime.py:39), so nothing promoted is re-registered and extensions() returns None, which the activate route answers as unavailable. Plugin grants: JARVIS_PLUGIN_GRANTS, which only ever widens access under least privilege, is ignored (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:613). Persona and contract overlays: soul_path_for (agents/core/agent.py:389) and identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolve through _pick_overlay (agents/core/agent.py:375), which in safe mode returns the shipped SOUL.md or IDENTITY.md and never a SOUL.local.md or IDENTITY.local.md from the data home or the repository; construction and the H672 compaction-boundary refresh both resolve through it, so a safe-mode session cannot pick an overlay up mid-conversation. Heartbeat: a HEARTBEAT.local.md is passed over for the shipped HEARTBEAT.md (agents/core/heartbeat.py:219). Owner jobs stay saved and are not put on the scheduler (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:64). What was left out is recorded by layer (note, agents/core/safe_mode.py:115; status, agents/core/safe_mode.py:202), logged once per layer and at boot (agents/web.py:479), and said on /healthz as a boolean (agents/core/routers/ops.py:56), on /readyz, whose readiness is unaffected (agents/core/routers/ops.py:142), on /status (agents/core/routers/status.py:109) and /api/status (agents/core/routers/status.py:119). The HUD reads it from /status (frontend/src/api/loaders.ts) and shows a red SAFE MODE strip that names the layers left out and cannot be dismissed (SafeModeBanner, frontend/src/safe-mode-banner.tsx). Safe mode only removes: the kernel, the security, secrets and approval modules, the tool profiles, the capability actions and the egress policy do not read it, and a test pins the exact list of modules that do.
