reviews.summary: The tool loop now ends with eight named fixed replies instead of three: _APPROVAL_REPLY, _DEADLINE_REPLY and _CONTEXT_REPLY (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:76-78), _TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:81), _WINDOW_REPLY and _REPEAT_REPLY (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:82-83), _FAILURE_REPLY (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:101), and the safety-limit string returned after a tool_loop_exhausted event (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:729-737). H672 added _TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY for an offer that comes back empty when it is re-resolved at a compaction boundary (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:602). The loop's typed events land in the bounded ToolEventLog ring (agents/core/observability/tool_events.py). They are tool_loop_repeated, tool_loop_failing, tool_cap_reached, tool_loop_exhausted, and, since H672, tool_offer_refreshed and tool_loop_withdrawn (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:574, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:597). The ring is readable through GET /api/admin/tool-events (agents/core/routers/admin.py:460-461) and `nerva tools` (agents/cli/nerva.py:880). The orchestrator names a per-agent timeout (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4030, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4032) and replaces an empty answer with a fixed cut-short message (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2469). The exit reason still exists only as prose. AgentToolRuntime.run returns a bare str (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:345), and there is no typed exit-reason enum. No diagnostic line logs why the loop ended, or that it stopped with a pending tool result. The SSE end event carries only text, pending_approvals, H677's warming flag and H674's notices (agents/web.py:1356), no exit reason. No file-mutation verifier footer, per-turn accounting line or live token-flow display exists.
reviews.remaining: (1) A typed turn exit-reason vocabulary (completed, approval_required, deadline, context_budget, tools_withdrawn, window_invalid, repeated_call, failing_tool, iteration_limit, no_tools, no_capability, agent_timeout), returned with the reply from AgentToolRuntime.run and carried to ChatResponse and the SSE end event. (2) One diagnostic log line per turn naming the reason: INFO normally, WARNING when the loop stopped with a tool result the model never answered. (3) A consolidated user-facing completion explainer that the HUD renders from that reason, replacing the fixed strings. (4) The file-mutation footer: file_write/file_delete calls that failed this turn and were never superseded by a later success on the same path, appended to the reply so the model cannot claim every file was edited. (5) A per-turn accounting line (tool calls, failures, tokens) and cumulative output tokens shown in the HUD.

reviews.summary: Runtime-ul oprește apelurile identice și seriile de eșecuri, aplică limite per unealtă și înlocuiește rezultatele identice reușite cu referințe.
Pe Python 3.12, rezultatele externe sunt delimitate ca date; taintul și semnalele de injecție sunt propagate inclusiv prin orchestrator și păstrate la compactare.

The supporting pieces exist, but the feature does not. Signed inbound webhooks exist: compute_signature is HMAC-SHA256 (agents/core/webhooks.py:107), and WebhookStore.verify_signature compares it in constant time (agents/core/webhooks.py:667), verified by tests/test_h16_4_signed_triggers.py. A lifecycle event catalogue now exists too: ExtensionEventBus builds allowlisted payloads from FIELDS for command.completed, session.started, session.ended and tool.completed (agents/core/extensions/events.py:51-56, agents/core/extensions/manifest.py:16). The orchestrator, the command runner and the tool-event log emit those events. Their only subscribers, however, are signed and consented extensions that run in a container with --network none (agents/core/extensions/runtime.py:32). Outbound HTTP goes only to chat channels (agents/core/channels/webhook_channels.py). There is no outbound lifecycle webhook: no registry of external subscriber URLs, no signed JSON POST of lifecycle events, no bounded retry or redirect policy, no estop or budget silencing of the feed, and no redaction hop on its payloads.
reviews.remaining: The whole accepted delivery path is missing: (1) an admin-managed registry of outbound subscribers (URL, secret, event filter) with an operator entry point (admin route plus a `nerva` CLI verb or HUD control). (2) A delivery worker subscribed to the same event catalogue as ExtensionEventBus that POSTs the allowlisted JSON payload with an HMAC signature header from compute_signature. (3) Bounded retries with backoff and an explicit no-follow redirect policy. (4) Egress through the plugin.egress kernel mediation (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:45) and an estop check, so a kill-switch or budget stop silences the feed. (5) Payloads passed through the redaction engine before they leave the box. The reaction/vibe detector is excluded by the rationale.

reviews.summary: Log redaction now covers every handler in the main process. setup_logging() (agents/core/log.py:92) calls _install_redaction() (agents/core/log.py:106), which runs install_log_redaction_everywhere() (agents/core/security/log_redaction.py:528). That attaches SecretRedactionFilter (agents/core/security/log_redaction.py:230) to the root handlers and to every handler owned by any logger in logging.Logger.manager, including uvicorn and uvicorn.access, which set propagate=False. The filter masks msg, args, exc_text and stack_info with SecretScanner and keeps record arity for uvicorn's AccessFormatter. It fails closed to [redaction-unavailable], and handlers that refused the filter are counted and reported. The enable flag is snapshotted at import (agents/core/security/log_redaction.py:140), so an agent-authored mid-session env write cannot switch it off. JARVIS_SCANNER_EXTRA_PATTERNS extends the pattern set. setup_logging() runs from agents/run.py at import and from the FastAPI lifespan in agents/web.py. tests/test_log_redaction.py and tests/test_log_redaction_collection_leak.py pass (66 tests). The module docstring itself acknowledges the uncovered processes and the missing PII pass (agents/core/security/log_redaction.py:24-27).
reviews.remaining: (1) Two process entry points configure logging with a bare logging.basicConfig and never install the filter, so every record they write is unredacted: the headless coordinator (scripts/coordinator.py:132), which boots the full Orchestrator with channels, heartbeat, the autonomy loop and the scheduler, and the MCP stdio bridge (scripts/nerva_mcp_stdio.py:151). (2) There is no sensitive query-parameter, header or body-key catalogue for opaque tokens that match no vendor prefix. Probed through SecretRedactionFilter.redact_text, all of these pass unmasked: 'GET /cb?access_token=abcdef1234567890', an unquoted '?api_key=abcd1234efgh5678', 'client_secret=Zx81kdfLq0PaW3', 'X-Api-Key: 9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2e' and 'Authorization: Token abcd1234efgh5678ijkl'. The cause: generic_api_key requires a quoted value (agents/core/security/scanner.py:190) and only password keys match unquoted (agents/core/security/scanner.py:178). (3) The checksum-validated Romanian patterns the rationale relies on, ro_cnp and ro_iban (agents/core/security/scanner.py:287-288), belong to PIIScanner, which the log filter does not run, so a CNP or IBAN reaches the log verbatim.

reviews.summary: A session is named from its first message, the way Hermes names one, in two stages. agents/core/session_titles.py holds the rules. instant_title (agents/core/session_titles.py:75) takes the first user message, normalises it (NFKC; control, format, private-use and unassigned characters dropped; one line with spaces collapsed) and cuts it at a word boundary to 60 characters with an ellipsis. A slash command or blank text is not a title, so the next real message names the session. The orchestrator calls _title_session (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2728) right after the user turn is stored, on both chat paths (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1897, agents/core/orchestrator.py:2085). It does nothing when the owner's switch memory.session_titles is off (agents/core/settings_db.py:226, on by default) or the session already has a title. Otherwise it writes the first-words title at once and queues one upgrade. handle_input and handle_input_stream start the queued upgrade only after the turn's reply is final (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1878, agents/core/orchestrator.py:2067), as Hermes titles after the first response, so the title call never competes with the answer for the local model. The upgrade (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2774) goes through model_title (agents/core/session_titles.py:113), which hands the message (bounded to 2,000 characters) to the model as a JSON string under a system prompt that says to name the conversation, not answer it or follow it. clean_model_title (agents/core/session_titles.py:83) accepts exactly one line of 1 to 10 words and at most 60 characters. It strips a Title:/Titlu: label, quotes and trailing punctuation, and rejects URLs and instruction- or refusal-shaped text; anything else keeps the first-words title. The call is strict-local (_session_titler, agents/core/orchestrator.py:2785): it uses LLMRouter.local_backend only, never a cloud backend, at temperature 0 and 24 tokens, with /no_think for Qwen3. It refuses under a job model pin. With no local backend there is simply no upgrade. The title lives in the session row's metadata as title and title_source (first_words or model). CheckpointManager.set_session_title (agents/core/checkpoint.py:266) is a compare-and-set: it creates a missing row, keeps the row's other metadata, and writes only when there is no title or the current one's source is in replace. The model's name therefore replaces only a first-words title, never a newer one, and never a legacy title with no source. session_title (agents/core/checkpoint.py:250) reads it, with unreadable metadata counting as no title. title_fields (agents/core/session_titles.py:101) gives every list the same view. GET /sessions returns title and title_source on each row (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:35). The /sessions command prints the title after the id and start time (agents/core/commands.py:218). The HUD SESSIONS card shows the title, with the id's first 8 characters and the full id on hover (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:84). The mobile resume list prefers the title over the summary and the id (mobile/src/components/SessionsModal.tsx:80). tests/test_h413_session_titles.py (86 cases) covers the first-words cut and cleaning, the model-answer filter (8 accepted, 20 rejected shapes), the JSON hand-over, the input bound and the failure paths. It also covers the compare-and-set store (missing row, kept metadata, no overwrite, legacy title, unreadable metadata, a closed or failing store), and the orchestrator hook (switch, titled session, slash command, no titler, unusable answer, lost write, newer title, no loop, and deferral inside a turn). The strict-local titler cases are temperature, tokens, default model, Qwen3, the job pin, no router, and a real HybridRouter with only a cloud backend. Two real golden turns (plain and stream) show that the turn's own call runs alone, the title arrives after it, and the second turn is not re-titled. The route, the /sessions command and the settings row are covered as well. frontend/src/test/sessions-title.test.tsx covers the HUD card. There are 67 mutants: 65 killed and 2 equivalent (the no-connection guard, which the except already covers; a source compare that no caller can tell apart).

IterationBudget (agents/core/iteration_budget.py) is still only a counter. AgentToolRuntime._run_loop consumes one unit per model turn (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:529). On exhaustion it emits tool_loop_exhausted and returns a fixed safety-limit string (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:729-737). Since the audit, Hermes absorption 5c has coordinated two of the scattered clocks. orchestrator._agent_call_timeout (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3454) picks a flat or reasoning ceiling per agent and hands it to the agent as wall_seconds (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4004). run() then clamps it into the tool-loop deadline (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:392-396), which tests/test_reasoning_timeout.py pins. There is still no single bounded-execution primitive or timeout resolver. The tool-call timeout (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1275), the sandbox file-RPC deadline (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:318), the per-attempt retry timeout (agents/core/resilience.py:28) and the per-plugin deadline (agents/core/plugin_gatherer.py:151) are each site-local. There is no 80%-spent wrap-up nudge and no iteration-budget exhaustion protocol.
reviews.remaining: (1) One deadline/budget primitive that extends iteration_budget.py, as the 2026-08-28 delta doc chose: a wall-clock deadline plus an iteration count, remaining and fraction-spent readings, and a timeout resolver per call kind. The orchestrator turn, the tool loop, tool calls, ToolRPC and plugin gathering derive their timeouts from it instead of their own constants. (2) An 80%-spent wrap-up nudge, injected once into the tool-loop transcript, asking the model to deliver from what it has. (3) The exhaustion protocol: tell the model exactly once, grant one final tool-less call, and force a summary from the transcript if that call yields no text, instead of returning the fixed safety-limit string. (4) Deadline and budget stops reported through the H396 exit-reason vocabulary.

reviews.remaining: Rămân timeline/as-of, paritatea exploratorului și controalele de memorie cerute de rând; o listă de vecini nu închide harta semantică.

reviews.summary:
The per-item cascade algorithm exists. DecayMemory.forget() (agents/core/memory/decay.py:112) walks _dependents() (:109) and removes the item plus its transitive dependents. It is exposed as POST /api/memory/decay/forget (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:575), which two HUD controls call: KgPanel's forget box (frontend/src/gap.tsx:201) and MemoryHygienePanel's per-row ✕ (frontend/src/gap.tsx:303).

The whole-store forget is governed. POST /api/admin/forget (agents/core/routers/backup.py:99) is admin-guarded and requires {"confirm":"FORGET"} (:115). It checks the data.purge contract, backs up first by default and reports not_erased when something survived.

The accepted adaptation for the per-item path is not built. The route crosses only user_guard and calls d.forget directly (memory_kg.py:589). There is no memory.forget kind in ACTION_REGISTRY; agents/core/kernel/registry.py:73 still lists /decay/forget as out of kernel scope. There is also no cascade preview, no approval card and no audit row: one click deletes irreversibly.

The cascade also retracts less than its name says. The ids it deletes are the decay tracker's activation entries: LivingMemory turn ids registered at agents/core/orchestrator.py:3394, and ambient situation ids. The route never calls LivingMemory.forget() (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:194) or any vector/KG delete. The LivingMemory record with the same id survives a per-item forget.
reviews.remaining: Add a memory.forget kind at the irreversible tier. POST /api/memory/decay/forget must return the transitive dependent list as a preview and queue an approval card carrying that list instead of deleting on the spot. The cascade runs only from the approved task and writes an audit row with the removed ids. KgPanel and MemoryHygienePanel show the preview and the pending state. The executed cascade must also retract the records the ids name (at least LivingMemory.forget for turn ids), not only the decay tracker's activation entries.

reviews.summary: Compaction now checkpoints the turns it is about to discard, and fails closed when a required checkpoint does not land. ContextCompressor takes a checkpoint callable (agents/core/context_compressor.py:321). compress() awaits it with exactly the turns the summary replaces (the evicted middle, all of it even when a prior summary covers part) and the whole transcript, before the summary is built (agents/core/context_compressor.py:574-581). The orchestrator builds that callable in _precompress_checkpoint (agents/core/orchestrator.py:362) and hands it to the compressor on every compacting history build (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3740). It calls precompress.run_checkpoint (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:95) over the registered providers, or the default transcript archive. The hook is versioned. A provider declares checkpoint_api_version, and only one at CHECKPOINT_API_VERSION 2 or above counts (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:58). The optional keyword arguments (evidence_messages, require_checkpoint, checkpoint_api_version, session_id) are passed only when the provider's signature accepts them (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:64). A synchronous provider runs off the event loop, and providers get copies, so they cannot change the transcript. The shipped provider, TranscriptArchive (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:159), appends each evicted turn once, by a hash of speaker, time and content, to a per-session JSONL file whose name is a hash of the session. The file lives under the data folder (compaction_archive), and the append is flushed and fsynced before on_pre_compress returns (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:191). It remembers what it holds across restarts, skips damaged lines, writes images as [image], and can read a session back. memory.compression_checkpoint_required (agents/core/settings_db.py:233, off by default; only a literal true turns it on) makes it fail closed. A failing checkpoint provider, or no checkpoint provider landing ("No active memory provider completed pre-compress checkpoint API v2"), raises CheckpointAborted. The compressor then returns the transcript exactly as it came in: no summary, images kept, no lineage row (agents/core/context_compressor.py:509-516). A turn whose uncompressed prompt would not fit the model's window is refused with the compaction refusal reply (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3784). With the setting off, a failing provider is logged and compaction proceeds. Every checkpoint writes memory.precompress_checkpoint to the signed intent log, and every abort writes memory.precompress_abort, with turn counts, provider names and the reason, never the turns. tests/test_h427_precompress_checkpoint.py (44 cases) covers the contract (version, names, signature sniffing, copies, a synchronous provider, nothing to evict), the not-required and required paths (failing provider, old provider, no provider, a missing or non-callable hook, a failing audit), and the archive (write once, fsync, restart, damaged lines, hashed names, images and structured content, turn identity, default location). It also covers the compressor (exactly the evicted turns before the summary, a prior summary, abort, under budget, compact fail-closed) and the orchestrator (archived and audited, required failure keeps the transcript with no clock commit, not required proceeds, no provider, refusal exactly at the window, a literal-true switch, the default archive, the settings row, no turn text in the audit). There are 51 mutants: 49 killed and 2 equivalent (a non-callable hook fails with the same TypeError either way; re-reading the archive file each time is only slower).

reviews.summary:
Continuation lineage exists in an explicit form. POST /sessions/continue (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:165, admin-guarded) is called by `nerva sessions continue` (agents/cli/nerva.py:1490) and runs ContinuationStore.create (agents/core/session_continuation.py:184, via create_continuation :344). create inserts a new sessions row and a session_continuations row carrying parent_id, root_id and a hashed immutable seed (:43-45), after verifying the ancestry chain. tests/test_session_continuation.py covers this with 50 passing tests.

Sessions are named by H413 but not by lineage:
- H413 gives each session a first-words title and one strict-local model upgrade, kept in the row's metadata with its source (first_words or model). The write is a compare-and-set (agents/core/checkpoint.py:266) that never replaces a newer title or one of unknown source. The model answer is filtered text, not a {"title"} JSON schema, and there is no human-set title or rename route.
- Continuations get no `base #N` titles and are not hidden from pickers: GET /sessions (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:26, :35) returns every row from get_sessions (checkpoint.py:470) with its title added.
- Nothing resolves a name to the newest member of a lineage.
The HUD SessionsPanel shows the title (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:84) and the mobile SessionsModal prefers it (mobile/src/components/SessionsModal.tsx:80); a continuation there reads as its own session.
reviews.remaining:
The two-stage automatic title exists (H413). Still needed:
- a {"title": string} JSON schema on the model call, if the backend supports one (H413 filters free text)
- a human-set title (rename route) that the model upgrade never overwrites
- `base #2`, `base #3` titles for continuations
- continuations hidden from GET /sessions, the HUD SessionsPanel and the mobile SessionsModal
- resume by title resolving to the newest lineage member

reviews.summary: Getting back into a conversation now comes with a free recap, rendered locally from the stored turns and never by a model, on resume, as /recap in every channel and in the HUD. render_recap (agents/core/memory/recap.py:76) groups a session's turns into exchanges (an owner turn and the replies that follow it), keeps the last 10 by default (DEFAULT_EXCHANGES, agents/core/memory/recap.py:24; at most 50, MAX_EXCHANGES, agents/core/memory/recap.py:25), and puts each turn on one line of plain text, whitespace folded, control and bidi characters removed and cut to 280 characters with an ellipsis (_clean, agents/core/memory/recap.py:35). A reply's tools collapse to a count and their distinct names, "[3 tool calls: web_search, web_fetch]" (tool_line, agents/core/memory/recap.py:53), names only, never arguments or results, and an owner turn never shows one. The answer carries the exchanges as data and the same recap as text lines (● you / ◆ the agent) with "the last n of m exchanges" when some are left out. The tools had to be recorded first: turns persisted only role, content, agent, time and tokens. The orchestrator opens a per-turn collection when an owner turn arrives (turn_tools.begin, agents/core/memory/turn_tools.py:23; agents/core/orchestrator.py:1898 and :2086), the agent's tool-event sink notes each finished call's tool (turn_tools.note, agents/core/memory/turn_tools.py:30, from the sink's record, agents/core/agent.py:895) while still landing every event in the trail, and the reply that closes the turn is stored with the names (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3417) on Turn.tools (Turn, agents/core/memory/conversation.py:36; a stored value that is not a list of names reads as none, _tool_names, agents/core/memory/conversation.py:62), persisted, reloaded at start and on resume, and absent from a turn that called none. The collection is a context variable, so concurrent turns in other sessions never mix, and a tool loop run through asyncio.to_thread still lands in its own turn. POST /sessions/resume answers with "recap" beside the last 20 raw turns it always returned (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:149), rendered from the whole stored session. /recap [n] (_recap, agents/core/commands.py:372; registered at agents/core/commands.py:397) answers in any admitted channel, from that channel's own session (a chat's session is its own, pinned by the channel handler), with n exchanges (at most 50; anything else is the default ten), and leaves out its own /recap line. The HUD's Sessions panel (SessionsPanel, frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:46) now shows the recap after a resume (RecapView, frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:25; toolLine, frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:18) as text, never markup, names a refused resume and drops the old recap then, and says "resumed <id>" when a hub sends none. tests/test_h441_session_recap.py (16 cases) covers the renderer (last exchanges and the count, tool lines, one bounded line, odd input, no model), the collection (terminal events only, names only, concurrent turns and a worker thread, no turn open, a caller's copy), the agent's sink, the turn's tools stored and reloaded at start and on resume, the manager passing them down, the resume route's recap with no model call, /recap in a guest's channel with a count, with nothing and with no memory, /help listing it, and the orchestrator storing a turn's tools; frontend/src/test/sessions-recap.test.tsx (3) covers the panel. 28 mutants (24 Python, 4 HUD), all caught, three after their cases were added (an owner turn with tools, a caller's copy of the list, the reload on resume). Test manual: CHT-118 (and CHT-011 names the recap). Adapted from Hermes: no per-terminal breadcrumbs for -c/--continue (they solve a multi-pane CLI problem Nerva does not have), and the recap is served to the HUD and the chat channels rather than drawn as a terminal panel.

file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). local_docs and agents/core/ingestion/ remain the bulk-ingestion path into memory.
reviews.remaining: The part this row says is worth copying is missing. A scanned (image-only) PDF extracts to empty or near-empty text, and file_read returns that as a normal successful read, with no coverage warning naming the page ranges that yielded no text. No size ceiling applies to a document: the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned, where Hermes refuses documents over 50 MB. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. The wider format matrix (.ipynb, .xlsx, legacy Office, OpenDocument, .rtf, .epub) and Markdown conversion are not built; the row's rationale does not ask for them.

reviews.summary: JobStore/HUD/CLI au creare și editare pentru cele patru acțiuni, constructor vizual de program, 16 blueprint-uri cu formulare tipizate, repeat limitat atomic și livrare per job către canale deja configurate sau doar istoric. Există doctor, incidents (pauze după eșecuri), notepad editabil, status/remove și tick idempotent în fusul scheduler-ului, refuzat când scheduler-ul rulează. Gate-urile task/quiet hours/buget/e-stop sunt păstrate; flush-ul mesajelor amânate verifică acum e-stop. Accesul Automations din bara principală deschide un spațiu dedicat; dialogul nativ de creare gestionează focusul, Tab, Escape și revenirea la buton. Tipurile OpenAPI includ cele patru rute noi. Review: update scrie doar câmpurile cerute și nu poate reseta rezervările atomice; istoricul păstrează textul efectiv pentru brief/remind fără livrare. Scripturile Python locale au acum snapshot de sursă legat de aprobarea fiecărei execuții, rezultate pending persistente și livrare directă no_agent sau context izolat ca date neîncrezătoare. API/CLI disting acceptarea de finalizare; conținutul gol nu apelează modelul. Manual run now persists a bounded receipt and returns HTTP 202; scheduler/offline tick executes through the shared job firing path. Atomic coalescing and portable cross-process locks prevent duplicate execution. Configuration snapshots, pending-script reconciliation, crash-unknown state without replay, and concurrent retention are tested. HUD and CLI restore accepted request status and distinguish queued, waiting and completed execution. Ask jobs now persist effective request-local model/provider pins through CLI/HUD options, with preflight routing, closed lifetimes, approved-model enforcement and resolved context budgets. Unavailable pins fail explicitly; ordinary chat configuration is unchanged. Independent review repaired file_read re-spilling under a pinned window. Owner-authored reminder media IDs now produce actual bounded Telegram file/text delivery with frozen content/recipient bindings, a validated total deadline and durable held/partial/unknown outcomes. CLI/HUD authoring and status expose these outcomes; editing an explicit empty options document clears prior settings correctly. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported. Model-bearing ask jobs now accept enabled_toolsets through CLI and HUD using an explicit installed basic/files/terminal catalog. Missing/null retains defaults; [] disables tool offers. Immutable per-run name sets intersect both runtime/profile offers and ToolRPC intake before preflight, handlers or approval enqueue. Nested scopes only narrow and inherit revocation; ordinary callers and concurrent jobs retain isolated defaults. Unknown/unavailable groups refuse. Existing approvals retain frozen concrete arguments and do not reread job options or revive a request scope. Doctor reports the configured tool-name upper bound, not effective contextual offers. Actual runner/Agent/RPC, queued-edit/restart, cancellation, UI and concurrency tests are evidence; tool selection grants no new authority.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc contextul izolat per job pentru model workdir și skills, agregarea între profile și noul grant schedule.create cerut de original (rădăcină protejată în afara scopului). Opțiunile fără runtime sunt refuzate, nu salvate inert. Nu există probă live pentru scheduler/canale sau autorare nativă mobilă; monitoarele depind de sursele configurate, nu instalează integrări. Cloud pins must match existing policy routing; changed local models require loaded context metadata, and LM Studio currently cannot resolve a changed model. Pinned jobs use deterministic compression and omit auxiliary embedding recall. The initial catalog intentionally excludes dedicated code-runner, delegation and dynamic plugin groups; their transitive restriction contracts remain unimplemented.

reviews.summary: Plain-words scheduling now covers the four families Hermes accepts that the job store did not. It also no longer turns a one-shot said in words into a daily job. (1) One-shots. nl_schedule.parse_schedule (agents/core/autonomy/nl_schedule.py:196) takes a now and a zone and answers a one-shot as {ok, at (UTC ISO), description} (_parse_one_shot, :120). It accepts a delay: in 30m, in 1h30m, in 2 hours and 5 minutes, in an hour, peste 2 ore, în 10 minute, peste 2 zile (_duration, :85). It accepts an ISO timestamp (2026-10-01 09:00, anchored to the zone, or with Z / ±HH:MM kept). And it accepts a day word with a time (tomorrow at 9, mâine la 9, today at 18:00, azi la 18, once at 9am, o dată la 9, the next 9 o'clock). A one-shot must be at least one minute ahead and within a year (MAX_ONE_SHOT_AHEAD, :29, _one_shot, :101); a passed time, a date without a time, an impossible date, a bad time, and a delay with anything else after it ("in 2 hours at 9") are refused by name. So 2026-10-01 09:00, tomorrow at 9 and once at 9am are no longer armed as the daily cron 0 9 * * *; a bare time with no day word still means daily, as documented. resolve_schedule (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:271) stores a one-shot in the cron column as @at <UTC ISO> (ONE_SHOT_PREFIX, :229; is_one_shot, run_at, :233-238). The store anchors times said in words to the scheduler's zone, which the runner binds (_schedule_zone, :987; :1123). schedule_trigger (:249) gives a DateTrigger for it. register arms a date job (:1170). tick fires it in the minute it falls in (:1264). slot_timing gives its one slot and none after (:1329). A one-shot runs once. Job.runnable is false after one attempt (:131). reserve_attempt refuses a second (:1001). _fire_once reserves the one run before any executor, script jobs included, and records a later firing as skipped: "one-shot already ran" (:1477). register_all does not re-arm a spent one-shot. Giving it a new time re-arms it (_reset_attempts, :978), and a rename does not. It stays out of H687's first run even when first_run is asked for (first_run_policy and first_run_decision answer "one-shot", :563, :589), so it never spends its only run early. The confirmation names its time (arm_confirmation, :606), and as_dict carries one_shot and run_at (:157). /remind in 30m | … works, and its usage says so. (2) Compact intervals and bare durations: every 2h, every 30m, 2h, 30m, la fiecare 2 ore (_COMPACT, _interval, nl_schedule.py:174-177). 120 minutes becomes every 2 hours. An interval a cron cannot keep (every 45 minutes fired at :00 and :45; 7h, 48h) is refused with the divisors to use. (3) Repeat normaliser: normalize_repeat (jobs.py:410) maps forever/unlimited/always/∞/mereu/la nesfârșit to unlimited, once/1x/x1/o dată to 1, twice/de două ori to 2, and Nx/N times/de N ori/N to N (1-10000). Anything else is refused. validate_options applies it, so options.repeat takes the words on every surface. (4) The HUD jobs panel shows a one-shot by its time (once at …, the viewer's clock) instead of @at, and shows a spent one as done (onceAt, frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:29, :61). Tests: tests/test_h450_schedule_words.py (fixed now and Europe/Bucharest zone; store and runner with a fake scheduler; the fallback ticker; script jobs), frontend jobs.test.tsx and jobs-first-run.test.ts. 62 mutants, all caught after fourteen cases were added. One survivor was a real bug: "in 2 hours at 9" read as a daily 9 o'clock; it is now refused.

reviews.summary: Scheduled self-contained Python scripts cross the existing local terminal approval path with exact source in argv. no_agent returns bounded stdout directly; script-as-context fences output and binds an inbound origin before asking the model. Empty/whitespace stdout skips both model and delivery. Pending approval, repeat reservations, deletion/e-stop races, bounded fair reconciliation, interrupted delivery and retained history survive restart in tests. Successful script stdout can suppress model and delivery with a final JSON boolean wakeAgent:false, except when transport output is truncated. Model replies support bounded-position [SILENT] and whole-response silence markers before truncation; suppression is successful history without notification spend. Bounded approved script monitors hash complete raw stdout on the trusted host, compare scrubbed snapshots and atomically persist each baseline before the model runs. Unchanged observations skip model/delivery; source/config generations prevent stale baseline updates and stale delivery. Invalid UTF-8, incomplete or oversized observations leave the baseline intact. URL monitors now use the existing signed enforced task queue for one exact plugin.egress GET per human-approved hop, with fresh approval for redirects. Public-address DNS validation/IP pinning, live post-DNS kernel/e-stop checks, one-use dispatch claims, credential screening and scrub-before-persistence are verified with real queue/worker/executor tests. Only complete final successful UTF-8 identity responses within 256 KiB advance the baseline. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported.
reviews.remaining: Unattended execution is not granted: each script firing and URL hop needs fresh approval, with live enforced signed mediation required for URL authoring. URL scope is credential-free public ASCII HTTP(S), at most five redirects, 30 seconds per hop and 256 KiB uncompressed UTF-8; private, credentialed, compressed or invalid-text observations are unsupported. Script snapshots remain bounded by the terminal cap (at most 50,000 bytes). Monitor mode excludes no_agent and treats wake JSON literally. Model workdir/tool contexts and monitor/URL authoring UI remain unsupported; script-only workdir and script/no_agent UI are implemented. No live production egress, scheduler/channel or full production-kernel proof.

reviews.summary:
H456 re-read against 55d625f. The 2026-09-07 evidence ("no per-item toolset allowlist") is stale, but the row stays partial.

The enabled_toolsets half of the contract is shipped and well built. agents/core/job_toolsets.py holds:
- an immutable CATALOG (:7-11: basic/files/terminal);
- a strict `validate()` that refuses unknown, non-list or duplicate ids (:14-21);
- `resolve()`, which refuses a group whose members are not all registered ('enabled_toolsets contains an unavailable toolset', :30-37);
- `toolset_scope()` (:63-79), whose nested frame is `parent.names.intersection(names)` (:72) with a shared _Lifetime, so a closed parent raises 'job toolset scope expired' (:66-67) instead of falling back to defaults. Intersect-never-union is enforced.

It is enforced at three boundaries, not one:
- the offering boundary (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:226,234 `allowed = allows(name) and _posture_allows(...)`, narrowed again by agents.yaml patterns at :239-240);
- the runtime filter before and after the profile (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:282-291), re-applied at the in-turn compaction boundary by `_resolve_offer` (H672);
- RPC intake, ahead of preflight and handler (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:413-415, reason `job_toolset_not_allowed`).

Store boundary: agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:435 lists the option, :438-442 validates it and refuses it with `no_agent`, validate_action:310-311 refuses it on non-`ask` actions, and create and edit both re-resolve it (:1307, :1375). Fire time: jobs.py:1583-1585 `with toolset_scope(self._toolset_names(job.options)), selection_scope(job.options)`. Doctor reports the catalog, each job's `toolset_upper_bound` and a `toolsets_unavailable` problem (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_health.py:51-55, :113). Reachable from the CLI (`--toolsets default|none|<ids>`, agents/cli/nerva.py:214,224,1326-1332) and the HUD (frontend/src/panels/job-builder.tsx:35-49). PATCH /api/jobs/{id} refuses an unavailable toolset with 422 (tests/test_job_toolsets.py:327-328).

Hermes' two removal rules are met structurally. Every register_tool on the production server was enumerated: agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:480-797 (image_generate, H313's `speak` at :493-509, desktop_run, terminal_run, desktop_plan, operator_plan, osint_enrich, echo, time) and :801-890 (session_search, file_*, web_search/web_extract, search_memory, execute_code), plus H315's `todo`, registered after the tool profile (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:934), which writes only its session's own checklist (on the owner's shared session, only an owner's turn keeps one). None creates a job, and no `schedule.create` kernel capability exists. None is a messaging/clarify tool that needs a live human. The new `speak` announces into a room, but it is registered only with JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR on and is gated (ask-tier card, trusted execution only from an owner-accepted row), so it is never offered off the owner posture.

Verified green at 55d625f: 27 cases in tests/test_job_toolsets.py and 28 in tests/test_job_model_pins.py. The HUD cases in frontend/src/panels/job-toolsets.test.tsx were not re-run in this pass.

What keeps the row open is the contract's second half: a job cannot pin reasoning effort.
- Selection carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25).
- validate_options rejects any unknown option (jobs.py:435), so the pin cannot be stored; neither jobs.py nor job_selection.py mentions reasoning at 55d625f.
- _ask never enters `reasoning_scope`, so every scheduled run inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read in agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:338,351,389,418-419.
- The closed-lifetime transport machinery already exists (agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72), but only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1252, :1315).

Secondary gap: the bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~18 tools the server can register. A job that needs web_search, execute_code or search_memory must run unbounded on the default net, a residual that docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names itself.
reviews.remaining:
(1) The per-job reasoning-effort pin (Hermes' `.cron-reasoning`, rolled into this row) is not implemented:
- `Selection` carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25), and `validate_pins` (:35-43) never sees an effort.
- `validate_options` rejects any option outside the known ten (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:435), so the pin cannot reach the store.
- `JobRunner._ask` (jobs.py:1583-1585) enters `toolset_scope` + `selection_scope` but never `reasoning_scope`. A job therefore always inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read at agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:338, :351, :389, :418-419.

The transport half already exists and is clamped: agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72; agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:81-86 with per-model overrides; agents/core/llm/gemini.py:134; agents/core/llm/xai.py:73; agents/core/llm/provider_request.py:46 and :54. Only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1252, :1315). Work owed:
- accept `reasoning` in validate_pins/validate_options against LADDER;
- enter `reasoning_scope(...)` in `_ask` beside the other two scopes;
- expose it on the CLI/HUD/doctor like the model and provider pins;
- test it in tests/test_job_model_pins.py.

(2) The bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~19 tools the production server can register. CATALOG (agents/core/job_toolsets.py:7-11) covers echo/time, the five file tools and terminal_run. These belong to no group: web_search, web_extract, search_memory, session_search, execute_code, desktop_plan, desktop_run, operator_plan, osint_enrich, image_generate and (with the Media Director on) speak, registered at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:480-797 and :801-890. A job that needs any of them must leave `enabled_toolsets` unset and run on the full default net. H315's todo is not among them: a job runs on the owner's shared session, where only an owner's turn keeps a plan, so no job uses it, with or without a group. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names this residual itself ("does not claim ... arbitrary plugin/delegation/code-runner groups"), and doctor reports the upper bound, not the effective offers.

(3) Minor: Hermes' middle precedence tier has no equivalent. That tier is a per-platform `cron` tools config that sets defaults for every scheduled job. Here, only the per-job list, the internal posture (`llm.internal_actuation`) and the agent's agents.yaml `tools:` patterns narrow an unattended run.

reviews.summary: The pieces around the feature exist, but nothing binds a standing instruction to a conversation. HeartbeatScheduler (agents/core/heartbeat.py:180) schedules per-agent routines from HEARTBEAT.md or agents.yaml, with MIN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL 3600 s (agents/core/heartbeat.py:52) and 15–30 s jitter. Since H506 it also refuses a HEARTBEAT front-matter that its injection scan flags. Admin routes /heartbeat/{agent_id}/start|stop|run (agents/core/routers/heartbeat.py:27) and the HUD HeartbeatPanel drive it. Owner-armed jobs accept plain-words schedules, can be paused, resumed and deleted, and include an `ask` action that sends a prompt to an agent. That prompt goes through a one-shot Orchestrator.process call on channel 'job' (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1591), and the reply goes to the owner's channel, not into the originating chat's history. The only chat slash commands are /help, /status, /sessions, /pause, /stop, /resume, /jobs, /remind and /voice. CommandContext (agents/core/commands.py:50) carries no explicit session id, but its principal is a Principal with channel and chat (agents/core/commands.py:37-46), and ctx.orch.session_id already resolves to the bound channel session because the channel handler sets the active session before handle_input dispatches a command. Turns are serialized per session: Orchestrator.turn_lease (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1638) keeps a per-session asyncio.Lock table with a re-entrant held set. But nothing records an idle boundary or consults that lease before firing a heartbeat. Existing heartbeat and jobs tests pass (tests/test_heartbeat.py, tests/test_heartbeat_actions.py, tests/test_owner_jobs.py).
reviews.remaining:
Every accepted part is missing:
- No `/heartbeat every <interval> <prompt>` entry point, and no pause/resume/clear/status for it.
- No per-session persistence binding a standing prompt to a session_id and originating channel/chat.
- No idle-only firing: turn_lease serializes turns but no heartbeat consults it, and no idle boundary is recorded (row H460's idle-boundary rule, also missing).
- No fire record written before the injected turn runs, so a long turn could double-fire.
- No coalescing of missed ticks with the anchor reset to now.
- No floor specific to this lane.
- No 'any DB failure degrades to no heartbeat' guard.
- No injection of the prompt as a user turn into that conversation's history, where its effects would cross the kernel normally.

reviews.summary: Only the human-wait restraint exists. ScheduleRuntime.due (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:163) returns a skip reason from SKIP_REASONS (schedule_runtime.py:50): terminal, stopping, blocked, budget_spent, not_due or at_capacity. A `blocked` run, one waiting on an owner ask, is not ticked (schedule_runtime.py:170). CompanySupervisor.tick short-circuits on blocked before planning or judging (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:182), so no step is spent. The only deadline on a work run is a budget bound: once passed, the run is exhausted (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:541). It is not a 'wait until' barrier. RUN_STATUSES has no waiting state. Judgement (agents/core/autonomy/work_judge.py:67) is pass/fail only and has no `wait` verdict. No background-process registry exists for a judge to see. Tests tests/test_schedule_runtime.py, tests/test_company_supervisor.py and tests/test_work_run_ledger.py pass and cover the blocked skip and deadline exhaustion.
reviews.remaining:
All three accepted barrier kinds are missing from the work-run ledger and supervisor: wait on a pid until the process exits, wait on a registered session or trigger until it fires, and wait until a wall-clock time. The mechanics around them are also missing:
- No short-circuit in ScheduleRuntime.due or CompanySupervisor.tick while a barrier is active, which would skip without a tick, a plan, a step or a judge call.
- No `wait` verdict or action that a planner or judge can return to set a barrier.
- The judge gets no live background-process list.
- No stale-barrier clearing: a dead pid, a fired trigger or an elapsed deadline should clear the barrier on the next check so it cannot wedge the run.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine [focus] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand.

The command:
- /refine [focus] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:347, registered at agents/core/commands.py:405). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command.
- The focus is one line of at most 200 characters.
- It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list.
- Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed [… error …] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "[Note: … error", or one a later [1] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3).
- A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:513).
- It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does.

Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3270):
- It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it.
- The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path.
- In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long.
- A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3290). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1).
- A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged.

The learning loop's knobs are declared settings (category learning, agents/core/settings_db.py:289): review_max_tokens (512, 1–32768), review_daily_budget (20, 0–1000), review_cadence (every_turn, every_n_turns, idle_gap), review_every_n (3), review_idle_gap_s (90) and review_max_facts (3), with the defaults the code already used, bounded in _LEARNING_INT_BOUNDS (agents/core/settings_db.py:723). The admin settings API, the HUD and nerva config set can change them; nerva config get shows a number named …max_tokens as the number it is, not masked as a credential, and masks every key the settings store encrypts (the GA4 service-account JSON among them), and nerva config set echoes such a value masked too (review-H465e nit 3). A model id is masked only under a hinted name: llm.default_model shows as typed. Every knob reads within its declared bounds whatever the stored row (a row from before the bounds, restored or hand-edited, reads as the default), the review's model call's token cap included (bounded_learning_int, agents/core/settings_db.py:729). A declared 0 for review_max_facts or review_idle_gap_s is honoured, not read as unset; corrections have a cap of their own (3), so a review_max_facts of 0 keeps no facts, still records corrections, and /refine says what it found but did not keep (_number, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:293).

BackgroundReviewer.run_on_demand (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:335):
- It skips the cadence gate but spends the daily budget, rolling over at midnight, and refunds it when no review was had (a model down, a cut-off answer, a timeout, a cancellation), on the day the pass spent it (review-H465f nit 1). A budget of 0 means no reviews and /refine says so (reviews_off); 2.5 reads as 2, and a value that is not a number or lies outside 0–1000 (text, infinity, a boolean, a hand-edited -3, a fraction below one) is logged once and 20 used (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:268). A per-turn pass that does not run leaves a DEBUG line naming why. It keeps the strict-local model, and is bounded at REFINE_TIMEOUT_S (150 s, below the lease's 180-second wait); no setting raises it.
- It neither resets nor delays the per-turn cadence. It runs one at a time and never beside a per-turn review: a /refine while a per-turn pass runs is refused busy, and a per-turn pass that would start while /refine runs is skipped, not deferred. The exclusion is taken in run() itself (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:394), so a per-turn pass spawned before the /refine, still waiting on the memory lock, is refused on_demand when it enters. A cancelled review leaves no busy flag.
- Its proposals, approval cards and new skills are labelled refine, not background_review; the label is passed down per pass, never kept on the instance. An injection-flagged correction is not recorded (on both paths). Facts found while living memory is off are counted after the injection scan, and said only to the owner who asked.
- run gains a focus slot in REVIEW_PROMPT ("Focus for this review: …", absent when there is none, so the per-turn prompt is byte-identical) and a context bound, which this path sets to the snapshot's.

Tests: tests/test_h465_refine.py (35 cases), tests/test_h465c_refine_review.py (9, the second review), tests/test_h465d_refine_review.py (31, the third review), tests/test_h465e_refine_review.py (37, the fourth review), tests/test_h465f_refine_review.py (34, the fifth review), tests/test_h465g_refine_review.py (18, the sixth review), tests/test_nerva_cli.py (a token budget shown unmasked), and tests/test_slash_commands.py pins the command in the owner's list. They cover:
- the focus slot and its bound;
- cadence skipped while the budget is spent, and the day's rollover;
- one review at a time, and facts written;
- the snapshot's bound, order, cutting and junk;
- a whole snapshot reaching the prompt;
- the reviewer receiving this session's snapshot while the session stays unchanged;
- busy while another turn holds the lease, and not busy inside the command's own lease;
- the empty and unavailable cases;
- the owner-only command and its report, each named refusal, and /help;
- the review's cases: a degraded reply is no review and costs no budget; the timeout; a cancelled review; mutual exclusion and the cadence kept; facts found with living memory off; an injected correction; the refine label; commands left out and contiguity; a chat of commands only; a refusal keeping the last result; the focus cut and where a new skill waits; a guest told /refine is the owner's.
