The exact-set pin beside it was tightened, not loosened. **Widened by #1177 (the #1161–#1174 adversarial review) — same mechanism, larger class, re-assessed here.** The roster is now `INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES` (`soul.md`, `agents.md`, `claude.md`, `gemini.md`, `.cursorrules`, `heartbeat.md`) and every `.md` name's gitignored `.local` overlay is *derived* by `_local_overlay` into `INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES` (eleven names) instead of being spelled out by hand — which is what brought `CLAUDE.local.md` / `AGENTS.local.md` / `GEMINI.local.md` into the class; the first cut listed only the SOUL and HEARTBEAT overlays, so a `CLAUDE.local.md` write — same harness, same authority, and it wins over the committed file — asked with the title of a scratch note. `looks_instruction_name` now also matches by extension through `INSTRUCTION_FILE_SUFFIXES = (".mdc",)`, so Cursor's freely-named `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files, the format that superseded `.cursorrules`, are in the class as well. `classify_mutation`, the `steers_future_runs` flag, `_authorize`, the `_mutate` floor and `register_file_tools` are unchanged, and `tool_rpc.py` is byte-identical. Tests: `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_floor.py` (44) pins both sets exactly (the six base names and the eleven derived ones), derives the overlay requirement from the roster in `test_every_name_in_the_roster_brings_its_local_overlay` so a name added later brings its overlay or fails, keeps the heartbeat.py-derived pin, and exercises `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` through `write_file` with the kernel off; `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_class_toolrpc.py` (18) proves the durable card for `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` carries `class=agent_instructions` and the notice in its title, and that nothing reaches disk before approval. **The read half, first piece (2026-09-22), and its review round.** `agents/core/heartbeat.py` — the loader that turns HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md into cron-scheduled runs — refuses a flagged entry at parse time. `scan_heartbeat_config` runs `detect_injection_normalized` over every string in the YAML front-matter, keys and values, nested to a bound of 16, and the walker fails CLOSED: a container at the bound (`nesting-too-deep`, a `&x [*x]` alias cycle included), a `!!binary` value (`unscannable-value-type:bytes` — decoded so the verdict names what it hid, refused regardless) or any type `yaml.safe_load` never produces is a refusal, not a leaf the walker had nothing to say about; `!!set` values are walked; YAML's own scalars (bool, number, null, date) are inert. It decodes and scans a TAG-plane payload so it is named rather than merely deleted, excusing only a run shaped like a subdivision flag emoji (🏴, up to eight TAG letters, CANCEL TAG — England, Scotland, Wales) from the bare-invisible-run flag while still scanning what such runs spell; and it joins UTF-16 surrogate pairs first, because PyYAML decodes a `\uDB40\uDC70` escape into two lone surrogates that no code-point range in `quarantine.py` matches but that a JSON serialiser on the way to a model re-joins into the invisible TAG character (reproduced). One hit refuses the whole entry — a heartbeat is one scheduled job with no 'rest of the persona' to preserve, so the fail-closed answer is not to schedule it: `_parse_heartbeat` never returns a flagged config, and `load_from_config` — which the orchestrator calls right after `load_all` at startup — skips a refused agent instead of writing the agents.yaml interval entry that put it back before `start()`, so nothing reaches `_heartbeat_configs`, `start()`, `start_heartbeat()` or the `POST /heartbeat/{id}/run` path; a flagged overlay does not fall back to the shipped template; a reload starts each directory from a clean slate (no stale verdict, no stale config, in either direction); the refusal is logged with the file's absolute path, its sha256 over the one buffer that was parsed and scanned, and the matched patterns, never the payload; and `get_status()` — what `GET /heartbeat/status`, a deliberately public route, and the runtime run-log read — carries a `blocked` list (agent, file named relative to its root such as `souls/<id>/HEARTBEAT.local.md`, flags, digest) in both of its shapes. Every shipped HEARTBEAT.md loads clean. **`agents/core/security/quarantine.py` changed with it, for both loaders.** The review found that a blank-rendering character put INSTEAD of the space — the Hangul fillers (letters, so they also kill the raw `you are now\b` match), U+2800, a private-use character, or any character already in the table — defeated the SOUL path and the HEARTBEAT path alike: the raw copy had no space to match and the stripped copy had the words glued. `_detection_variants` also scans a copy in which every invisible character becomes a space, the table gains U+2800 and the three private-use planes (Co), and each copy is scanned again over its NFKC fold (fullwidth, ideographic space, ligatures). **An independent review of the first cut — two reviewers, ten distinct findings: two blocking, three major, four minor, one nit — eight fixed here, each red-first and neutered once:** `!!set`/`!!binary` skipped by the walker (blocking); the depth bound fail-open, and the 'at any depth' claim in this row, the BACKLOG bullet, the code comment and the test docstring false (blocking — corrected); blank-instead-of-space (major); `load_from_config` resurrecting a refused agent, and 'a refused entry is never scheduled' overstated for the production load order (major — corrected); the absolute path on the public route, the flag-emoji false refusal and the stale verdict on reload (minor); the two-read digest (nit). `tests/test_instruction_files_read_side_scan.py` (47) pins all of it — including equality with the plain spelling for fourteen blank characters through the detector, the HEARTBEAT loader and the SOUL per-line scan — and pins through `Agent._load_soul` the SOUL spellings the previous version of this row named as unproven ('You are now<U+200B>in developer mode' and 'You are now<U+0007>in developer mode'), which #1179 had already closed in code by routing `_scan_soul_body` through `detect_injection_normalized`.
reviews.remaining: **The read half now covers two of the three Nerva loaders and none of the external ones — the row stays partial.** H506 requires the same file class to be scanned at context-load time with a positive match replaced by `[BLOCKED: … Content not loaded.]`. What holds: SOUL.md / SOUL.local.md through `Agent._scan_soul_body` (H387's evidence, not this row's — per-line quarantine over the union of raw and normalised copies, cross-line wraps, whole-body drop above the ratio; the U+200B and U+0007 spellings after 'now' are pinned in this row's own test file), and HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md through `scan_heartbeat_config`, entry refused rather than line-stubbed. **Precisely what is not covered, stated rather than smoothed over:** the Markdown body after the front-matter is discarded by `_parse_heartbeat` and reaches no model, log or scheduler, so it is not scanned — `test_the_prose_body_is_not_loaded_and_therefore_not_scanned` is the tripwire a loader that starts reading it must flip; no heartbeat text is model input today — the checklist strings are keyword-routed to skills with constant arguments and echoed into a logged run summary — so the scan guards the mapping the loader hands to the agent, not a live prompt path; the keyword scanner is literal after normalisation, so a Cyrillic homoglyph ('Іgnore'), a combining overlay, markdown emphasis inside a phrase ('Ignore _all_ previous') and a phrase split across two checklist items still scan clean — a confusables fold is a separate `quarantine.py` slice, and the homoglyph is pinned as a tripwire in this row's test file; and the SOUL cross-line path (`_wrapped_injection_hits`) builds its own normalised copy inside `agent.py`, so a blank-instead-of-space spelling that ALSO wraps across lines is not covered there (agent.py is untouched here; it is H387's evidence, being re-evaluated by a sibling stream). **Adjacent, pre-existing, NOT fixed:** the orchestrator's `load_from_config` overwrites every shipped HEARTBEAT.md cron+checklist with the agents.yaml interval (all twelve shipped agents carry one), so at runtime `Agent.run_heartbeat` finds no checklist and returns None for the shipped roster — the loader semantics this row describes are what the code does, not what the shipped agents experience (recorded as a separate task); `load_all` keys the config by the front-matter's own `agent` field, so a clean `HEARTBEAT.local.md` in one agent's directory that says `agent: jarvis` replaces Jarvis's schedule (a refused file cannot — the verdict is keyed by directory); and `enabled: false` is parsed and never honoured. Still open on the read side: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / `.cursorrules` / `*.mdc` are read by the external harnesses rather than by Nerva, so 'the same file class on the way in' is not met for them. The write-side deviations stand as before: the row's *"fails closed on a config read error"* clause has no analogue because the roster is a hard-coded frozenset; `allow_session=False` holds only incidentally through the gated toolrpc `autonomy_level="ask"` intake, with nothing pinning it; and the class covers `file_write`/`file_delete` only — the terminal contract, the skill importer and the desktop operator are outside it. Unverified, stated as such: whether the Telegram decision card and the HUD decision inbox render the write-side notice verbatim, and whether any HUD renders the `blocked` list (the API carries it; `frontend/src/gap.tsx` and `agents/web/static/systems.js` read `heartbeats` only). `_mutate`'s floor remains lifted by a caller-supplied `approved=True` by design.

reviews.summary: Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 25 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:59), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or `%`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, crypto.createCipher without an IV, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote `<script>` without integrity=. A separate check (agents/core/code_guidance.py:117) flags `${{ github.event.* }}` inside a GitHub Actions `run:` step, on the run line or in its `|`/`>` block, but not in `if:`, `env:` or `with:`. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: `model.eval()` and `obj.eval()`, `yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)`, `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`, `regex.exec()`, an `===` comparison with innerHTML, `hashlib.md5(data)`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:163) returns `{rule, line, message}`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB. The findings go to three places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1157) adds `code_warnings` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), `code_warning_count` and a title notice; it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. On the write result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:956), the model reads `code_warnings` with a `code_guidance` note that they are warnings, not refusals; a refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:169; install and install-zip answer `code_warnings` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:462) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:595), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:220) walks the folder, skipping symlinks and bounding files and findings; it logs a warning and keeps the list. The owner's switch is `security.code_guidance` (agents/core/settings_db.py:217, on by default; only an explicit off turns it off, and an unreadable store keeps it on). tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (83 cases) covers every rule firing (40 cases), 26 guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. There are 46 mutants: 44 killed and 2 equivalent (skipping non-code files before reading them is only a saving; a reset already done at the start of generation).

Reviewed against live code; the inherited 2026-09-07 "partial" verdict stands, but for a different and much smaller reason than the audit recorded. The audit's "no Host-header validation anywhere" is stale: agents/core/host_policy.py is a 204-line module whose docstring (:4-22) names DNS rebinding explicitly, with normalize_host() at :54, parse_allowed_hosts() at :104 refusing a `*` entry at :119-120 and a leading-dot suffix wildcard at :121-122, host_accepted() at :157-181 matching loopback names, any IP literal, JARVIS_HOST, the ASGI scope's arrival address and JARVIS_ALLOWED_HOSTS, and assert_parseable_allowed_hosts() at :184 refusing boot on an unparseable list. It is wired at agents/web.py:20 (import) and :820-839 (`_host_guard`, returning {"error": "host not allowed", "code": 400}), registered so it runs before the rate limiter and inside the security-header and golden-signal layers (:793-796). Dumping app.user_middleware on the HEQ lot-1 head gives _golden_signals, _security_headers, _host_guard, _rate_limit, _no_store_for_polling, then lot 1's pure-ASGI _ForwardedProtoMiddleware, which only sets the request scheme and runs inside the guard. The boot guard is genuinely reached on the real serve path: agents/core/boot_guards.py:354, inside enforce_boot_posture, which the lifespan calls at agents/web.py:462-463 after the .env files load (agents/web.py:456-457, H273), so a list that lives only in .env is checked too; assert_front_door runs the same check over a caller's own mapping (agents/core/boot_guards.py:320). Refusal logging is rate-shaped (agents/web.py:802-804, agents/web.py:835) and logs only a coarse peer trust class (agents/web.py:807-816), never the attacker-chosen header value. Driven live on the lot-1 head with a loopback TestClient: `Host: evil.test` gets 400 on /status, /dashboard and /api/agents, where the real host gets 200 on /status and /api/agents. The row's other two asks hold, and lot 1 (H691) tightened the proxy half. Trusted-proxy entries are validated as bounded CIDRs at agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107 and :165 (note :308 only WARNS on a wide entry, it does not refuse). uvicorn's own forwarding-header allowlist (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, --forwarded-allow-ips) now refuses boot from the boot pass, which runs after the .env files load, when an entry is a wildcard, a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES and loopback (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570). serve.py switches uvicorn's proxy-header layer off, X-Forwarded-Proto is believed only from a listed peer, and the rate limiter's localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:778), so an unlisted same-box proxy is throttled. CORS is validated with reported rejections at agents/core/cors_policy.py, and no CORS middleware is installed at all by default. The WebSocket clause is excluded by the row itself and the exclusion still holds: no WebSocket server route exists in agents/ (lot 1's _ForwardedProtoMiddleware maps a listed proxy's scheme onto ws/wss scopes but adds no route), agents/web.py:797-798 says a future one must call host_accepted() itself, and agents/web.py:674 is the only ASGI app. 104/104 tests pass across the five relevant suites on the lot-1 head. What keeps this off "equivalent" is the residual the code names about itself at agents/web.py:799-801: _PROBE_PATHS is exempt from the guard (:823-824), so `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz. Re-confirmed live on the lot-1 head: a rebound page therefore still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts — cross-origin, because rebinding makes the browser treat them as same-origin. That is low severity and a deliberate operability trade, not an oversight, but it is a real deviation from Hermes' clause as written (which has no carve-out) and it is shippable work, so the row is partial rather than equivalent.
reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:766, applied at :823-824), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:799-801 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body.

reviews.summary: The tamper-evident sink exists. AuditLogger.log (agents/core/security/audit.py:111) appends to a hash-chained SQLite log checked by verify_chain (agents/core/security/audit.py:209). The admin HUD reads it through GET /api/admin/audit (agents/core/routers/admin.py:492). One credential event is recorded: POST /api/admin/rotate-tokens (agents/core/routers/admin.py:350) writes a best-effort SecurityEventType.AUDIT_LOG row (agents/core/routers/admin.py:368) with action_taken token_rotated and no token value, and a sink failure only logs a warning. Nothing else in authentication reaches the audit. SecurityEventType (agents/core/security/types.py:22) still lists only secret_detected, pii_detected, ssrf_blocked, egress_downgrade, audit_log, llm_call and settings_change. _admin_guard (agents/web.py:246) and _user_guard (agents/web.py:327) return or raise 401/403 without writing an event, so a wrong admin token leaves only an HF-2 rate-limit bucket entry. TokenStore.issue, rotate and revoke_all (agents/core/security/token_store.py:73, agents/core/security/token_store.py:131, agents/core/security/token_store.py:143) write no audit, so CLI mint/rotate/revoke (agents/core/security/token_store.py:229) is invisible. No test asserts any auth audit row, including the existing rotation row.
reviews.remaining: Add auth event types: admin/user auth success, auth failure with reason (missing, invalid, network-disabled), token issued, token rotated, token revoked. Emit them from _admin_guard and _user_guard: failures always; successes deduplicated per token hash and client so the chain is not flooded. Also emit from TokenStore issue/rotate/revoke_all, which covers the CLI. Each event records scope, client host, reason and a token-hash prefix. A fixed redacted-field set (token, x-admin-token, x-user-token, authorization, cookie, code, state, ticket) is dropped before serialisation. Writes are best-effort: an audit failure must never change the allow/401/403 decision. The rotation route should switch to the new type. Tests must cover all of this.

reviews.summary: Two of the three accepted parts exist. Surface scoping: agents/core/tool_profiles.py resolves the offered tool set per agent × surface × principal in one module (classify_turn at agents/core/tool_profiles.py:127, resolve_tools at agents/core/tool_profiles.py:213). A call outside the profile is refused before execution (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:420), and tests/test_tool_profiles.py pins the resolved sets in a snapshot. Install posture: requirements-beta.lock is hash-pinned and gated in sync by .github/workflows/lockfile.yml, with no runtime installs; docs/FLAGS.md states the risk delta of each flag. The data-handling part, which the row named as the gap worth closing, is still mostly absent. The lot added one narrow control. `llm.openrouter_data_collection` (agents/core/settings_db.py:174), seeded `deny` (agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:41), is sent as OpenRouter's `provider.data_collection`, asking OpenRouter to route only to upstreams that do not store or train on prompts. HybridRouter hands OpenRouterBackend a reader that re-reads it before every request (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:395), only the openrouter profile carries it (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:70), and it is written only through the admin-guarded, audited PUT /api/admin/settings/{category} (agents/core/routers/admin.py:166). tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py pins the `deny` default and the wire object. It is not a provider tier. ProviderProfile (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:28) carries auth, capabilities, fallback models and reasoning vocabulary but no data-handling or training tier. HybridRouter.select_backend (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:498) routes to Gemini, Claude or a non-OpenRouter compatible provider without consulting one. Switching the OpenRouter knob to `allow` is taken silently. GET /api/security/posture (agents/core/routers/security.py:282) and the HUD PosturePanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:988) report secrets, signing, sandbox, hardened and product posture only. No acknowledgement setting and no warning exist.
reviews.remaining: Missing: a per-provider data-handling tier (for example no_training / may_train / unknown) on the provider metadata, covering the direct Gemini and Claude routes and the openai-compatible, openai-responses and xai providers that `llm.openrouter_data_collection` does not reach; a warning emitted every time a turn is routed to a may_train or unknown provider, including an OpenRouter turn under `data_collection=allow`; a durable per-provider acknowledgement written only through an admin_guard settings route. Following Hermes, the acknowledgement removes the stop on unattended runs but never the warning. The tiers, the OpenRouter `data_collection` value and the acknowledgement state are also missing from /api/security/posture and PosturePanel.

reviews.summary: Implemented configured local ComfyUI backend aliases and allowlisted checkpoint selection, up to four opaque generated-image references blended before editing, and explicit 2x bicubic upscale. Options remain bound into the existing exact, single-use approval tuple. HUD submits and displays these choices. A separate cloud-image adapter now completes one exact human-approved OpenAI gpt-image-1.5 request with finite size/quality options, fail-closed secret screening, fresh DNS-bound transport and durable no-replay attempts. Validated PNG bytes persist under an opaque local ID; opt-in catalog finalization is idempotent and reaches the existing gallery/blob/export flow. Independent mocked-transport checks cover the full guarded path; no live paid generation was performed. The owner Images panel now defaults to local and exposes the fixed cloud provider with finite size/quality controls. Read-only status does not sign, write configuration, probe network or expose credentials. Cloud serialization excludes local-only options. Decision Inbox shows immutable paid-operation details and retains a visible task-return link after approval. Strict task-ID URL restoration only reads existing tasks; no automatic resubmission. Independent click-only browser tests cover a nonempty prefix, signed worker, PNG, gallery and ZIP with mocked provider transport. After the separate HUD grid repair, the actual approved cloud browser workflow also passes at1280px and Pixel7; the desktop fixture no longer avoids the reproduced overflow. The model-callable image_generate tool now accepts an explicit cloud selector with only the existing fixed OpenAI model/size/quality vocabulary. Server-owned gated intake preserves the trusted actor and turn origin and proposes one signed plugin.egress task; the agent loop stops for the same human approval. Local generation/edit remains the default. Cloud arguments cannot execute as a local tool.rpc task, and missing runtime or ambiguous enqueue does not trigger fallback or resubmission. Actual ToolRPC/approval/worker/mock-provider/PNG/catalog and cancellation/restart regressions pass. The default-off local residency manager now requires exact controller acknowledgments before confirming loads or forgetting unloaded models. Refused unloads retain prior accounting and stop replacement; request references alone never imply residency. Strict LM Studio and Ollama adapter checks, cancellation/concurrency cases and actual Agent best-effort continuation pass offline and independent review.
reviews.remaining: The real ComfyUI path does not yet use the existing LLM unload/restore orchestrator. Frozen media.generate/file.write action-kind requirements need explicit architecture adjudication; current local tool.rpc and cloud plugin.egress mediation are verified but are not silently equated to that requirement. Local reference blending is pixel composition and upscale is bicubic resampling. The accepted adaptation requires one cloud seam, not eight-provider fan-out. Ambiguous provider attempts never retry automatically; catalog opt-out is respected. No live ComfyUI, billed provider or native-device validation is claimed. This acknowledgment foundation is not a VRAM swap: canonical aliases, production backend/controller identity, atomic per-generation leases, owner control coordination and authoritative hardware snapshots remain unresolved. Existing coarse headroom and no-victim overcommit behavior remain. ComfyUI unknown submissions need reconciliation before any future exclusive lease can safely release.

reviews.summary: The unified gallery now scans retained generated and attachment metadata through bounded keyset pages. Search and kind filters apply during each scan, including MIME matches; zero-match pages retain continuation to older records. Cursor fields, ordering and filter/source binding are checked before catalog or header I/O. Each request inspects at most 200 candidate headers and retains the existing authenticated path/byte validation. The HUD resets and cancels stale searches, reports retained versus loaded/scanned counts separately, and exports an explicit selection of at most 200 files/128 MiB. Independent review and desktop/responsive-browser tests cover older-only matches, empty-page continuation, deletion boundaries, source flags, malformed cursors and exact export selection. Shared attachment previews now abort on card unmount and reject late fetch/body continuations; owned object URLs are revoked even before a pending React state update commits. Reassessment against the frozen keep/superior row confirms the bounded retained-catalog browse/search/export contract. Retention and unavailable-byte handling match the original scope; deleted/evicted history restoration, native controls and unlimited ZIPs are not acceptance requirements. Timestamp/key traversal excludes newer appends without promising exact membership against backdated inserts. The current local generator catalogs produced assets; legacy cloud proposals do not execute a cloud image backend. Future approved cloud completion must persist catalog output as part of H515, not be inferred from generic text-task completion. No live-provider or universal producer-provenance proof is claimed. The implemented cloud-image producer now writes canonical validated output and an idempotent opt-in catalog record before successful completion; independent signed-worker/mock-provider/blob/ZIP checks cover the previously conditional writeback obligation. The legacy generic text task is not treated as an image producer.

Generated/cache and attachment bytes are served by opaque ID through one authenticated shared reader, bounded canonical roots, 16 MiB file caps and MIME/disposition checks. The unified gallery opens and exports retained entries. Scheduled reminders now send 1..8 exact owner-bound media IDs (32 MiB aggregate) through the real Telegram binary/text adapter under one validated 1..300-second total deadline, default 300, including lookup, reads, all files, final text and held flushing. Durable sending/partial/unknown states, current recipient/content checks and process locks prevent automatic replay, stale-held duplication and late-ack continuation. Independent review confirms owner-authored IDs satisfy the frozen cron-media clause; no model MEDIA parser or every-channel requirement was accepted. At the original review: fresh 148 reader/generation/media checks, independent 98 backend/16 frontend checks and full 1,315 frontend tests pass. Synchronous local I/O is not preemptible, but no subsequent dispatch occurs after expiry. This is code equivalence with mocked HTTP; no live Telegram, new-provider/native-codec or arbitrary-path guarantee. The complete integrated backend suite collected 11,428 tests with 11,404 passes, 23 skips and one expected failure; no unexpected failures. Workdir integration rechecked previously-current evidence against base 837d6d08: additive script-only option validation and adjacent HUD fields leave the media contract unchanged. Existing media and frontend regressions remain green.

A spoken reply now sounds like speech rather than read-out markdown, as Hermes requires, at every text-to-speech entry point. agents/core/voice/speech_text.py is the one normaliser (for_speech, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:143). It drops <think>/<thinking>/<reasoning> blocks, an unclosed one to the end, and everything before a closing tag that never opened. It drops fenced code (``` or ~~~, an unclosed fence to the end) and HTML tags. [text](url) reads as its text, ![alt](url) as its alt, and a bare or <autolinked> URL as "link"; the URL no longer eats a closing parenthesis or the sentence's full stop, so "doc (https://…)." is "doc (link).". Headings, list items (-, *, +, •, 1., 1), task boxes), block quotes and table rows lose their markers and end with a full stop (_line, :115). Table cells read with commas; separator rows and horizontal rules are dropped. Bold, italic, strikethrough and inline-code markers go and their words stay (_inline, :104), with word guards so 2*3*4 and my_var_name survive. Symbols are said in the reply's language (_symbols, :95, WORDS, :79): & as and/și, % as percent/la sută, -> → => as to/spre, and °, °C, °F as degrees/grade (Celsius, Fahrenheit). The language comes from the request, else a ro-RO-… voice, else the engine default (speech_lang, :85). Emoji go: pictographs, flags, keycaps, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, variation selectors and tag flags (_EMOJI, :61). Fish [emotion] tags are kept intact. Text with no letter or digit left is "" (_SAYABLE, :76), and the result is a fixed point. Wiring: TTSEngine.speak normalises before any backend, Fish included, and synthesises nothing when nothing is left (agents/core/voice/tts.py:150-158). An emotion-tags-only reply is also nothing for the other backends (:182). speak_stream normalises the whole reply before splitting sentences (:222), so a code or reasoning block spanning sentences is dropped whole. Through TTSEngine.speak this covers the wake-word VoicePipeline, VoiceChannel.send and chat voice notes: speakable() is for_speech plus its cap, and SpokenReply passes the chat's language (agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:68). POST /tts answers 204 with X-Nerva-Speech: nothing_to_say instead of synthesising (agents/core/routers/voice.py:65), and /tts/stream frames carry the spoken sentences. The HUD twin is frontend/src/speech-text.ts (speechText, frontend/src/speech-text.ts:105). Both implementations are pinned by the same cases (frontend/src/test/speech-text-cases.json, 47 cases, read by both suites). SpeechStreamFilter (:129) drops a fenced block or reasoning block whose markers arrive split across token deltas, holding back a tail that could still become a marker (including a <reasoning …> tag split inside its attributes). An unclosed block at the end is never spoken. frontend/src/voice.ts uses it on the live sentence stream (:281, :332, :343). It normalises the whole reply for /tts/stream, /tts and the browser's own speechSynthesis voice (:204), and every streamed sentence (:302). A 204 is silence, never an empty clip or the fallback voice (:244, :314). Mobile sends the reply to /tts, so the hub normalises it; ttsFetchBase64 reads 204 as '' and speak() finishes at once (mobile/src/api/client.ts:2402, mobile/src/audio/tts.ts:23). Tests: tests/test_h526_speech_text.py (Python, every shared case plus the fixed-point property), frontend/src/test/speech-text.test.ts and voice-speech-text.test.tsx (a live push-to-talk turn with a fence split across deltas), and mobile/src/api/__tests__/tts.test.ts. 126 mutants: 124 caught after nine cases were added; the other two were redundant code, removed.

Conducta de transcriere validează, pregătește și livrează: acceptă octeți direct (`BytesIO`, fără fișier temporar, deci vorbirea nu ajunge pe disc), îi mărginește, trece rezultatul prin filtrul de halucinații și întoarce santinele oneste în loc de text inventat. Are acum doi consumatori — ruta HTTP a browserului și canalul Telegram — peste un singur motor local partajat, nu unul per apelant.
reviews.remaining: Un singur backend. Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, `local_command`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC `TranscriptionProvider`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin `plugin.egress` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. Cache-ul motorului stă tot în `routers/voice.py`, care e casa greșită pentru el; canalul îl importă în loc să-l dubleze, iar mutarea lui e o schimbare separată. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat.

reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul.

A turn can read a document directly through file_read instead of relying on pre-indexed memory. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte).
reviews.remaining: There is no scanned-PDF coverage detection. An image-only PDF extracts to empty or near-empty text and is returned as a successful read, with no warning and no list of empty page ranges, and there is no OCR anywhere in the repo. Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: slides (.pptx), spreadsheets (.xlsx) and the other converter formats are not read, and no Office skills are bundled. The drop-a-file-in entry point belongs to the chat-attachment row.

reviews.summary: Modelul poate căuta și extrage pagini prin egressul existent, cu rezultate limitate și marcate ca date.
reviews.remaining: Rămân cerințe de extracție/paginare/cache/configurare din rândurile complete; x_search exclus nu este reinclus.

reviews.summary: Nerva has no ACP editor-agent surface. No handler for session/new, load, resume or fork exists anywhere under agents/, and the editor-surface row H542 is itself still missing, so nothing can accept an mcpServers array from an editor. The only outbound MCP registry is the process-wide MCPManager (agents/core/mcp/client.py:728-730), which holds a single servers dict. It is filled by the admin-guarded POST /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:174-175) and the persisted global config. There is no per-session server scope, no per-session mcp-<name> toolset, no bounded discovery join and no late refresh of the tool registry. tests/test_mcp_client.py and tests/test_mcp_admin.py exercise only the global registry.
reviews.remaining: Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (4) A scheduled late refresh that re-reads the session's tool list after slow discovery finishes. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's.

reviews.summary: Filtrele allow/deny pe nume și glob (`tools_allow`/`tools_deny`, potrivite cu `fnmatchcase` pe numele original al uneltei) restrâng atât listarea, cât și apelarea uneltelor MCP; deny prevalează (`tool_visible`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:603-610). `_list_tools` nu oferă o unealtă ascunsă (:596-601), iar `MCPServer.call_tool` răspunde `tool_filtered` înainte să plece vreun frame (:616-617), deci scoaterea unei unelte din filtru o revocă imediat, și la apel, nu doar la înregistrare. Un filtru malformat îngustează, nu lărgește: un allow care nu e listă devine `[]` (`_clean_tool_patterns`, :124-135). Limitele (64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere, :120-121) sunt fail-closed. Ruta de add (`admin_mcp_add`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:200-209) refuză cu 400 `{"error": "invalid_tool_filter", "field": ...}` un `tools_allow` sau `tools_deny` peste limite, în loc să-l taie (`tool_patterns_over_bounds`, client.py:138-154), la fel ca pe o valoare care nu e listă sau pe o intrare goală. Un deny care nu poate fi păstrat (peste 64 de pattern-uri, un pattern peste 128 de caractere, sau care nu e listă) venit dintr-un config editat manual prin `load_from_config` îngustează serverul la nimic (`tools_allow = []`) și loghează un avertisment (:407-418), pentru că un deny tăiat ar face din nou vizibilă unealta pe care o numea. Filtrele fac round-trip prin `to_config`/`load_from_config` (:808-809, :852-853). Teste (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py, 13/13 verzi): listare și deny prevalează (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:47-57), unealtă filtrată refuzată la apel pe nume (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:60-70), filtru malformat → nimic și round-trip de config (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:73-84), ruta primește filtre și refuză formele malformate (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:98-109), ruta refuză 129 de caractere / 65 de intrări pe ambele câmpuri (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:121-129) și acceptă un filtru exact la limită (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:132-138), un deny imposibil de păstrat ascunde toate uneltele cu avertisment (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:141-147), iar un config editat manual cu deny peste limite se încarcă fail-closed fără să atingă serverul vecin (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:150-159). Resursele/prompts sunt urmărite separat în H552.

Trust tiers și readOnlyHint limitează doar apelurile MCP, nu oferta. Tier-ul (`read-only` implicit, `full` explicit; alias-uri + `normalize_trust`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:105-117; `MCPServer.__init__` ridică ValueError pe o ortografie necunoscută, :397-400; `load_from_config` tratează tier-ul lipsă ca full-cu-avertisment și unul necunoscut ca read-only, :825-842; ruta de add validează tier-ul, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:194-197) și `MCPTool.read_only` (adevărat doar când `annotations.readOnlyHint is True`, :401-403) sunt consultate exclusiv în `_trust_denial` (:636-649), pe care `call_tool` îl rulează înaintea contractului de formă și înainte ca vreun frame să plece (:618-624): pe un server read-only orice tool nemarcat sau nelistat e refuzat pe nume cu `trust_denied` (`readOnlyHint_required` / `unlisted_tool`); `full` lasă totul la contractul de formă. Oferta (listarea) e îngustată numai de `tools_allow`/`tools_deny` (`_list_tools`/`tool_visible`, :584-610 — mecanismul H-4c pe care îl fixează tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py; un deny care nu încape în limitele de 64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere îngustează serverul la nimic tot prin `tools_allow`, :407-418); tier-ul și hint-ul nu ascund nimic: un server read-only își listează și tool-urile de scriere (`get_tools` :742-746 neîngustat; tests/test_mcp_trust.py:61-68; ruta admin le afișează cu `read_only: false`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:106-112).
reviews.remaining: Rămâne reconcilierea fiecărei căi de autorizare outbound față de contractul complet: nu există hop de aprobare (`kernel|authorize|approval|elicitation|retry` apare în agents/core/mcp/client.py doar în comentariul de la linia 103; `request_elicitation_consent` nu există în Nerva), tier-ul read-only refuză scrierile în loc să le ruteze la consimțământ, dict-ul de refuz (liniile 643-649) nu îi spune modelului să nu reîncerce, `_tool_call_blocked` (:651-670) evaluează doar forma `kind/server/tool/transport/args_keys`, iar apelul outbound nu scrie niciun rând de audit — singura cale outbound guvernată (kernel + audit) rămâne agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py, construită manual pentru un singur server `full`. Dovada pentru mecanismul trust/readOnlyHint e în tests/test_mcp_trust.py (necitat); tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py fixează doar filtrele: serverele pe care le apelează sunt construite cu `trust="full"` (helper-ul `_server`, tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:33-44), iar celelalte (inclusiv cazurile fail-closed pentru limite, tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:141-159) rămân pe tier-ul implicit fără să aserteze ceva despre el.

reviews.summary:
H557 is PARTIAL, not missing and not equivalent. The 2026-09-07 verdict is stale on one half and still correct on the other; the overnight triage's "already equivalent" is wrong. Re-read 2026-09-22 after #1179 (cda4e19d): that PR touched agents/core/mcp/client.py only in the stdio env-baseline disclosure — the scope paragraph of the module docstring (client.py:17-36), `from pathlib import Path` (:58), the `_CWD_SECRET_FILES` comment block + constant + `cwd_secret_files()` (:211-242) and the "withholding is undercut" warning block in `MCPServer._merged_env` (:560-571) — none of which this row relies on; `MCPTool`, `_list_tools`, `MCPManager.get_tools`/`_resolve`/`find_tool`/`call_tool` are byte-identical to the pre-#1179 file, and the six other evidence files are unchanged. Only line numbers moved (they had already drifted 94 lines at #1174 and were 151 off after #1179). Re-read again 2026-09-23 after the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1): it added `tool_patterns_over_bounds` after `_clean_tool_patterns` (client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (:407-418), a bounds refusal in `admin_mcp_add` (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:202-208) and bounds tests at the end of tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:112-159); none of it touches a schema, a tool name or the resolver, so client.py pointers moved another +19 (the `MCPTool` block) or +31 (from `MCPServer.__init__` on) and routers/mcp.py pointers past the filter check moved +4. Every pointer below is at HEAD. One fact did change between the 2026-09-07 stamping and HEAD, by #1152 (0ef4002f, 2026-09-15) rather than #1179: a fifth provider serialization path now exists (see NOT SHIPPED).

SHIPPED (the row's rationale half). The name-collision correctness bug is fixed and tested: agents/core/mcp/client.py:748-777 `MCPManager._resolve` accepts a bare tool name only when exactly one server offers it and otherwise returns `{"error": "ambiguous_tool", "servers": [...]}` (:772-776); `server/tool` or an explicit `server=` pins the server (:756-767); `find_tool` (client.py:779) and `call_tool` (client.py:788) both route through it; `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:367-370) is the `server/tool` form. tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-74 proves first-wins is gone (3 tests, passing; file 6/6 at HEAD). This is a genuine different-spelling equivalent of Hermes' disambiguation property, so `missing` under-reports the row.

NOT SHIPPED (the row's headline half). There is no `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` equivalent. agents/core/mcp/client.py:584-601 `_list_tools` still stores `t.get("inputSchema", {})` verbatim (client.py:592) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (client.py:357) with zero repair — the 2026-09-07 evidence sentence is still literally true. Nerva repairs at the dialect boundary instead, and on only ONE of five provider serialization paths: agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-438 `gemini_schema` covers Hermes' `required`-pruning (:424-428) and missing-`type` coercion (:421), and :441-451 `gemini_function_declarations` avoids the empty-OBJECT 400 (:447-449); its output feeds only gemini.py:340-342. The other four paths pass `input_schema` through byte-for-byte: Anthropic (tool_dialects.py:147-151 `anthropic_tools`, :149, via anthropic.py:171), OpenAI chat-completions (tool_protocol.py:19-27 `ToolSpec.as_openai`, :25 — shared by base.py:556, the Ollama path base.py:811 and openrouter.py:95), OpenAI Responses (responses.py:72-81, :77) and xAI Responses (xai.py:79-80 — `XAIBackend._payload` at xai.py:55 overrides `ResponsesBackend._payload` at responses.py:59, so the responses.py builder never runs for xAI; this path landed in #1152 on 2026-09-15, after the original verdict counted four). Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path: re-run at HEAD, `gemini_schema({"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null})` → `{"default": null, "anyOf": [{"type":"string"}, {}]}` (the Pydantic null branch is not collapsed; on the Gemini path it degenerates to an empty schema, and the Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI paths ship the raw nullable union untouched — reproduced through `anthropic_tools` and `as_openai` on a ToolSpec carrying that property), and `{"definitions":{"Node":…},"properties":{"node":{"$ref":"#/definitions/Node"}}}` → `{"type":"object","properties":{"node":{}}}` (draft-07 `definitions`/`$ref` are not promoted to `$defs`, the referenced shape is silently deleted). No name sanitization exists anywhere: `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` is empty, and `qualified_name`'s `/` is not a legal provider function-name character.

ON REACHABILITY. The triage is right that this is currently unreachable from a model: `MCPManager.get_tools()` (client.py:742-746) has zero callers in the whole repo, `MCPTool.input_schema` is read nowhere outside its constructor (`grep -rn "MCPTool" agents/` hits only client.py; `grep -rn "\.input_schema" agents/` outside agents/core/llm/ hits only client.py:357 and the hub's own MCP-server side in route_tools.py), the only `MCPManager` instances are `orch.mcp` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:598, reached from agents/web.py:1783 and agents/web.py:1821 and routers/mcp.py for config and HUD only) and worldview_write.py:77, and agents/core/routers/mcp.py:105-112 and :269-270 expose only name/description/read_only to the HUD, never the schema. But the triage's grep was scoped wrong and missed a real production consumer of the dispatch path: agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:163 calls `self.mcp.call_tool(tool, mcp_args)` by bare name (it lives inside agents/core/mcp/, which their grep excluded). So `_resolve` is not dead code, and its bare-name path is live today.

Unreachability is a reason the remaining work is small and belongs inside the bridge PR — it is not a reason to record the row as done. Six of Hermes' nine clauses are unsatisfied or satisfied on only one of five provider paths, and no test anywhere exercises repair of a third-party `inputSchema`. Recording `equivalent` would put a false claim on a public status page; `partial` with a named remainder is the honest row.
reviews.remaining: No provider-agnostic repair of a third-party MCP server's JSON Schema exists (re-verified at HEAD 2026-09-22, line numbers re-mapped 2026-09-23 after the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change, which touches none of this path; #1179 changed nothing on this path either — its client.py hunks are the stdio `cwd_secret_files` disclosure at :17-36, :58, :211-242 and :560-571; the only change since the 2026-09-07 stamping that bears on this row is #1152 adding a fifth unrepaired provider path, below). (1) `agents/core/mcp/client.py:584-601` `_list_tools` still stores `inputSchema` verbatim (`:592`) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (`:357`); add a `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` applied at registration. (2) Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path, verified by running the code: draft-07 `definitions`/`#/definitions/...` are never promoted to `$defs`/`#/$defs/...` (and `gemini_schema` silently reduces a `$ref` property to `{}`, deleting the shape), and a Pydantic nullable union `anyOf:[{...},{"type":"null"}], default:null` is never collapsed to its non-null branch (`gemini_schema` yields `anyOf:[{"type":"string"},{}]` with `default:null` retained on the Gemini path; the other four paths ship the raw nullable union untouched). (3) The three repairs that do exist (`required` pruned to declared names `:424-428`, missing `type` coerced `:421`, empty-OBJECT avoided `:447-449`) live only in `agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-451` and therefore apply to Gemini alone; the other four serialization paths pass `input_schema` through unrepaired: `anthropic_tools` (tool_dialects.py:147-151), `ToolSpec.as_openai` (tool_protocol.py:19-27; used by base.py:556, the Ollama path base.py:811 and openrouter.py:95), the OpenAI Responses payload (responses.py:72-81) and the xAI Responses payload (xai.py:79-80, whose `_payload` overrides responses.py's, added by #1152 on 2026-09-15). (4) No name sanitization or provider-legal prefixing: `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:367-370) is `server/tool`, whose `/` is outside the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` function-name charset both Anthropic and OpenAI enforce, and nothing replaces characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` returns nothing. (5) The row's security property — a third-party tool shadowing a built-in governed tool name — is unaddressed: `_resolve` (client.py:748-777) disambiguates only among `self.servers` (:768), never against the agent tool registry. (6) No test covers any of this; `grep -rln "gemini_schema" tests/` returns only tests/test_cloud_tool_turns.py, and neither test that constructs `MCPTool` (tests/test_mcp_hardening.py, tests/test_mcp_trust.py) asserts on `input_schema`. All of the above is currently unreachable by a model because no MCP-client -> tool-registry bridge exists (`MCPManager.get_tools()`, client.py:742-746, has zero callers repo-wide), so the normalizer plus its tests should land inside whichever PR first offers MCP client tools to the model, not as a standalone pure function — and that normalizer must sit at registration, ahead of all five dialect serializers, not inside `gemini_schema`.

reviews.summary: S2: consimtamant pe hash-ul suprafetei declarate, inregistrare dovedita in sandbox-ul semnat si dispatch al uneltelor declarate; gazda nu importa niciodata cod tert.
