reviews.summary: The model can read a document mid-turn through a tool call. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte).
reviews.remaining: Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: no .ipynb, .xlsx, .doc, .ppt, .odt, .rtf or .epub, and the text comes back plain rather than converted to Markdown. There is no size refusal for documents (Hermes refuses over 50 MB): the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned. There is no scanned-page coverage warning naming the page ranges that yielded no text, which the row calls the clever half. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. A missing parser is named (`parser_missing`) rather than installed lazily.

reviews.summary: The owner's own chat expands @file:path and @file:path#L10-40 inline. agents/core/context_refs.py holds the rules. expand (agents/core/context_refs.py:129) finds every reference that starts a word (agents/core/context_refs.py:42), including a quoted path, #L7 for one line and #L2-L3, and not trailing punctuation. It keeps the message as typed and appends each file's text under "--- Attached Context ---" in a fence labelled as attached file content, not instructions. Each path is resolved through the same FileScope as file_read (_attach_one, agents/core/context_refs.py:78), so outside the file roots, .. traversal, a symlink escape and a secret-looking path such as .env are refused. A missing file, a directory, a binary file (a NUL in its first 8 KB), a bad line range, a range past the end and an unreadable file each become a one-line warning in the same section instead of failing the message. With no file roots configured, the message says nothing was attached. The limits are 8 references per message, 64 KB per reference and 128 KB in all, counted in bytes. A cut reference says so, and a repeated one is attached once. A line range reads only the lines it needs; invalid UTF-8 is read with replacement characters. The expansion runs on /chat and /chat/stream (agents/web.py:1232, agents/web.py:1392), off the event loop, so both the HUD and nerva chat get it. It never runs for a channel message, as Hermes' gateway does not expand either. A message that attached anything marks its turn: the route binds the marker (agents/web.py:1242, and inside the stream task at agents/web.py:1307). handle_input and handle_input_stream then call _taint_attached_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:332, :1860, :2049), which raises the turn's action origin to recall:untrusted. An action planned from attached content therefore escalates GRANT to QUEUE at the kernel, while an inbound turn keeps its more specific origin. complete (agents/core/context_refs.py:190) lists in-scope completions for what follows @file:, with directories ending in /. It shows dot files only when asked and never secret paths or links out of the roots, is bounded to 50 entries, and returns nothing for a prefix over 1,024 characters. GET /api/context-refs (agents/core/routers/commands.py:63, user-guarded, read-only) serves it and answers 503 no_file_roots without roots. The HUD composer (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:226, :275, frontend/src/context-refs.tsx) lists completions above the input while an @file: reference is being typed; Tab or a click takes one. tests/test_h579_context_refs.py (44 cases) covers the bounds, parsing, whole files, line ranges (single, L-form, past the end), every refusal and warning, a symlink, punctuation, word starts, dedupe, the byte cut, the shared budget, the reference limit, an unreadable file, invalid UTF-8, no roots, an explicit scope and the marker. It also covers completion (prefixes, dot files, secrets, roots, a long prefix, a file or missing folder, the bound), both routes, the completion route, the turn taint on both paths, and an inbound turn. frontend/src/test/context-refs.test.tsx has 3 cases. There are 53 mutants: 49 killed and 4 equivalent. Two of them bound memory only (reading no more than the budget); the other two are a fast path and a context reset that the request's own context already scopes.

OpenRouter provider routing ships, and the owner's changes reach the live backend on the next request. Six llm rows are seeded right after compatible_provider (agents/core/settings_db.py:169-174): openrouter_sort, openrouter_only, openrouter_ignore, openrouter_order, openrouter_require_parameters, and openrouter_data_collection, seeded deny. The HUD PUT /api/admin/settings/llm and `nerva config set` both validate through settings_db.validate_category, and the three slug lists share one slug check (agents/core/settings_db.py:783 -> agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:97). build_provider_block (agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:110) turns the knobs into OpenRouter's `provider` object. It lower-cases and de-duplicates slugs, caps each list at 32, sends require_parameters only as a literal true, omits empty knobs, and raises on an invalid value instead of dropping it. HybridRouter.detect hands OpenRouterBackend a reader over the rows, not a snapshot (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:395). Before every text or tool-turn request the backend re-reads and re-validates them off the event loop (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:94, called at agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:163 and agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:201) and puts the object in the body (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:124). A HUD change, or a `nerva config set` run from another process against the same settings DB, therefore governs the next request, so the CLI's '(a running hub picks it up within 30 s)' holds for these rows. The object goes only to the openrouter profile, never to openai-compatible (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:70). Fail-closed limits: a stored value that decodes but does not validate refuses to build the backend at detect (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:398, logged). After detect it refuses that request: '[OpenRouter error]', nothing sent, and an error log naming llm.openrouter_* (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:107-111). The next request flows once the row is fixed. Known limit: a row that cannot be read or decoded (a sqlite error, or malformed JSON written around the API) is swallowed by settings_db.get_value into that knob's seeded default with no log line. Such a request keeps data_collection deny but loses only/ignore/order/sort/require_parameters. A 400/404 to a request that carried the object logs OpenRouter's own message (log-safe, 200 chars), the object sent and the settings to loosen (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:128), so the seeded deny does not fail opaquely after an upgrade. Coverage is tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py (30 tests). It checks the exact body on the tool-turn and text paths (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:78, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:93), and on the wire through the real egress client with a MockTransport injected through its public transport kwarg (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:135). It checks that no object is sent with nothing set or for openai-compatible (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:102, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:114), and that bad values are refused (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:174, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:180). It covers the rows, the deny default, write validation and the CLI entry point (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:192, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:206, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:223), and router wiring with a stubbed read (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:274, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:287, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:300). Three router tests run on a real temporary settings DB: rows -> detect -> body (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:346); a change after detect reaching the next request, tightening and loosening (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:358); and a tampered row after detect refusing the request, then healing (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:384). Two more cover the policy-404 hint and its absence without an object or on a 401 (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:406, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:424). Nerva has no Nous Portal provider, so the knobs apply to OpenRouter only.

Both halves of the accepted adaptation are delivered: the HUD composer and the terminal. useComposerImages (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx) takes image paste and drag-drop (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:42-43) plus a file chooser. It accepts at most eight PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images of up to 4 MiB each, and the shared InputBar wires it in (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:244). App.submit sends an image draft to runVision (frontend/src/app.tsx:397, frontend/src/app.tsx:372). runVision posts to the user-guarded POST /api/vlm/composer/describe (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:216, registered at agents/web.py:1522). The route checks data-URI signatures and bounds raster decoding (validate_raster, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:53). It binds the request to the reviewed destination/model revision and refuses a non-local VLM unless the owner has acknowledged it (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:237). It then calls VLMBackend.generate_vision_checked (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:357). Images reach only the configured VLM, never the text chat model. The taint governance holds through isolation rather than a taint flag. The vision answer is a client-only transcript entry, and ordinary turns post only {message, agent} to /chat/stream (frontend/src/app.tsx:323), so no tool plan can be derived from image content. tests/test_composer_vision.py (27 passed) covers validation, auth, binding, the remote acknowledgement and error shapes. Intake and the vision turn are covered by frontend/src/test/composer-images.test.tsx, frontend/src/test/composer-vision-turn.test.tsx and frontend/e2e/composer-images.spec.ts, (the two vitest files, 10 cases, pass; the Playwright spec was not run here). The terminal: `nerva chat --image PATH` (repeatable, up to eight) and `--clipboard-image` (agents/cli/nerva.py:300) turn the chat verb into the same vision turn (_vision_turn, agents/cli/nerva.py:2223), dispatched before any /chat body is built (agents/cli/nerva.py:1875). Each file is opened once without blocking, must be a regular file, is read up to 4 MiB and sent by the type its signature says, never its name (_image_mime, agents/cli/nerva.py:1966; _read_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:1976). The clipboard is read by the platform's own reader with a fixed argv, no shell, its output read no further than the bound against a 10 s deadline, in a session of its own whose whole process group is killed at the deadline, past the bound or on an interrupt, so a descendant holding the pipe cannot stretch it (_run_reader, agents/cli/nerva.py:2076): wl-paste on Wayland, xclip on X11, pngpaste or else osascript on macOS, Windows PowerShell from the system directory, else the first powershell.exe or pwsh.exe in an absolute PATH entry that is not the current directory (never shutil.which, which puts the current directory back on Windows), on Windows, and through interop under WSL (the /mnt/c default, else the PATH's powershell.exe) (_clipboard_command, agents/cli/nerva.py:2051; _clipboard_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:2161). The verb reads GET /api/vlm/composer/status, sends that destination and binding with the images, so a model changed in between is refused (409), and a destination off the hub's machine is used only when --remote-vision names it, the terminal's form of the HUD's per-destination acknowledgement (agents/cli/nerva.py:2286). The describe call waits up to 240 s (the hub gives the model 180 s), and a timeout after the status answered is a failed turn, not a missing hub; the reply is checked as the HUD checks it (ok, a string answer of at most 128 KiB); a status without its destination, binding or local sends nothing. The --remote-vision address is compared as the hub names it (scheme and host in any case, the default port, a trailing slash); one with a user name, query or fragment is refused as a look-alike, and --remote-vision without an image is refused. A body the route refuses is answered with its first reason as {error, reason}, never FastAPI's default 422 that echoed the images back (_BoundedValidationRoute, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:22), and the CLI prints it, with the field a validation reason names; hub text is filtered before it reaches the terminal. --agent, --session and --reasoning are refused with images: the turn goes to the vision model only, never to /chat, an agent or a session. -z, --json and --usage-file keep their meaning. tests/test_nerva_chat_image.py (30 cases) covers the route taken, the real route answering the CLI, a model changed in between, each raster kind, the remote acknowledgement, the refusals before any request, the hub's answers and the clipboard readers; its 20 mutants are all caught. The first adversarial review (0 major, 6 minor, 9 nits) found the 30 s timeout reported as no hub, the clipboard buffered whole, the route's refusal without its reason, PowerShell resolved from the current directory, 16 surviving mutants of its own, and macOS/WSL gaps; all are fixed, and tests/test_h586b_image_review.py (50 cases) pins them, its 35 mutants all caught. Test manual: CHT-115, CHT-116. The second review (0 major, 4 minor, 8 nits) found an oversized clipboard image reported as empty, the deadline stretched by a descendant, the Windows fallback still reaching the current directory through shutil.which, and 8 real survivors; all are fixed, tests/test_h586c_image_review.py (23 cases, real processes for the deadline, the group kill, the exit code and the bound) pins them, and its 16 mutants are all caught but one equivalent. Known limits: the receipt's model stays null for an image turn, and the route's own 403 (no acknowledgement) is told apart from an auth 403 by its message, a case the binding already makes unreachable.

Nerva reads a project's convention files into the turn, as Hermes reads its context files and subdirectory hints. agents/core/project_context.py walks from the nearest git root (never above the file root) down to the working directory, the first JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS root, and reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc in each directory in that order (CONVENTION_NAMES, candidates). A directory that file_read, file_list, file_search or a local terminal_run touches is noted for the session (note_tool_path, bounded to 8 directories and 256 sessions); its chain is read on every later turn, and the tool's own result carries the files the turn had not seen yet, marked tainted so the loop fences it (attach, attach_terminal; agents/core/file_tools.py _with_project_context; agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py _rpc_terminal_run). A project SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md or IDENTITY.md is never read, not even through a symlink (HUB_FILES, _admit). Every file is resolved through FileScope (outside the roots, symlink escape and secret paths refused), must be a regular file (a FIFO is never opened), and is bounded to 20 KB, with 40 KB and 12 files a turn; a cut says how much was shown and a file past the budget is named (load_file, collect, render). Each file is scanned with detect_injection_normalized and a flagged one becomes a [BLOCKED ...] line with none of its text. The caveated block sits after the core-memory block in _build_agent_turn_text; _begin_project_context builds it off the event loop at turn start in both turn paths and marks the turn recall-tainted when any file was given, so an action planned from it escalates GRANT to QUEUE. It is off with llm.project_context_files and in safe mode (layer project_context, named on the HUD banner). tests/test_h594_project_context.py: 47 cases; 51 mutants, all killed.

K1/K2/K3 are delivered: default-off execute_code with fresh host authorization, persistent session namespaces, operator status/reset, and redirected Python stdout/stderr stream spills on both one-shot and session paths. Each stream spill keeps at most 5,000,000 bytes (the ToolResultStore default, which the coordinator does not override). Past that, the file ends in one explicit spill-capped marker, the result reports the cap with kept and on-disk byte counts, and the notice says the stream's end survives only in the inline tail. Bounded previews retain file references, original byte counts and the on-disk file hash without buffering the full stream. A notice names the exact file_read(path, offset, max_bytes) paging call, also returned as a read_with field and continued by next_offset, only when two conditions hold: the run's own offer includes file_read, and the coordinator's probe confirms file_read can open that spill through the live file scope or the spill directory's read-only door. Otherwise the notice says the file is kept for the owner and cannot be paged from that turn. H660 now supplies the detached Docker transport. Review fixes retain unconfirmed teardown as quarantined/retryable state and prevent fallback dispatch after current authority or e-stop refusal. Native macOS and Linux real-Docker containment are now verified. The host CLI and local Unix endpoint are frozen; private CLI configuration prevents operator proxy credentials reaching the worker, including after context changes.
reviews.remaining: Generic SSH/Modal provisioning remains unsupported; the validated Docker transport accepts local Unix endpoints. Deliberate native-fd bypass output is not a redirected Python stream. Stream spills are capped at 5,000,000 bytes per stream: later bytes are counted but not kept, so only the inline tail shows a runaway stream's end. Hermes project|strict mode remains intentionally represented by Nerva tool profiles (agent x surface x principal), not copied as a separate switch.

reviews.summary: The pool mechanism is wired end to end. AuthProfilePool (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py) holds several keys per provider, read from *_API_KEYS with a *_API_KEY fallback (from_env, agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:86). hybrid_router builds Gemini and Anthropic pools (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:327). ClaudeBackend and GeminiBackend fail over to the next key on a rotatable status (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:116, agents/core/llm/gemini.py:201). report_failure (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:159) applies an exponential cooldown from 30 s to 15 min. Pool health is exposed. status() (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:178) returns masked per-profile failures and health through the admin-guarded GET /api/llm/auth-profiles (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:442). AuthProfilesPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2606) renders it, under the console route at frontend/src/console-routes.ts:119. tests/test_h12_20_auth_rotation.py (18 passed) and tests/test_route_guard_contracts.py::test_llm_auth_profiles_requires_admin (passed) cover the pool and the guard.
reviews.remaining: The accepted branches are missing. _ROTATABLE_STATUS (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:28) is {401, 403, 429}, so a 402 billing failure neither rotates nor gets the long (1 h) cooldown. No OAuth credential type exists, and a 401 has no refresh-then-rotate step. Keys resolve only from os.environ in from_env; VaultResolver (agents/core/secrets_vault.py:16) is never consulted for LLM keys. The owner also cannot see partial degradation. AuthProfilesPanel shows one healthy/failing tag per provider, derived from the pool-level healthy count, so a pool with some keys cooling still reads green. The API returns per-profile cooldown, but the panel does not render it.

reviews.summary: Local image generation and editing retain exact single-use approvals; the HUD now offers configured local ComfyUI backend/checkpoint choices, up to four blended opaque references, and explicit 2x bicubic upscale. The API additionally accepts one governed OpenAI image generation with fixed model and finite size/quality options; the current HUD still authors local requests.
reviews.remaining: Cloud HUD authoring, additional vendor model inventories and broader provider controls remain open. Reference blending is pixel composition and upscale is bicubic; no real ComfyUI or billed cloud provider proof was performed.

reviews.summary: Memoria și graful au backend; DW-1 afișează entități și legături reale, cu mostre doar în Demo.
reviews.remaining: Rămân timeline/as-of, paritatea exploratorului și controalele de memorie cerute de rând; o listă de vecini nu închide harta semantică.

reviews.summary: Modelul poate căuta și extrage pagini prin egressul existent, cu rezultate limitate și marcate ca date.
reviews.remaining: Rămân cerințe de extracție/paginare/cache/configurare din rândurile complete; x_search exclus nu este reinclus.

reviews.summary: Five TTS backends exist: Edge (the default), ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, local XTTS and Kokoro. TTSEngine.speak (agents/core/voice/tts.py:150) sends Fish, XTTS and ElevenLabs voices to _speak_fish, _speak_xtts and _speak_elevenlabs (agents/core/voice/tts.py:293, agents/core/voice/tts.py:231, agents/core/voice/tts.py:254) by voice-name marker. Otherwise it falls back to edge-tts, then Kokoro (agents/core/voice/tts.py:198, agents/core/voice/tts.py:338, agents/core/voice/tts.py:349). strip_emotion_tags is applied for every backend except Fish. The consent gate for cloned and persona voices is intact. is_persona_or_cloned_voice (agents/core/voice/tts.py:55) checks PERSONA_VOICE_MARKERS (agents/core/voice/tts.py:36), and voice_persona_consent_granted (agents/core/voice/tts.py:63) reads the voice.persona_voice_consent setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:209). STT is faster-whisper only (STTEngine, agents/core/voice/stt.py:53; transcribe at agents/core/voice/stt.py:85). tests/test_tts.py (10), tests/test_tts_fish_emotion.py (12), tests/test_q4_voice_consent.py (7) and tests/test_voice_stt.py (6) pass.
reviews.remaining: Both accepted additions are missing. There is no Piper provider: agents/ and tests/ never reference piper, and the only mention is a demo ADMIN fixture in the HUD. A fully local Romanian voice therefore still depends on Kokoro or XTTS being installed. There is also no command-provider escape hatch for TTS or STT. The voice.tts_voice setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:208) only chooses among the hard-coded backends in speak, and STTEngine has no alternative to faster-whisper.

reviews.summary: S2: consimtamant pe hash-ul suprafetei declarate, inregistrare dovedita in sandbox-ul semnat si dispatch al uneltelor declarate; gazda nu importa niciodata cod tert.
reviews.remaining: Jumatatea de hook-uri este acum livrata doar ca observare: patru evenimente ajung la o extensie izolata, dar niciun hook nu poate bloca sau transforma. Jumatatea blocanta ramane inchisa prin decizie: H021, H163 si H514 exclud explicit hook-urile shell scrise de owner, iar calea lor de redeschidere cere un kernel kind `hook.exec` cu token de capabilitate si script fixat prin hash - adica agents/core/kernel/**, cale protejata. Este o decizie a owner-ului, nu una de luat scriind cod.

reviews.summary: Motorul SQLite, CLI și HUD pot crea, porni, pune pe pauză, relua și șterge joburi; există istoric.
reviews.remaining: Reevaluat 2026-09-19: repeat (`options.repeat`, 1–10000), ținta de livrare per job (`Job.channel`), workdir (`jobs_workdir.py`), pin-uri de model/provider (`llm/job_selection.py`), scripturi fără agent (`jobs_scripts.py`), rulări manuale asincrone (`jobs_dispatch.py`), media programată (`jobs_media.py`), doctor (`jobs_health.py`) și toolset-uri per job (`job_toolsets.py`) sunt livrate — textul anterior le cerea ca lipsă. Rămân din cerința Hermes: înlănțuirea `context_from` între joburi și continuitatea, intenția de rutare `all` și rutarea pe topicuri Telegram, suprimarea `[SILENT]`, livrările continuabile care se reatașează unei sesiuni, raportarea fire-urilor ratate și recuperarea misfire, joburile susținute de skill-uri, programarea gestionată de agent în spatele unui flag, efortul de raționament per job, și clauza de guvernanță: crearea unui job ca `schedule.create` prin kernel (path protejat, owner). NEVERIFICAT pe scheduler și canale reale.

reviews.summary: Din cele patru sisteme de hook-uri exista doar observarea: patru evenimente livrate unei extensii semnate, consimtite si izolate.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc gateway event hooks, ctx.register_hook cu catalogul de 37 de evenimente, hook-urile shell si webhook-urile semnate pe evenimente de ciclu de viata. Jumatatea blocanta ramane inchisa prin decizie: H021, H163 si H514 exclud explicit hook-urile shell scrise de owner, iar calea lor de redeschidere cere un kernel kind `hook.exec` cu token de capabilitate si script fixat prin hash - adica agents/core/kernel/**, cale protejata. Este o decizie a owner-ului, nu una de luat scriind cod.

reviews.summary: S2: consimtamant pe hash-ul suprafetei declarate, inregistrare dovedita in sandbox-ul semnat si dispatch al uneltelor declarate; gazda nu importa niciodata cod tert.
