reviews.summary: The three external intakes now honour an Idempotency-Key, so a retried request returns the original run instead of starting a second one. agents/core/idempotency.py holds the rules. parse_key (agents/core/idempotency.py:67) accepts 1-255 visible ASCII characters and refuses anything else with HTTP 400 invalid_idempotency_key. check_header (agents/core/idempotency.py:257) runs first on every route, before the body is read or the caller is checked. IdempotencyStore (agents/core/idempotency.py:92) keeps a SQLite row whose primary key is (scope, key), in the data folder (idempotency.db). reserve (agents/core/idempotency.py:131) runs inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so two workers or processes on the same file cannot both win (8 racing threads get exactly one reservation), and a reservation survives a restart. A row holds only the fingerprint (SHA-256 of method, path and body, each length-prefixed; agents/core/idempotency.py:76) and the public reference of what the request started, capped at 2 KB. It never holds the body, a reply or a credential. A retry with the same fingerprint returns that reference with Idempotent-Replayed: true, and nothing runs again. The same key with a different request gets 409 idempotency_key_reused. A retry while the first attempt is still running gets 409 idempotency_in_progress with Retry-After. A first attempt that raised or answered 5xx releases the key, so its retry runs. An attempt abandoned by a dead process is taken over after 600 s. Rows expire after 24 h. When the store cannot be written, a keyed request is refused with 503 idempotency_unavailable rather than run without its guarantee. durable (agents/core/idempotency.py:113) says whether the store is a file rather than :memory:. The scope is the authenticated caller, and the key is reserved only after authentication and before anything is queued or run, so a duplicate never becomes a second approval item, kernel task or audit row. POST /api/actions/request (agents/core/routers/actions.py:63) reserves in the owner's action scope after the body is validated. A replay returns the queued action, or its id if the queue no longer holds it. POST /api/a2a/task (agents/core/routers/a2a.py:72-73) reserves in the scope a2a:<peer> only after the peer's signature verifies. A forged retry is refused with 401 and never reads the peer's receipt, and a refused task releases its key. The stored receipt is id, status and accepted. POST /api/webhooks/{id} (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:551) reserves in the scope webhook:<id> after the token or signature, the receiver switch and the enabled check, and before the delivery is counted, run or sent. _run_delivery (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:581) is the previous delivery body, unchanged. _public_outcome (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:570) keeps only ok, target, skipped and error; a replay answers those with the original status code, never the reply, steps or delivery. tests/test_h659_idempotency.py (70 cases) covers the key grammar, the fingerprint, and every store state: TTL, stale take-over, restart, two workers, a thread race, an in-memory store, the reference cap, an unreadable reference, and rollback on a file and in memory. It also covers the begin/claim mapping and all three routes: replay, conflict, no key, a malformed key checked first, an invalid body or unauthenticated caller not burning a key, a failed attempt released, scopes per hook and per peer, a skipped delivery replayed, and a forged A2A retry. There are 57 mutants, all killed.

K2/K3 now include a production detached Docker worker over run-to-completion CLI calls, with a private size-limited container mailbox, bounded response packets/backpressure, ready handshake, cell nonces, asynchronous liveness monitoring, and kill/reset/cancel lifecycle. Each cell still crosses the current host authorization and ToolCallBroker. Only a proved pre-dispatch startup refusal permits explicit isolated per-call fallback; dispatched/ambiguous cells never retry. Python cell stdout/stderr streams now reach existing ToolResultStore spills before preview truncation, retaining the middle without unbounded worker buffers up to a 5,000,000-byte per-stream spill ceiling. Past the ceiling, the file ends in one explicit capped marker and the result reports the cap with kept and on-disk byte counts. Spill notices name the exact file_read paging call (path, offset, max_bytes, continued by next_offset) only when the run was offered file_read and it can open that file; otherwise they say the file is kept for the owner and cannot be paged from that turn. Session tool-RPC uses directory-pinned no-follow I/O and random cell directories, closing a reproduced host-write symlink issue. Existing opt-in settings and digest-pinned Docker isolation remain. Independent-review repairs recheck e-stop/expiry and authorization inside fallback dispatch, retain unconfirmed removals as quarantined records with retryable operator reset, validate hostile stream labels, and keep deadline/stop monitoring independent of awaited tool calls. Late broker replies cannot write after cancellation; old-cell cleanup cannot destroy a replacement kernel. Native macOS and Linux real-Docker containment are now verified. The host CLI and local Unix endpoint are frozen; private CLI configuration prevents operator proxy credentials reaching the worker, including after context changes.
reviews.remaining: Generic SSH, Modal and remote TLS provisioning remain unsupported and require an explicitly isolated governed transport design. Docker selection currently supports local Unix endpoints. Correlation tokens/nonces reject stale frames but cannot attest output against Python introspection inside the same worker; authorization is enforced by the host broker. Spills cover redirected Python stdout/stderr up to 5,000,000 bytes per stream; deliberate native-fd bypasses and the part of a runaway stream past that ceiling are not kept on disk. Production deployment evidence is separate from these real-container tests.

reviews.summary: Oversized output is paged back from its spill file instead of being re-run. execute_code stdout/stderr are spooled to disk as they arrive (agents/core/code_tools.py:480, agents/core/tool_result_store.py:431) under <data root>/workspace/tool_results. Each stream is capped at DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES = 5,000,000 (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:130): StreamSpill.write stops writing at the cap but keeps counting (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:600), close appends one '[... spill capped at N bytes: M more bytes ...]' marker (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:642), and the result carries <stream>_spill_capped and <stream>_kept_bytes (agents/core/code_tools.py:274-275). Head and tail stay inline with omitted-byte accounting (agents/core/environments/output_limits.py:42, tests/test_environment_output_limits.py:38). A whole result the loop spills (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1404) keeps both ends in its preview (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:705-706, tests/test_tool_loop_result_spill.py:139), and file_read itself is never spilled (tests/test_tool_loop_result_spill.py:287). Every notice carries the exact call from page_recipe (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:145): file_read(path="<resolved path>", offset=0, max_bytes=N). The same arguments are returned as <stream>_read_with (agents/core/code_tools.py:272) and read_with (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:736), and stream recipes propose pages of at most 8,000 bytes (agents/core/code_tools.py:226). file_read takes an integer offset from 0 to MAX_OFFSET = 2**53-1 (agents/core/file_tools.py:123, agents/core/file_tools.py:1511). Anything else is refused as bad_offset, both in the preflight and in a direct call (agents/core/file_tools.py:1430, agents/core/file_tools.py:740). An offset at or past the end is an empty final page, answered without seeking (agents/core/file_tools.py:758). A page that stops early returns next_offset (agents/core/file_tools.py:1285) and never ends inside a UTF-8 character (agents/core/file_tools.py:1237). A .pdf/.docx pages through its extracted text (agents/core/file_tools.py:1289). The named call is one file_read answers in every live setup, including the three the review found broken. The recipe path is resolved (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:207). A spill is never named like a secret (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:190). file_read alone gets a read-only door for exact spill-file names in the coordinator's spill directory (agents/core/file_tools.py:648, agents/core/file_tools.py:685, agents/core/file_tools.py:1202), wired at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:819. So JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS pointing elsewhere, a symlinked JARVIS_HOME or a bridged tool with a secret-looking name no longer strands the file (tests/test_spill_paging.py:507, tests/test_spill_paging.py:535); the door's limits are pinned by tests/test_spill_paging.py:414. The recipe is named only where that call is answered. ToolResultStore.readable(path) (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:361) asks the coordinator probe (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:823). The probe requires four things: file_read registered, allowed by the job toolset, in this turn's profile offer (noted at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:977), and able to open this very path (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:835, agents/core/file_tools.py:713). execute_code also requires file_read in its own run's offer (agents/core/code_tools.py:462, agents/core/code_tools.py:559). Otherwise the notice says the file is kept for the owner and cannot be paged from this turn (tests/test_spill_paging.py:545, tests/test_spill_paging.py:589, tests/test_code_tools.py:866), and concurrent turns each see their own offer (tests/test_spill_paging.py:627). A failed spill just omits the path (agents/core/code_tools.py:258-259, tests/test_code_tools.py:698). Retention is unchanged (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:490, tests/test_tool_result_store.py:214, tests/test_tool_result_store.py:353). End to end, a real AgentToolRuntime follows read_with and then next_offset through the real file_read and rebuilds the spilled result byte for byte, while the producing tool runs once (tests/test_spill_paging.py:719). execute_code stdout does the same on the one-shot and session paths (tests/test_code_tools.py:824), and a runaway stream stops at its ceiling with one marker (tests/test_code_tools.py:877, tests/test_spill_paging.py:233). Adaptations: offsets are bytes, not Hermes' lines. The 5,000,000-byte cap covers streamed spills, which is Hermes' execute_code scope; whole-result JSON spills stay bounded by the 256 MB retention sweep. A spill stays third-party when it comes back: every file directly in a spill directory counts as one (agents/core/file_tools.py:699), a file_read page of it and a file_search whose matches reach it declare tainted (agents/core/file_tools.py:765, agents/core/file_tools.py:917), and the loop fences the result as DATA and raises the turn's recall taint, in the turn that spilled it or any later one (tests/test_spill_paging.py:761, tests/test_spill_paging.py:812, tests/test_spill_paging.py:834, tests/test_spill_paging.py:856). A trusted tool's spill counts too, because a spill's file name cannot say reliably which tool wrote it.

Built in #1207 and fixed after one adversarial review (review-H666: no major; five minors and eight nits, all fixed). Hermes nests the agent's subtasks with one optional parent on each todo item (the id of another item) instead of a nested array, so merge-by-id keeps working, and draws the list through one defensive tree builder. Nerva now does both, for the todo tool's items and for mission plan steps.

The tree builder:
- agents/core/todo_tree.py tree() (agents/core/todo_tree.py:48) returns (item, depth) pairs in depth-first order, children in list order under their parent, with every item exactly once. It is stdlib only, because the CLI imports it.
- Depth is capped at MAX_DEPTH = 4 (agents/core/todo_tree.py:30); a deeper item is drawn at depth 4, under its parent.
- An item whose parent is missing, itself, or not an id at all is drawn at depth 0 in its place (agents/core/todo_tree.py:65). ref() accepts only text or whole numbers as ids; a bool, a fractional float, a list or a dict is no id, and a whole-valued float is its number, as JSON's 1.0 is 1 to the HUD (agents/core/todo_tree.py:33). When two items share an id, the first holds it. Anything that is not a list is an empty tree.
- Cycle members, and anything under them, are reached from no root, so they are appended flat at depth 0 in list order (agents/core/todo_tree.py:78). A getter that raises counts as no parent. The walk uses an explicit stack, so a 5,000-item chain costs no recursion.
- The HUD's twin is frontend/src/todo-tree.ts todoTree() (frontend/src/todo-tree.ts:28), with the same rules. Both suites read one shared file of 47 cases, frontend/src/test/todo-tree-cases.json (hand-written shapes plus seeded random ones over text, number, whole and fractional float, bool, null, list and dict ids and parents), and assert the same drawn order and depths. The review's fuzz had found the twins differing on whole-valued floats; that is fixed and pinned.

The todo tool:
- An item may carry parent: the id of the item it sits under. It is an allowed item field (agents/core/todo_tool.py:84) and is in the schema as a string of at most MAX_ID (agents/core/todo_tool.py:102); the description tells the model how to nest and un-nest.
- _clean_parent (agents/core/todo_tool.py:197) cleans it like an id. Empty or whitespace-only text means no parent, as Hermes clears it. Anything else that is not an id is refused as todo_bad_parent, with a sentence the model can act on, and changes nothing.
- A parent need not name an item in the list: a dangling, self or cyclic parent is stored and drawn at the top, never refused and never lost.
- On a merge, parent null means not sent (as for content and status), and "" clears it. A changed parent counts as a write, so the plan cap applies. A parent moved by an untrusted turn taints the item, as a status does. Re-sending the same parent changes nothing: no taint, and the plan's labels stay (agents/core/todo_tool.py:400).
- model_items answers the parent only when it is set (agents/core/todo_tool.py:227), so a flat list answers exactly as before and plan_bytes counts a parent's bytes.

Mission plan steps:
- MissionStore.create (agents/core/autonomy/missions.py:203) gives every step a nullable parent. _plan_step (agents/core/autonomy/missions.py:390) reads each entry.
  - A title, or any other value, is a top-level step with its own text, as before; a mapping without title or parent is still stringified.
  - {title, parent?} may sit under an earlier step: parent is that step's index, and only an earlier one. A plan is therefore a forest by construction.
  - Anything else is refused as bad_plan_step: a self, later, out-of-range, negative, bool, text or float parent, a missing or blank title, or an unknown key.
- POST /api/missions (agents/core/routers/missions.py:50) accepts such a plan. A bad step answers 400 with one fixed sentence and code bad_plan_step (agents/core/routers/missions.py:73); no request data reaches the body.
- The build-queue plan kept out-of-range and self parents on mission steps and let the tree degrade them. The store refuses them instead: a mission plan is written once, by its creator, so a bad parent there is a caller's mistake worth a 400. The tree still degrades any step the store did not check, such as a row written before this change, which has no parent key. A legacy entry {title, <other key>} is now refused too; nothing in the repo sends one.
- finish_step budget charging and the completion gates are unchanged. A child step is charged like any step, closing a child does not close its parent, and exhausting the budget still auto-fails the mission.

Rendering:
- nerva todo draws the tree through todo_tree, indented two spaces a level (agents/cli/nerva.py:1556).
- The Decision Inbox's plans in flight (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx) orders items through todoTree and indents each row 14 px a level, with data-depth (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:78). ITEMS_SHOWN counts rows in tree order.
- MissionCanvasPanel draws plan steps through todoTree, the tree keyed by each step's idx (frontend/src/panels/mission-canvas.tsx:248). The finish controls name the step's own idx, not its drawn position: the test clicks done in a nested row drawn third and asserts it posts that step's idx.

Tests:
- tests/test_h666_subtasks.py (39 cases):
  - the tree: DFS order, a child listed before its parent, the depth cap, dangling, self and cyclic parents, non-id parents, duplicate ids, a getter that raises, and a long chain;
  - todo parents: storage, merge, clearing, cleaning, refusal, the cap, labels, taint, the schema and the tool answer;
  - mission step parents in the store and through POST /api/missions, with the refusal cases, budget charging on a child step, and nerva todo indentation.
- Vitest: frontend/src/test/todo-tree.test.ts (9, including the shared cases), plus one case each in the plans-in-flight and mission-canvas suites (indentation, dangling or cyclic parents kept in view, and the finish control's idx).
- 43 mutants of the new guards were all killed (four survivors of the first run were killed by added cases). One unreachable guard, a placed-twice check in the walk, was removed. The review's 51 mutants left three survivors: two (a boolean read as an id in the TS twin, a finish control addressing its drawn position) are now killed, and the third (the tree keyed by position) is equivalent, since a step's idx is its position. Six mutants of the fix round's guards were all killed.

Code execution no longer keeps its files on the system temp root. Where a Sandbox built without an explicit work_dir makes its run directory, first match wins: JARVIS_EXEC_TEMP_DIR in the process environment, then the owner's security.sandbox_temp_dir setting, then the managed cache <data root>/cache/exec (resolve_root, agents/core/exec_cache.py:149). A value that is not an absolute path, or cannot be read as one (a relative path, ~nosuchuser, a NUL byte), is skipped with a warning (_as_root, agents/core/exec_cache.py:117), and the setting refuses such a value on write, as it refuses an age outside 1-8760 hours (agents/core/settings_db.py:747); a choice that names the managed cache, however spelled (through a link or a '..'), is the managed cache, compared by identity (_same_dir, agents/core/exec_cache.py:138). Each run directory is an absolute private mkdtemp (mode 0700, named nerva-sandbox-*) under a root made 0700 when this user owns it; a root that cannot be used gives the system temp directory for that run, with a warning, unmanaged and never pruned (new_work_dir, agents/core/exec_cache.py:177). The Sandbox takes it at construction (agents/core/sandbox.py:85); the orchestrator's one production sandbox (agents/core/orchestrator.py:610) passes no work_dir, so it gets the managed cache. A run directory removed under a live sandbox, or there without its lock or wider than 0700, is made again 0700 and its lock taken again before the next run, and the tool-RPC runtime asks for that before it makes its mailbox inside the directory (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:381) (ensure_work_dir, agents/core/sandbox.py:100). Docker bind-mounts it with --mount, CSV-quoted, so a ':', ',', '"' or line break in the data root is data (_bind_mount, agents/core/sandbox.py:29). A managed run directory's lock lives outside it, in <root>/.locks/<name>.lock, where code run in the directory cannot remove, replace or forge it: an flock held for the sandbox's lifetime, recording host, pid, whether the flock was taken, the kernel's boot id and the pid's start time, written under a private temporary name and renamed into place so it is never seen empty and a link planted at its name is never written through, in a .locks directory that is private and not a link, and released (closed, then removed, as Windows needs) when the sandbox is gone (release, agents/core/exec_cache.py:312; hold, agents/core/exec_cache.py:257). An hourly job (schedule_exec_cache_prune, agents/core/scheduler_service.py:229; run_exec_cache_prune, agents/core/scheduler_service.py:595) prunes the managed cache whatever root is chosen now, off the event loop, never raising into the scheduler (prune, agents/core/exec_cache.py:499). Each run directory is aged as one group: the newest date anywhere inside it, links never followed, dates the whole directory (_newest, agents/core/exec_cache.py:327), a file being dated by the older of its mtime and ctime so a date set in the future never keeps it forever (_date, agents/core/exec_cache.py:323). A directory is removed only when that is older than security.sandbox_temp_max_age_hours (72 by default, never under an hour; max_age_hours, agents/core/exec_cache.py:596), it is not the hub's own live sandbox, and its lock is not held: on the kernel that wrote it (same boot id), a record whose writer took the flock is held exactly while the flock is, so a crashed sandbox whose pid came back (the hub is pid 1 in a container) is free; a record written without a flock is held while its pid is alive with the same start time, asked of the process table on Windows (OpenProcess and GetExitCodeProcess, never os.kill, whose signal 0 is a console Ctrl+C there) (_pid_alive, agents/core/exec_cache.py:390); only a busy flock reads as held, and any other flock error (a filesystem that refuses flock) reads the record; a record from before a reboot of this host, or from before the flag existed, is free when the probe gets the flock; a pid is read only in the pid namespace that numbered it; another host's record, another namespace's, a record whose flock the probe could not test and one with a pid no hold writes are kept until the directory is ten times the age limit old; a lock that cannot be judged is kept and logged and the sweep goes on (_held_safely); a lock that cannot be opened reads as held, and anything but a regular file is no lock (_held, agents/core/exec_cache.py:407). It is claimed by a rename before it is deleted, so a directory that cannot be claimed is kept whole; one swapped for a link after the checks is only unlinked and not counted; an unfinished claim is finished by the next sweep, and a lock whose directory is gone is removed (another host's once the lock is ten times the limit old). Only nerva-sandbox-* entries are considered, in a managed root that is a real directory (not a link or a Windows junction) owned by this user and not writable by others; otherwise the sweep is reported failed to the scheduler, as is an unreadable root (_root_problem, agents/core/exec_cache.py:477). A root the owner chose is never bulk-deleted. Backups leave out the cache and, directly under a root the owner chose inside the data root, the run directories exactly as mkdtemp names them; an owner folder that merely starts with the prefix is kept (agents/core/backup.py:405), and `nerva config set security.sandbox_temp_dir` says it needs a restart. tests/test_exec_cache.py (60 cases) covers the resolution order and the refused values, the relative data root, the sandbox's own directory, its mode and its lock outside it, the owner record without flock, another host, locks that are not files, the probe's descriptors, a sandbox that is gone, a directory removed under a live sandbox (host and Docker paths), group aging by the newest date and by the directory itself, a future date, the age setting and its floor, the live list, the owner-root exclusion, foreign entries and links, a root that is a link or writable by others, a directory swapped for a link, a claim that cannot be made or was left unfinished, orphan locks, an unreadable root, the hourly job (the owner's age, off the loop, never raising, the managed cache while a root is chosen), its registration, the backup and the restart note; tests/test_h667d_exec_cache_review.py (30 cases) covers the third review: refused flocks (ENOLCK, EOPNOTSUPP, EINVAL) and a busy one, owner folders named like the prefix and nested run files in backups, another kernel's record under a free flock, a reboot, a failed exit-code query, a cache that does not exist yet, an owner-root directory made again, a failed replace, a root we do not own, a record from before the flag, another pid namespace, odd pids and a lock that cannot be judged, staged records, an interrupt during hold, a first lock taken later, reparse tags and the label; tests/test_h667c_exec_cache_review.py (55 cases) covers the second review: Windows liveness through a faked process table (no such process, access denied, exited, a reused pid) and a dead sandbox's directory pruned there, the release order, a free flock against a live pid (this process, pid 1, the parent), a renamed host on the same kernel, a flock still held, a record without a flock (alive, reused), another host's record and orphan lock ageing out, the record's fields, the tool-RPC path's re-creation, a directory there without its lock, the managed cache through a link or a '..', control characters, the mount's quoting, the planted link, the private .locks, the backup, a real tree aged with the production date and the record written before the lock has its name. Test manual: PNB-167, PNB-168. The first adversarial review (0 major, 8 minor, 9 nits: a bad setting that stopped the hub's start, a relative data root, backups including the cache, an unreadable cache reported ok, a later choice stranding the cache, lock and mtime games from inside a run directory, no flock on network filesystems, test gaps) is answered in full; its 31 follow-up mutants are all caught but three equivalent ones. The second review (one major: on Windows os.kill(pid, 0) is a console Ctrl+C that never says dead, and an open lock cannot be removed, so the cache was never pruned there; four minors: the record overrode a working flock, the tool-RPC path made the run directory again without its mode and lock, the managed cache spelled another way took no lock, twelve mutant survivors; seven nits) is answered in full; its 36 mutants, all caught but two equivalent ones (a .locks mkdir mode the chmod repairs, samefile behind resolve), five after their cases were added (a probe that took no flock, the start tick's field, a wide .locks, the mailbox made after the repair, a file named like a run directory). The third review (no major; three minors: a filesystem that refuses flock read as busy, backups dropping any folder with the prefix, eight real survivors; eight nits) is answered in full; this round's 18 mutants were all caught but three equivalent ones, three after their cases were added (an odd pid ageing out, another host's pid never read, an owner folder under the chosen root). Not taken: the collision-safe task-id directory naming, which the rationale made conditional on persistent per-task sandboxes, which do not exist (mkdtemp names are unique). TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP still pass through to child processes (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:24-26); the sandbox's own files no longer depend on them. Known limits: Windows liveness is exercised here through a faked process table (the Windows lane runs after merge); on a filesystem whose flock is local to each host (SMB, NFS with local_lock), another host's record is kept by age alone; the settings label and PNB-167 say that JARVIS_EXEC_TEMP_DIR makes a root the owner keeps (never pruned) and that a pruned cache moves with the data root; a live sandbox's own directory is exempt as a whole, not aged file by file; each Sandbox keeps its directory until the prune (there is no close()).

The shared identity band exists. agents/_identity/IDENTITY.md is one behaviour contract: the reply-sizing rule (match length to the weight of the ask), earned depth, the named prohibitions (no filler, no restating the request, no re-summarizing, no narrating visible tool calls), the anti-sycophancy line ('agree because it is right, not because the owner said it') and 'say when you do not know'. Its reply rules govern the agent's own replies to the owner: text drafted in someone else's voice (an email, a post, a message written as the owner) keeps that voice, greetings and sign-offs included, and a persona's warmth or curiosity lives inside the answer (review-H670 m-5); its honesty rules hold for everything an agent writes, drafted text included (review-H670b m-1). Its leading maintainer note (stripped before the model sees it, _strip_maintainer_note, agents/core/agent.py:453) says never to add 'be targeted and efficient in your exploration', and why. The repo-root SOUL.md mirrors the text, so agents working on the repo read the contract the product ships; a test keeps the two equal. identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolves it as soul_path_for does a persona: the data home's souls/IDENTITY.local.md, then a gitignored agents/_identity/IDENTITY.local.md, then the shipped file. read_identity (agents/core/agent.py:481) runs it through the same H387 helpers as a SOUL (the injection scan on the uncapped body, then the cap), announces a flagged or truncated contract (its blocked and quarantined stubs name the contract, not a persona), caps it at its own 4,000 characters (IDENTITY_MAX_CHARS, never above the persona's cap, so the two bands stay within the persona cap plus 4,000), and reads it once per settled file signature for the whole process. An override that cannot be read (not UTF-8, a directory, no permission) is reported at ERROR and the shipped contract used instead, cached against the shipped file's signature so an edit of it is seen; a contract that cannot be located or read at all leaves the agent without it; none of these stops an agent from being built. Agent.system_prompt (agents/core/agent.py:572) is the contract, then the agent's persona (either may be empty; an agent without a SOUL still gets the contract). Every place a system prompt is built uses it: Agent.process (agents/core/agent.py:1008) and the synthesis path in agent.py, and the orchestrator's two sites (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2212, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3863) through _system_prompt_of (agents/core/orchestrator.py:451). At a compaction boundary refresh_soul (agents/core/agent.py:730) re-reads the contract as it re-reads the persona (_refresh_identity, agents/core/agent.py:599): a few stats when unchanged; when the file that resolves is absent, vanishes before the read or cannot be read, the contract in force is kept, reported at the boundary as failed-open and warned once per episode (an override absent for an instant resolves to the shipped file for that boundary, as a persona's does); and a moved contract reported as rebuilt, so an edit reaches running agents without a restart. The contract in force at start is committed to the prompt VC (SoulVersionStore) as _identity (_record_identity_version, agents/core/orchestrator.py:433), a no-op when unchanged or empty, so its history is recorded and diffable through /api/admin/prompts/_identity/... beside the personas; what is served is the file (a rollback in the VC does not change it), and an edit picked up at a boundary is recorded at the next start. The prompt-size report counts it as a shared component every call pays (identity_component, agents/core/prompt_size.py:136), and the packaged build ships it through its agents/*/*.md glob (overrides, *.local.md, never ship). IDENTITY.md and its .local overlay are in the H506 instruction-file class (INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES, agents/core/file_tools.py:259), so a file write to them asks as an instruction file; a test derives the class from every name the contract's and a persona's loaders can resolve. The data home's README lists souls/IDENTITY.local.md. Persona SOULs and Persona.prompt_block (agents/core/cognition/persona.py:142) stay the character layer on top. tests/test_identity_contract.py (18 cases) covers every rule's presence, the banned line's absence and the kept warning, the mirror, the scan verdict, every active agent's system prompt starting with the contract (and exactly contract then persona), an agent without a persona, the orchestrator's helper and all four sites, both overrides and their order, the scan and the cap on an override, an edit reaching a running agent at the boundary, the one-stat unchanged path, a failed re-read keeping the last-good contract, the version record (once, and a failing store never stopping a start) and one read shared across agents; tests/test_h670b_identity_review.py (21 cases) covers the first review: the instruction-file class, a contract absent or vanishing at a boundary, a non-UTF-8 or unreadable override, the contract's own cap, no empty version, the start-time record, the contract's scope, a mid-file comment, the prompt-size component, the ERROR on a flagged contract, the stubs' wording and CHT-117; tests/test_h670c_identity_review.py (14 cases) covers the second review: honesty unscoped, a shipped contract that stops being UTF-8, a vanish before the real read, the hub's start recording the contract, one warning per episode and a second one, a reader that raises, the fallback following a shipped edit, a directory override, a permission error at load and at a boundary, the fallback rules once when both bands are blocked, and the docs. The first review (one major: the contract was outside the instruction-file class; seven minors: a missing contract emptied at a boundary, a non-UTF-8 override stopped every agent, the two bands exceeded the cap, the VC's rollback and A/B claim, the contract's unscoped rules against drafting personas and trait directives, six untested survivors, CHT-117 naming a retired agent; six nits) is answered; its six real survivors are pinned. The feature's 17 mutants were caught but one equivalent; the first review round's 15 were caught, one only against a stand-in (the vanish case, now driven through the real read). The second review (no major; three minors: the scope lifted the honesty rules from drafted text, a shipped contract that stopped being UTF-8 emptied the contract at a boundary, three real survivors; eight nits) is answered; its 31 mutants' three real survivors are pinned, and this round's 10 were all caught, two after their cases were added (a reader that raises, a second warning episode). Known limits: the prompt-size report measures the shipped contract, not an override in force (as it measures shipped personas); PromptRefresh.text is still the persona alone; the contract's scan verdict is reported only in the log (a persona's also reaches GET /api/agents/{id}/soul); the data home's README is written once, so an existing install does not get its new row. Test manual: CHT-117; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md names the band.

Durable session birth is resolved through an immutable, generation-checked continuation root. Explicit owner-created child sessions carry bounded retained context and root birth through multiple generations, text/stream/process entrypoints and restart without switching the shared default. SQLite atomically commits child identity, seed, lineage and initial clock; idempotent request receipts resolve retries. Corrupt newer snapshots, reused identities and failed recovery stop dispatch or writes instead of silently replacing context. Accepted history/tool compaction alone advances the durable rebuild clock through compare-and-swap; request snapshots preserve same-day prefix bytes, reject late inherited commits, and add the trusted current-date line only when rebuild and root-birth days differ. Production rendering resolves explicit TZ or existing local IANA discovery and uses historical/current DST rules with an explicit UTC offset. Unknown birth is omitted; invalid or unavailable zone discovery preserves truthful offset-only rendering rather than inventing an IANA name. Independent actual-route, Agent, restart, concurrency, cancellation, failed-resume and observe-only regressions support the full frozen clock contract. This is code-equivalence, not a live-provider claim; ordinary subsequent JSON persistence remains best effort and turn leases are process-local. H672 hangs the persona re-read on the same commit: `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` calls `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` after the clock CAS and only when the compressor reported a compression, so a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing and an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order (`test_a_refused_clock_commit_migrates_nothing`, `test_an_accepted_clock_commit_is_followed_by_the_refresh_in_that_order`); the re-read neither reads nor writes the clock, so the same-day prefix bytes and the current-date line are untouched by it. #1188's edit to `orchestrator.py` is the pairing store's registry path, nothing on this row.

Both refreshes from Hermes's row exist (`agents/core/session_refresh.py`, the parked mechanism commit 89b53e85 cherry-picked unchanged; its module docstring has since gained a note on where each half is wired) and are wired at Nerva's two compaction boundaries, each failing in its own direction. **Nerva is turn-based, so most of the row was already true between turns and is pinned as such**: `Orchestrator._prompt_context` reads the skills catalog per turn, the plugin block is rendered per turn, and `AgentToolRuntime._run_loop` resolves ToolRPC → capability registry → tool profile at the top of every run (`test_between_turns_the_offer_was_already_live`). Two things were not live. **(1) The system prompt.** `Agent._load_soul` ran once in `__init__` and `orchestrator.py` sent `agent.soul["content"]` for the life of the process, so a persona edited or quarantined mid-session needed a restart. `Agent._read_soul` is the one builder (same file resolution, same H387 scan, same cap) behind both `_load_soul` and `Agent.refresh_soul`, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (orchestrator.py, a module function so the bare-stub tests of that path keep working) calls it for every agent from `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` — after the clock CAS, never before it, and pinned as such: a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing, an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order. In front of the builder sits an `os.stat` probe (`_soul_signature`: resolved path, inode, size, mtime, ctime and the body cap), because once a session is over budget the conversation-level commit happens on **every** turn — `ContextCompressor.compact()` recomputes from the raw turns each call — and the walk is process-wide: an unchanged persona costs one stat, and only a file whose kernel signature moved reaches the builder (measured over the 18 shipped SOULs, 76 KB: 59.0 ms → 0.55 ms per boundary, 18 → 0 reads and scans). A file written within the last two seconds has no trusted signature (git's racy rule: a same-size edit in the same timestamp tick would be invisible to a stat) and is read and compared by bytes until it ages. Past the probe the keep path is byte equality of the builder's whole output — body *and* front-matter, so a tier or trait edit with the same body is adopted and the HUD's `soul["meta"]` follows — never a dirty flag; a builder that throws keeps the last-good bytes (fails OPEN); a file absent for the instant of an editor's save-by-rename keeps them with a plain warning, and an agent that had no persona and still has none is unchanged, not failed. A scan verdict is not a failure — a persona that is now mostly injection is dropped exactly as a restart would drop it — and it is announced exactly as a restart announces it: `_announce_soul_verdict` is the one place both moments log, so a quarantine at the boundary is the H387 ERROR line, not an INFO line. **(2) The tool set inside one turn.** A loop of up to `llm.tool_loop_max_iterations` model turns kept the list it resolved at the top. `_run_loop` treats a committed fold (`_compact_context` grew `compacted`) as the boundary and re-resolves through `_resolve_offer` (the same three steps, minus the turn-start side effects) via `session_refresh.refresh_tools`, which fails CLOSED: a resolver that raises withdraws every tool, an empty resolution is a revocation, and either ends the loop with `_TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY` after a `tool_loop_withdrawn` event rather than asking a provider a turn on a stale or empty list. The offer and the executor move together (`_specs_for` rebuilds the specs, the gate map the executor checks `offered` against, and the untrusted set) — pinned by a tool withdrawn through the *profile* while still registered in ToolRPC, the one shape that can tell the executor's `tool_not_allowed` from the RPC's own (keeping the stale gate map runs the handler, and that test goes red). Between folds the registry is not consulted at all, so the set stays stable between two folds; Nerva's fold happens inside one user turn, so Hermes's "mid-turn tool sets stay stable" reads here as *between folds*. A `tool_offer_refreshed` event (added/removed/reason) is written only when something moved. 17 mechanism tests (`tests/test_session_refresh.py`, red-proofed by mutation in the parked commit) plus 26 wiring tests (`tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py`). An independent review of the first cut found 14 items (4 major, 6 minor, 4 nits: the per-turn, process-wide re-read cost; the H387 verdict suppressed at the boundary; the overclaim that `ToolRPC.handle` refuses profile revocations; the unpinned gate map and CAS order; the front-matter blind spot; the traceback for a persona-less agent; the docstrings); 13 are addressed here and each code fix was neutered once and shown red (8 mutations, 11 distinct tests red).
reviews.remaining: **The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates**: the conversation-level commit exists only with `memory.context_compression` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with `llm.tool_loop_enabled` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. **Profile revocations are not enforced on the execution path**: `ToolRPCServer.handle` checks the job toolset, registration and the gate, never the tool profile, and the executor's gate map is rebuilt only at a fold — so in a loop that never folds (small results, the common shape) a tool the profile withdrew mid-turn stays offered *and* executes until the loop ends; pre-existing, unchanged by this slice, pinned as a limit by `test_between_folds_a_profile_revocation_is_not_enforced_by_the_executor_either`. **The persona migration is process-wide**: `orchestrator.agents` is every agent and `agent.soul` is the one dict every session's system prompt reads, so the session that commits migrates the persona for all sessions (the boundary log line says so); refreshing only the routed agents would need the route at `_history_for_prompt`, which it does not have. **On the staged shared-route path the turn's budget is computed against the persona in force before the commit** (`_shared_route_plan` → `build()` measures `agent.soul` while planning; the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`), so a persona that grew is sent that turn with a budget computed for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, self-correcting next turn; the H363 cached prefix and the H673 usage anchor under-count for one turn after a rebuild the same way. The probe trusts the kernel's signature; what the builder reads outside the file (the scan patterns) is code and needs a restart. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild `messages[0]`: a persona change reaches the *next* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" is only as true as the MCP manager's registration into ToolRPC is hot, which this slice did not verify. The lineage row stays at `nerva.context-compaction.v1`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. `refresh_tools` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. The stale comment at `agents/core/file_tools.py` saying `_load_soul` runs no injection scan predates H387 and is left for a hygiene commit (it would drift five unrelated rows). Nine ledger rows cite `agent.py`, `agent_runtime.py` or `orchestrator.py` and were drifted by this branch (and by #1188 on main: its registry path in `orchestrator.py`, and the pairing kwarg, refusal branch and lifespan hand-over in `telegram.py` and `web.py`, which H146, H449, H364 and H671 also cite and were read against — the pairing store is not their subject); each was re-read against the diff on its cited paths before its hashes moved. Six keep their text and take fresh stamps — H146, H298, H363, H364, H449, H679: the in-turn re-resolution runs through `_profiled`, which still applies the job toolset on both sides of the profile, and the result-spill, cache, reasoning and job-pin mechanism those rows cite is untouched. Three are rewritten — H387: the ERROR line now comes from `_announce_soul_verdict` behind the `_read_soul` builder, for boot and boundary alike; H671 and H673: `publish()` re-reads the personas after the clock CAS, and the staged-route budget limit above is now on H673's own row. The 16 other needs_review rows on main (H060, H061, H068, H071, H104, H108, H130, H135, H139, H398, H477, H510, H523, H683 from #1188's edits to `orchestrator.py`, `web.py` and `telegram.py`; H288 and H684 from #1187's `heartbeat.py` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`) are main's own drift, not this branch's, and are left untouched here; #1187's five-line comment in `orchestrator.py` re-drifted the nine rows above once more, and they were re-read against it and re-stamped.

reviews.summary: Configured Ollama num_ctx is sent on generate/tool/stream; /api/show model parameters can resolve a cached effective ceiling, ignoring architectural model_info maxima. Shared-history compression clamps to that ceiling, hard threshold cannot exceed 85%, and a Gemini compaction model reserves its concrete cloud output cap including auto=8192. Review repair: effective soft/hard thresholds are normalized together and actual compression target stays below the effective hard trigger, including soft=hard=1 configurations; protected head/tail remains intact. Ollama and LM Studio structured tool turns now retain the provider-reported input/output token counts. Strict count normalization preserves valid answers when usage metadata is absent or malformed. Tool-loop usage accumulates for metering while context anchors replace with the latest request count; unavailable input does not erase a prior anchor. Gemini structured turns now retain inclusive prompt counts and disjoint candidate/thought output counts; explicitly OpenAI-compatible profiles retain standard prompt/completion totals without adding nested breakdowns. Complete context anchors now include Anthropic disjoint input/cache-read/cache-write counts, including cache-only requests, while totals-only mappings count the full prompt once. Billing semantics remain unchanged. Complete non-stream text replies now publish provider usage through closed request-local observers. Non-stream agent gathers retain per-agent measurements and complete-prefix anchors; ToolRuntime remains the single structured-turn reporter. Retries publish only accepted response usage; cancellation and inherited late tasks cannot outlive the observer. Public string/stream signatures and guardrails are unchanged. OpenRouter inherited streaming reports its single complete text request once. Ollama, LM Studio and Anthropic actual streams now publish one measurement only after confirmed completion: literal done=true, usage-only snapshot plus [DONE], or valid start/final cumulative message_delta usage plus message_stop respectively. Errors, interruption, malformed frames/containers and missing final usage do not reuse intermediate counts. Retry state resets, disjoint cache categories and text callbacks remain intact. Gemini streams now retain a terminal response's own validated prompt/candidate/thought counts after clean HTTP exhaustion and response close. Known single-candidate completion or explicit blocked-prompt semantics are required; errors, raw trailers, cancellation, conflicting response identities and nonzero/malformed candidate indices invalidate the whole attempt. Retries remain isolated and answer callbacks are unchanged. Pinned ask jobs now resolve and freeze their model/window before history construction, cap completion, and omit an unrelated prior usage anchor; unchanged default models retain their existing estimate. Ordinary tool turns now also use immutable configured/cached backend capacity forwarded before guardrails; known limits include completion, initial/later transcript, schemas and structured tool-call arguments. Unknown capacity remains estimated rather than discovered. Reasoning integration was reviewed against previously-current grid33165622 evidence: request-shaping refusals/empty controls do not change this row's cache, session or context/usage semantics. Existing focused regressions are retained. Responses completed text/tool turns and validated terminal streams now retain reported input/output usage. Inclusive input totals split cached_tokens once into disjoint uncached input and cache_read; output reasoning detail is not added to output totals. Missing/malformed metadata does not invent counts. Stream errors, incomplete/contradictory terminal items, cancellation or failed close do not publish usage; request-local sinks preserve existing single-publication semantics. The xAI Responses dialect inherits the same strict reported input/output/cache split and complete terminal accounting, while its own completed-response acceptance rechecks reasoning/replay lifetimes. Reasoning token detail is not added twice to output totals. Opaque function replay preserves main-loop provider usage without introducing ciphertext persistence, per-vendor prices or cache discount assumptions. Shared history compression now preplans each actual governed specialist route and its finite or dynamic completion reserve instead of borrowing the router default model. The strictest input budget stages one shared summary; final prompts/routes are revalidated through at most three monotonically tightening passes before a single accepted clock/history publication. Prepared text/SSE dispatch preserves backend/model/session/lifetime identity, policy gates and known-versus-estimated context metadata. Selected Ollama resolves its own context. Usage anchors require matching backend/model, session generation and retained-history digest; unmanaged old anchors are not promoted to exact managed measurements. Existing disabled-compression behavior and direct local auto output remain unchanged. Since H672 the accepted clock/history publication is followed by the persona re-read (`_refresh_souls_at_boundary`, after the CAS): it changes nothing in how pressure is measured or anchored, but on the staged shared-route path `_shared_route_plan` measured `agent.soul` while planning and the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`, so a persona that grew at that boundary is sent that turn with a budget planned for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, and the next response's usage anchor measures the real prompt. #1188's edit to `orchestrator.py` is the pairing store's registry path, nothing on this row.
reviews.remaining: A model with no num_ctx parameter and no operator configuration remains unresolved (server environment/running context is not probed). Fixed image estimates remain incomplete. Gemini usage-only final frames, absent terminal-local counts, unknown terminal semantics and ambiguous multi-candidate streams deliberately remain unreported. Synthesis/compression/background model calls are deliberately outside conversational usage attribution. Cache discounts/write premiums and undocumented vendor-specific usage mappings are not modeled by the new totals-only adapters. No live provider or billing proof. Responses accounting is limited to supported API-key GPT-4.1 and exact xAI Grok4.5/4.6 dialects, not Codex subscription usage or general OpenAI reasoning-model replay. Cache counts do not establish live discounts, prices or physical context occupancy. Actual specialist planning applies to the existing opt-in shared-compression path; disabled/unmanaged callers retain their existing behavior. Unknown capacity remains a conservative planning estimate, not verified provider metadata.

reviews.summary: A compaction summary no longer holds the owner's turn past a short bound, and a silent summarizer is cut. Hermes keeps two clocks: how long the summary may make the user wait, and how long the summarizer may go quiet. Nerva awaited the strict-local summarizer inline with neither. Its only limit was the httpx read timeout (120 s for Ollama), a total-duration wait on a non-streaming call, and nothing told the owner. (1) Bounded hold. ContextCompressor takes a gate (agents/core/context_compressor.py:325, used at :591). The orchestrator builds it per turn (_summary_gate, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3574, passed at :3741) around SummaryHold (agents/core/compaction_hold.py:136). SummaryHold.wait (:146) waits at most memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds for the LLM summary (settings_db.py:254; default 10 s, 0 = never wait, clamped 0..120 by hold_seconds, :63). One summary per session is written at a time: a turn that finds one still in flight neither waits on it again nor starts a second. Past the hold the turn goes on without the summary, and compress marks the result summary_deferred (:629). compact (:527) then sends the turns verbatim, their old images dropped, when they still fit the window under the owner's memory.compression_max_tokens; otherwise it sends the deterministic digest. The summary keeps being written. When it lands it seeds this session's iterative-merge prior (_ctx_summary_cache), but only if no newer turn has replaced the prior this turn started from, and never through the compaction-clock CAS: publish commits only what the prompt was built from, and never writes the digest over the pending summary (orchestrator.py:3796). A turn cancelled while it waits (Stop, a client gone) still leaves its summary for the next turn. A summary that fails later seeds nothing and is logged by name. aclose stops what is still being written within the task budget (orchestrator.py:4481; SummaryHold.aclose, :185). (2) The owner is told. record_turn_notice (agents/core/turn_notices.py:35; a per-turn sink collected like turn_approvals, one notice per code) carries DEFERRED_NOTICE (compaction_hold.py:38) out as notices on /chat (ChatResponse.notices, agents/web.py:1101, TurnNotice :1084) and on every /chat/stream end event, the failed one included (:1356, :1362). The HUD shows each notice as a system line under the reply (frontend/src/turn-notices.ts, app.tsx:339). The hub log says the summary was deferred and, later, that it landed. (3) Inactivity deadline. The summarizer now streams (stream_summary, compaction_hold.py:88, called at orchestrator.py:3566). It is cut after memory.compression_summary_idle_seconds with nothing received (settings_db.py:255; default 60 s, up to 600, no "off": idle_seconds, :71). Any chunk counts as life: a visible token, and a reasoning chunk that shows no text, through the new on_activity callback on the Ollama and LM Studio streams (agents/core/llm/base.py:625, :874). A slow stream that keeps talking is never cut. A cut stream is cancelled and given CLOSE_GRACE (1 s) to close its HTTP response. A backend with no stream is awaited whole. A degraded reply ("⚠️ …", "[backend error …]") or an empty one is now a failure, and so the digest is used. Before, the non-streaming generate could hand an error text over as the summary. Tests: tests/test_h674_compaction_hold.py (52) covers both settings, the idle deadline (silent, slow-but-talking, token-only, thinking, degraded, no stream), the hold (in time, at the bound, single flight, zero, cancelled wait, late failure, failure within the hold, aclose), the compressor's deferral (digest, verbatim when it fits, owner's budget, covered with a prior), and the orchestrator: the turn going on at the hold, the late summary seeding the next turn, a newer prior never overwritten, no clock commit for the deferred summary, the idle setting reaching the summarizer, aclose. It also covers the notice on /chat and every stream end event, the collector unbound after /chat, and on_activity on both local streams. frontend src/test/turn-notices.test.ts covers the HUD. 72 mutants: 70 caught after nine survivors got cases. Two were equivalent. m23 (busy ignoring done()) is equivalent because the done callback always pops the flight first. The other was a redundant typeof check in the HUD helper, which was removed. The phase-2, H20.3 and compaction-policy suites pass unchanged. The AUD-7 and H677 end-event and reply pins gain the notices key.
Joburile au refuz/raportare explicită și livrare prin aprobări existente.
reviews.remaining: Politica configurabilă queue/deny pentru toate originile fără operator nu este echivalată prin simpla livrare a joburilor.

reviews.summary: Boot now waits for the local model before it accepts work, and every shutdown wait has a short explicit budget. (1) Warm-up gate. load_agents still starts LLMRouter.warm_up as a background task (agents/core/orchestrator.py:928). The web lifespan now waits for it before orch.start_channels(): gate_warmup (agents/core/lifecycle_budget.py:102, called at agents/web.py:627). The wait is bounded by system.startup_warmup_timeout_seconds (settings_db.py:369; default 20 s, 0 = do not wait, clamped to 0..300 by warmup_timeout, lifecycle_budget.py:37; a bad value keeps the default). The HTTP app is not served before the lifespan yields, so /chat waits too. On expiry the gate logs the setting's name, opens anyway, and the warm-up finishes in the background; the gate never cancels it. WARMUP (WarmupState, :51, :99) holds off / warming / ready / cold (warm_up answered False: nothing local to warm) / failed (raised or cancelled), the gate_expired flag, and the seconds it took (frozen when it ends). GET /api/status (routers/status.py:120) and /readyz (routers/ops.py:143) report it; it is never a reason to be not-ready. A turn served while it is still warming is marked: ChatResponse.warming (web.py:1098, :1250), every end event of the stream, the failed turn's included (:1356, :1362), and a log line for channel turns (orchestrator.py:1597). (2) Shutdown budgets. bounded (lifecycle_budget.py:128) runs one step for at most its budget, logs an overrun or an error by name and moves on; a step that ignores cancellation is abandoned, never awaited. wait_task (:147) cancels a background task and waits at most its budget. ChannelManager.stop_all bounds each channel's stop at 3 s (channels/manager.py:126). _cancel_task bounds each cancelled task at 2 s (orchestrator.py:1396). stop_channels bounds the Oracle watcher and plugin close_all (:1416, :1419). aclose bounds the checkpoint flush, each context-cache task, the warm-up task, the LLM router, the Ollama client, MCP, the context cache, the plugin HTTP clients and each channel's aclose (:4470-4519). So one wedged step costs its budget, not the service manager's stop budget. The budgets are per step; there is no total deadline, so several wedged steps still add up. (3) Per-chat lanes. ChatLanes (agents/core/channels/chat_lanes.py:24) runs a chat's turns in order and different chats side by side, at most 8 turns at once. A failed turn never stalls its lane. drain (:66) gives the lanes a bounded time at stop, cancels what is left and names how many it abandoned. Telegram's poll loop creates the lanes (channels/telegram.py:420) and hands each batched turn (_deliver_turn, :543), each button tap (:454) and each observed group line (:500) to its chat's lane through _in_chat (:548). Work with no chat waits for every lane first (settle), so H117's order holds: what a chat said before a tap is handled first. The loop goes straight back to reading, so one slow answer, or a 180 s lease wait, no longer holds other chats. stop() and the loop's exit drain the lanes within 2 s (LANE_DRAIN_BUDGET, :53). The voice-reply mark (H071 "voice for voice") is taken when a note is read, while the chat's previous turn may still be running; the note's turn now carries it into its lane (_voice_pending, :236, :712; _deliver_turn; _run_turn, :561) and sets it only when it runs, so the earlier, typed, reply is never the one spoken. Tests: tests/test_h677_boot_and_shutdown.py (51) covers the setting, every gate phase, the lifespan order, status/readyz, the /chat and stream marks, the channel-turn log, bounded and wait_task, a hung channel stop, a stubborn task, a hung aclose step, a source pin that no teardown await is bare, lane order, concurrency, failures, bound, drain and settle, Telegram reading the next update while a chat is answered, and a voice note read while its chat is busy keeping its own spoken reply. The H117 batching and Telegram suites pass unchanged. 84 mutants, all caught after cases were added (a cancelled or None-returning warm-up, the frozen duration, a zero budget, cold vs failed, an abandoned step's cancel and late error, lane order after an earlier turn ends, drain cancelling, the poll loop's own lanes, a tap in another chat, cache-task cleanup, the warm-up cancelled at close, the budgets nesting); one was equivalent (asyncio.shield around asyncio.wait, which never cancels) and the shield was removed. Building the lanes exposed a regression they would have introduced (the voice mark taken by the busy chat's earlier reply), fixed red-first.
Dialectele de unelte cloud, compactarea în tură și recuperarea răspunsului gol au implementări și regresii.

reviews.summary: Cached per-model tri-state hooks now preserve undeclared defaults, suppress all reasoning controls for explicit empty declarations, and canonically clamp nonempty vocabularies to the nearest weaker level. Below-minimum requests refuse before HTTP rather than escalating or restoring defaults. Immutable backend-owned Gemini/compatible declarations retain cold/reconnect/concurrent isolation; actual Anthropic text/stream/tool requests enforce empty declarations, including registry precedence and default-on families. Budget-only models expose existing product rungs while emitting only their budget schema, never an invented effort field. Independent 162-case guarded review and original mocked-wire counterexamples pass. Operator declarations must match actual provider capabilities; no live acceptance/billing or catalog-discovery proof is claimed. New Nebius/local wire support is not required by this frozen contract.

SubAgentManager (agents/core/subagents.py) provides capped, isolated, steerable spawns, and a schema-invalid child is recorded as failed (agents/core/subagents.py:408-414). The production runner _subagent_runner (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1523-1526) calls orch.process(task, agent=picked, channel='subagent') with no model, provider or request override. SubAgentManager.spawn accepts only task, agent, parent and output_schema, and SubAgentSpawnBody (agents/core/routers/mesh.py:191-195) accepts no model fields. A reusable model/provider pin exists for owner jobs (selection_scope, agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:54, used at agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1585) but is not wired to delegation. Provider failure is not reported honestly. Orchestrator.process returns '' on any backend failure or error/timeout marker (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1754-1761). The runner wraps that as {'output': ''}, and the manager records the child as done with ok=True; a scratch probe returned status 'done'. There is no batch spawn surface, and nothing collapses a batch of identical failures into one 'configured subagent model rejected' notice.
reviews.remaining: (1) Per-child API settings: accept model/provider, plus bounded request overrides such as max_tokens/temperature/extra_body deep-merged one level, on SubAgentManager.spawn, on the /api/subagents/spawn body and through a default autonomy.subagent_model setting. Apply them in _subagent_runner through selection_scope with documented precedence: explicit, then setting, then parent. (2) Failure honesty: a child whose provider call failed (empty output, degraded reply or error marker) is recorded as failed with the error class, not done. (3) Batch report: a batch spawn surface whose result emits one notice when every child failed with a model-not-found phrase AND the configured subagent model name. The notice names the model, the setting that controls it and whether a fallback exists. A failure naming a model that is not the configured one must not trigger it. (4) Tests for all three.
