reviews.summary: Re-read on main at 55d625f4. Telegram has the partial-then-edit mechanism: TelegramDraft (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:57) sends the first token as a message, then edits it in place through _edit_message (telegram.py:365) at most once per STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL (telegram.py:51, 1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; finish() (telegram.py:130) settles the final text in the streamed message, sends overflow as new messages, retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text and falls back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. The adapter declares supports_edit=True (telegram.py:173) and exposes begin_stream (telegram.py:381). The real caller is Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1603), invoked for every non-observed channel turn (orchestrator.py:1479): it opens a draft only when the adapter has begin_stream, its descriptor says supports_edit, the owner setting channels.streaming_replies is on (orchestrator.py:1611) and the delivery router would send to this source; the turn then runs through handle_input_stream with on_token=draft.push (orchestrator.py:1600) and draft.finish (orchestrator.py:1524) replaces the whole-reply send. The conservative default is declarative rather than a stub: ChannelDescriptor.supports_edit defaults to False (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:36), so an adapter that declares nothing gets the whole reply. Slack and Discord are deliberately excluded from streaming (orchestrator.py:1608) because their replies go through the governed channel.reply approval queue (_queue_workspace_reply, orchestrator.py:1533-1534); test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens pins that an editable transport alone cannot publish tokens before that approval. Tests: 82 passed, 1 skipped (tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py needs slack_sdk, absent on this box) across tests/test_telegram_streaming.py, tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py and tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py. #1188's change to telegram.py (the process's shared SenderPairing handed in at construction, deeplink pairing refused when none is wired) does not touch the draft, edit or send paths.
reviews.remaining: (1) No edit or delete in the base contract: ChannelAdapter (agents/core/channels/base.py:14) still declares only abstract start/stop/send plus receive, and no adapter implements a delete operation (no delete_message or deleteMessage anywhere in agents/), so a sealed streamed preview cannot be removed and there is no base method that fails loudly for a channel that cannot edit; the fallback to a whole reply is silent. (2) Slack and Discord do not stream: both descriptors declare supports_edit=True (agents/core/channels/slack.py:102, agents/core/channels/discord.py:32) but neither adapter implements begin_stream or an edit call (Slack's send posts via chat_postMessage only, slack.py:333), and _begin_channel_draft refuses both because a streamed draft would publish tokens before the channel.reply approval; streaming there needs an approval contract that covers output not yet generated. (3) No acknowledgement at ingest: Telegram sends a typing chat action only while reading an inbound attachment (telegram.py:699) and a record_voice action before a spoken reply, so an ordinary text message gets no receipt signal until the first streamed token or the whole reply; Slack and Discord send none (the Slack Socket Mode envelope ack is a transport ack to Slack, not a signal the sender sees).

reviews.summary: Read-only jobs doctor reports scheduler stop/pause, missing registrations, missing/invalid/overdue next runs, execution failures and delivery failures. CLI failures exit non-zero. Bounded native scheduler outcomes and owner delivery results survive restart; intentional skips do not erase failures. Real APScheduler and migration tests pass; the two diagnostic modules have 97% branch-inclusive coverage. Doctor also checks script paths and no_agent configuration without reading source; persisted jobs remain inspectable when a script disappears. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported.
reviews.remaining: Model workdir and wider per-job tool context remain unsupported. Production-host observation, complete runtime-availability diagnostics and the wider job-option contract remain open; this is not full Hermes cron-doctor equivalence.

reviews.summary: The per-turn data exists on the server. TokenUsage carries provider cache_read/cache_write (agents/core/llm/tool_protocol.py:70-72). The stream path sums provider usage per agent (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2368). The post-turn record writes input, output and cached tokens, a per-turn cache_hit boolean and usage_source into the learning ledger (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4251-4254). Aggregate readouts exist: /api/metrics/north-star (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:166) with %-local and p95 turn latency, shown as a HUD stat card (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:214), and the bench computes a chars/sec throughput (agents/core/bench.py:79). None of it reaches the chat surface live. The /chat/stream end event carries only agent, text, pending_approvals, H677's warming flag and H674's notices (agents/web.py:1356), and ChatResponse (agents/web.py:1089) has reply, pending_approvals, warming and notices only. No HUD component shows tokens/sec, latency, context % or cache hit for the current turn. There is no field-selection setting. Cache hit is not computed as a delta since the last invalidating event: the stored cache_hit is a per-turn boolean that does not reset on model switch or compaction. Nothing hides the readout when there are no cache reads.
reviews.remaining: (1) Compute a per-turn readout: wall latency; output tokens/sec over generation time; context % of the resolved model window; compressions count; and cache hit as a delta since the last cache-invalidating event (model switch or accepted compaction), omitted when there were zero cache reads. Attach it to the /chat/stream end event and the /chat response, leaving fields absent when there is no data. (2) Add a display.status_bar_fields setting with a fixed field vocabulary shared by backend and HUD. (3) Add a HUD status strip on the chat surface that renders only the selected fields, hides omitted ones and colours cache hit at the 70/40 thresholds. (4) Backend and frontend tests.

reviews.summary: Nerva has a durable install identity, one hub per data root and isolated profiles, as Hermes does. agents/core/install_identity.py keeps one 32-hex id in <data root>/install_id (install_id). It is minted once under an in-process threading lock and a cross-process file lock (fcntl.flock, or msvcrt.locking on Windows, on install_id.lock). It is written atomically: mkstemp, fsync, os.replace, then a directory fsync. It is read back before it is cached and returned. A file holding anything but an id, one that cannot be read, or a write that fails answers None, never a fresh value, and the file is left as it is. The consumers use it. agents/core/first_action.py stores it as the activation clock's install_id; mark_installed no longer re-mints over an unreadable or foreign record, and infer_install_at_boot and record_first_action never write over one. agents/core/node_mesh.py issues node grants as node:<id>@<install> and keeps hub_id on the record. agents/core/channels/pairing.py stamps each deeplink with hub, and redeem_deeplink refuses another install's (other_install). agents/core/satellite_hub.py gives SatellitePairing a validated hub_id, and SatelliteHub refuses a pairing pinned to another install (other_install, read lazily through _own_hub_id). serve.py stops on a bad JARVIS_PROFILE (paths.profile_error). It holds <data root>/hub.lock for the life of the process (acquire_hub_lock), so a second hub on the same root stops with HubAlreadyRunning naming the holder's pid, and it prints the data root and install id. agents/core/paths.py gives JARVIS_PROFILE a meaning. A valid name (profile_name: lowercase letters, digits, - or _, up to 32; "default" is the default root) makes data_root <root>/profiles/<name>. Settings, memory, the install id and lock, and the credentials follow it; agents/core/secrets.py resolves DEFAULT_STORE under the root the process starts with. It is classified in env_provenance READ_BEFORE_LOAD and FROM_PROCESS_ONLY. Tests: tests/test_h689_install_identity.py (43), including racing processes that agree on one id and a real second-process lock refusal; tests/test_first_run_first_action.py pins the no-re-mint rule; 32 mutants, 30 killed, 2 fixed.

JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES is the only allowlist that decides whose forwarding headers count: X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-Proto alike.

Parsing and refusals: parse_trusted_proxies (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:134) reads each entry with ip_network(strict=False) (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:160), so a bare address becomes its own /32 or /128. It refuses '*', 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 by name (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107), any prefix length 0 (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:165), unreadable entries and more than 64 entries, naming the variable and the position, never the value. A malformed list refuses boot through assert_parseable_trusted_proxies (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:411), whose message tells the operator to list the proxy's own address or a bounded CIDR range with no wildcard; it runs in enforce_boot_posture (agents/core/boot_guards.py:350), which the lifespan calls after the .env files load (agents/web.py:456-463, H273), and assert_front_door runs it over a caller's own mapping (agents/core/boot_guards.py:318). That is stricter than Hermes, which drops a bad entry and carries on. At request time a malformed list fails closed and is said once (agents/web.py:166). The default trusts nothing, not even loopback; the legacy JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXY flag means loopback only (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:206).

One trust set: uvicorn's own proxy-header layer used to rewrite the client address and scheme from loopback, or from whatever FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS named, before the app looked. serve.server_config now builds uvicorn with proxy_headers=False (serve.py:99) and records that choice (serve.py:101). docker-compose.yml passes --no-proxy-headers (docker-compose.yml:13); the Dockerfile, the systemd unit, start.sh, START.bat and the packaged build already start through serve.py. The app reads X-Forwarded-Proto itself, only from a listed peer and only when there is exactly one http/https/ws/wss value (forwarded_proto, agents/core/proxy_trust.py:389, applied by _ForwardedProtoMiddleware, agents/web.py:200, registered at agents/web.py:678), so a TLS proxy still yields https:// base URLs for the MCP resource and the widget snippet. The scheme is set on the scope in place, as uvicorn's layer did, so the route the router records reaches the golden-signals middleware and a forwarded request keeps its per-route metrics label (agents/web.py:231, tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:582). assert_server_proxy_layer_within_trust (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570) runs in the same boot pass (agents/core/boot_guards.py:353) and in assert_front_door (agents/core/boot_guards.py:319). It refuses FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, or --forwarded-allow-ips on a uvicorn command line when an entry is '*', a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES plus uvicorn's loopback default.

Gates: the localhost auth bypass (_real_client_host, agents/web.py:176) and the HF-2 rate-limit key (_client_ip, agents/web.py:359) resolve the client through forwarded_client, which trusts only a listed peer and walks the chain right to left. The HF-2 localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:778), so an unlisted same-box proxy, or a listed one whose chain vouches for nothing, is not waved through.

Logging: web.py's import-time read is silent (agents/web.py:158). The lifespan calls announce_trusted_proxies after setup_logging and the .env load (agents/web.py:519). When anything is trusted it logs one INFO line naming the source and the canonical networks (_log_trust_set, agents/core/proxy_trust.py:253), together with the wide-entry and legacy warnings that belong with it, which are repeated when the set was resolved before logging existed (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:294). Nothing is logged for the default. It also names uvicorn's layer whenever that layer believes anyone (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:528): on a raw uvicorn start without --no-proxy-headers, or under a launcher it cannot identify.

Tests: tests/test_trusted_proxies.py covers parsing and refusal (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:58, tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:74), the LAN-peer loopback spoof (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:183), the INFO line (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:295), the lifespan wiring run through the real lifespan (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:434), the silent import (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:416), and the served config with uvicorn's ProxyHeadersMiddleware in front, where a LAN peer sends X-Forwarded-For 127.0.0.1 under FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*' (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:506). It also covers the throttle exemption (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:534), X-Forwarded-Proto believed only from a listed peer (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:562), and the uvicorn-allowlist refusals (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:624). tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py pins the new guard in the boot pass and in the mapping check (tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py:148, tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py:200), and that the lifespan loads the .env files before the boot pass (tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py:218). tests/test_rate_limit_hf2.py and tests/test_admin_guard_hf7.py cover the two gates. Operator documentation is in docs/FLAGS.md.

Known limits, which the row does not require: a raw python -m uvicorn agents.web:app without --no-proxy-headers (the CI openapi, soak and smoke jobs, and dev use) still lets uvicorn believe loopback's forwarding headers, which is Hermes's own default. On that raw start uvicorn's loopback walk can also rewrite a loopback peer into a listed proxy's address, after which Nerva's walk trusts the rest of the chain; using it needs the raw start, a list naming a non-loopback proxy and a same-box unlisted proxy that passes the client's X-Forwarded-For through verbatim. The guard caps that layer at the Nerva list plus loopback, and the boot names it at INFO. A launcher that embeds uvicorn some other way passes its allowlist out of the app's sight. The RFC 7239 Forwarded header is not parsed. Behaviour change: a same-box proxy that is not listed no longer gets per-client throttle keys or https:// base URLs through uvicorn's implicit loopback trust until it is listed (127.0.0.1/32).

Nerva already has the shape of a small bundle plus a large on-demand catalog. 12 first-party skills ship under skills/ (for example skills/brief/SKILL.md). They are rendered into the 'Available skills' prompt block (agents/core/agent.py:849), which skills_index_component measures (agents/core/prompt_size.py:149). Hermes skills are not bundled; they are imported one at a time on request. POST /skills/import (agents/core/routers/skills.py:440) is user-guarded and DEV_MODE-gated, and frontend/src/panels/skills-import.tsx drives it. It calls SkillImporter.import_from_hermes (agents/core/skills/importer.py:206). That import checks an exact, digest-verified pin allowlist and fails before any network call (tests/test_hermes_import.py). The pin still predates the upstream reorganisation. agents/core/skills/hermes_pin_v1.json:4 and agents/core/skills/importer.py:50 are v2026.8.27 with 78 entries (tests/test_hermes_import.py:232). So the catalog still lists github-auth, github-code-review, github-issue-to-pr, github-issues, github-pr-workflow, github-repo-management, plan, session-librarian and blogwatcher. It has neither the consolidated github skill nor grill-me or the other new optional skills. _safe_pin_path requires every pinned path to start with skills/ (agents/core/skills/importer.py:113), so upstream's optional-skills/ tree cannot be pinned at all. Each pin entry digests only one SKILL.md, so reference files cannot be imported.
reviews.remaining:
1. Re-pin to upstream's current release (v2026.8.31 or later). Read the bytes, record sha256, execute nothing, and keep the fail-before-network posture.
2. Pin format. The pin must accept the optional-skills/ root, which agents/core/skills/importer.py:113 currently rejects. Each entry must digest-verify and import the skill's reference files as well as SKILL.md, because the consolidated github skill and the pdf and AgentMail skills keep their per-workflow detail in references.
3. Catalog content. The re-pinned catalog must expose the consolidated github skill and grill-me, and drop the merged/deleted skills.
4. Move importer constants, tests and the doc-consistency check to the new tag.
